/**

 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: staff.js recipients and edition (3d Task 4)", () => {

    const lines: string[] = [];
    const code = await runStaffCommand(args, env(), { log: (line) => lines.push(`out ${line}`), error: (line) => lines.push(`err ${line}`) });
    return { code, lines };
  };
  const YEAR = 2006;
  const today = () => new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  const cleanUp = async () => {
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.transparency_editions where year between 2005 and 2007`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.recipient_months where month between '2006-01-01'::date and '2007-12-01'::date`);
  };

  beforeAll(async () => {
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 1 });
    await cleanUp();
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await cleanUp();
    await closeDb(migrateDb);
  });

  const insertMonth = (month: string, signedIn: number, signedOutDays: number | null) =>
    migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into public.recipient_months (month, signed_in, signed_out_days, method) values (${`${month}-01`}::date, ${signedIn}, ${signedOutDays}, 1)`);

  test("recipients prints each of the six full months before the day, a month not recorded as such, and the average as two bounds", async () => {
    // Asked on 10 March 2007: the six full months are September 2006 to February 2007; October was not recorded.
    for (const [month, signedIn, out] of [["2006-09", 100, 300], ["2006-11", 110, 310], ["2006-12", 120, 320], ["2007-01", 130, 330], ["2007-02", 140, 340]] as const) await insertMonth(month, signedIn, out);
    const at = new Date("2007-03-10T12:00:00.000Z");
    const done = await figureCommand(migrateDb, { command: "recipients", months: 6 }, at);
    expect(done).toEqual({
      ok: true,
      lines: [
        "recipients: method 1; the 6 full months to 2007-02.",
        "recipients: 2006-09: signed in 100; signed out, summed by day, 300",
        "recipients: 2006-10: not recorded",
        "recipients: 2006-11: signed in 110; signed out, summed by day, 310",
        "recipients: 2006-12: signed in 120; signed out, summed by day, 320",
        "recipients: 2007-01: signed in 130; signed out, summed by day, 330",
        "recipients: 2007-02: signed in 140; signed out, summed by day, 340",
        "recipients: only 5 full months are recorded.",
        "recipients: average monthly active recipients: between 120 and 440.",
      ],
    });
    // A month that did not count signed-out readers: "at least", and no second bound.
    await insertMonth("2006-10", 100, null);
    expect(await figureCommand(migrateDb, { command: "recipients", months: 6 }, at)).toMatchObject({
      ok: true,
      lines: expect.arrayContaining(["recipients: 2006-10: signed in 100; signed out, summed by day, not counted", "recipients: average monthly active recipients: at least 117; signed-out readers are not counted."]),
    });
    expect(describeRecipients([], 2, at)).toEqual([
      "recipients: method 1; the 2 full months to 2007-02.",
      "recipients: 2007-01: not recorded",
      "recipients: 2007-02: not recorded",
      "recipients: only 0 full months are recorded.",
      "recipients: average monthly active recipients: not recorded.",
    ]);
  });

  test("recipients and edition run as commands: their words, the usage on a wrong word, and nothing written", async () => {
    const audits = async () => (await migrateDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.audit_log`))[0]!.n;
    const before = await audits();
    const asked = await run(["recipients", "--months", "3"]);
    expect(asked.code).toBe(0);
    expect(asked.lines[0]).toMatch(/^out recipients: method 1; the 3 full months to [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}[.]$/);
    expect(await run(["edition", String(YEAR - 1)])).toEqual({ code: 0, lines: [`out edition: none stored for ${YEAR - 1}.`] });
    expect(await audits()).toBe(before);
    for (const args of [["recipients", "--months", "0"], ["recipients", "6"], ["edition"], ["edition", "06"], ["edition", "2006", "--fix"]]) expect((await run(args)).code).toBe(2);
  });

  test("edition prints the newest stored version a line a figure; --correct stores the next version, the migrator's alone, and is refused for a year not due and for one with no edition", async () => {
    for (const [month, signedIn, out] of [["2006-09", 100, 300], ["2006-10", 100, 300], ["2006-11", 100, 300], ["2006-12", 100, 300], ["2007-01", 100, 300], ["2007-02", 100, 300]] as const) {
      await migrateDb.execute(sql`delete from public.recipient_months where month = ${`${month}-01`}::date`);
      await insertMonth(month, signedIn, out);
    }
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`select public.edition_publish(${YEAR}::int, 'first')`);
    const printed = await run(["edition", String(YEAR)]);
    expect(printed).toEqual({
      code: 0,
      lines: [
        `out edition: ${YEAR}, version 1 of ${today()}, first.`,
        "out edition: restrictions by ground: none",
        "out edition: restrictions, all: 0",
        "out edition: restrictions by kind of measure: none",
        "out edition: decisions that found no breach: 0",

        "out edition: findings by a program: none",
        "out edition: measures a program took: none",
        "out edition: recipients: between about 100 and about 400",
      ],
    });
    const corrected = await run(["edition", String(YEAR), "--correct"]);
    expect(corrected).toEqual({ code: 0, lines: [`out edition: ${YEAR}, version 2 stored, every table computed again. The page lists version 1 as replaced on ${today()}.`] });
    const [audit] = await migrateDb.execute<{ action: string; target_id: string; metadata: Record<string, unknown> }>(
      sql`select action, target_id, metadata from public.audit_log where chain_seq = (select seq from public.audit_head where id = 1)`,
    );
    expect({ ...audit }).toEqual({ action: "edition_published", target_id: `${YEAR}.2`, metadata: { year: YEAR, version: 2, reason: "correction" } });
    expect((await run(["edition", String(YEAR)])).lines[0]).toBe(`out edition: ${YEAR}, version 2 of ${today()}, correction.`);

    const running = new Date().getUTCFullYear();
    expect(await run(["edition", String(running), "--correct"])).toEqual({ code: 1, lines: [`err edition: edition_not_due: the edition of ${running} is due on ${running + 1}-03-01; nothing changed`] });
    expect(await run(["edition", String(YEAR + 1), "--correct"])).toEqual({
      code: 1,
      lines: [`err edition: invalid_edition: no edition of ${YEAR + 1} is stored yet; the job publishes its first version on or after ${YEAR + 2}-03-01; nothing changed`],
    });
  });

  test("an edition's every table, its programs' rate and its order section print as the page prints them, a null figure as not recorded", () => {
    const figures: TransparencyFigures = {
      restrictions: { byGround: [{ label: "R1", count: "about 60" }, { label: "law", count: "about 10" }, { label: "other", count: "about 10" }], byMeasure: [{ label: "remove", count: "about 80" }], total: "about 80" },

      orders: {

        annex3: Object.fromEntries(ANNEX3_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, 0])) as never,
        scrutiny: { requested: 1, annulled: 0, upheld: 1 },
        reinstated: Object.fromEntries(ORDER_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, 0])) as never,
        authorityAccess: null,
        terroristWithoutOrder: 1,

      },
      recipients: { low: "about 120" },

    expect(describeEdition(2025, { version: 2, published_on: "2026-05-02", reason: "hold_ended", figures })).toEqual([
      "edition: 2025, version 2 of 2026-05-02, hold ended.",

### Create `apps/api/test/integration/transparency-figures.test.ts`

```ts
import { performance } from "node:perf_hooks";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { EDITION_REASONS, TRANSPARENCY_RULES, TransparencyFigures, band, type OrderView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../../src/auth";
import { tcoCounts, type TcoCounts } from "../../src/cli/counts";
import { aPost, act, decideIn, imagePost, newTestStaff, refusal, removeFixtures, report, staffProfile, type TestStaff } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { noticesWorld, type NoticesWorld } from "./notices-harness";
import { closeNotifyFixtures } from "./notify-fixtures";
import { rolledBack } from "./staff-fixtures";
import { yearForTest, type YearCells } from "./transparency-fixtures";

vi.setConfig({ testTimeout: 180_000 });

/**
 * The public figures on the database (3d design, sections 2 rows 1 to 5 and 8, 6.4 and 7.6; Task 4; invariants 1 and 21;
 * LAB E repeated on the built code, 12.3). transparency_figures() and edition_publish() over yearForTest's years, which
 * lie twelve and more years back, where nothing else in the test database stands: every row is written as the migrator
 * inside a transaction that is rolled back, and the figures are read inside it. This file runs on a database that has no
 * migration after the transparency one, which is how 12.1 row 1 asks that edition_publish be called before the label
 * automated exists.
 */
describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("integration: the public figures and the yearly edition (3d Task 4)", () => {
  let w: NoticesWorld;
  let moderator: TestStaff;
  let admin: TestStaff;
  const NOW = new Date().getUTCFullYear();
  const YEAR = NOW - 12;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    w = noticesWorld();
    moderator = await newTestStaff(w.authDb, w.migrateDb, w.repo, "moderator");
    admin = await newTestStaff(w.authDb, w.migrateDb, w.repo, "admin");
    await staffProfile(w.apiDb, moderator);
    await staffProfile(w.apiDb, admin);
  }, 60_000);
  afterAll(async () => {
    await removeFixtures(w.migrateDb, [moderator.id, admin.id]);
    await closeNotifyFixtures();
    await w.close();
  });

  type Figures = TransparencyFigures & Record<string, unknown>;
  /** The figures of a year at an instant, as the migrator (the one role that may compute them). */
  const figuresOf = async (tx: DbTx, year: number, asOf: Date = new Date()): Promise<Figures> => {
    const [row] = await tx.execute<{ f: Figures }>(sql`select public.transparency_figures(${year}::int, ${asOf.toISOString()}::timestamptz) as f`);
    return row!.f;
  };
  /** edition_publish() as the caller's role, in a savepoint: the version it wrote, null, or the code it was refused with. */
  const publish = async (tx: DbTx, year: number, reason: string): Promise<number | null | string> => {
    let version: number | null = null;
    const refused = await refusal(
      tx.transaction(async (sp) => {
        const [row] = await sp.execute<{ v: number | null }>(sql`select public.edition_publish(${year}::int, ${reason}) as v`);
        version = row!.v;
      }),
    );
    return refused ?? version;
  };
  const editions = (tx: DbTx, year: number) =>
    tx.execute<{ version: number; reason: string; method: number; figures: Figures; computed_at: string; published_at: string }>(
      sql`select version, reason, method, figures, computed_at::text, published_at::text from public.transparency_editions where year = ${year} order by version`,
    );
  /** The newest audit row: its action, actor, target, metadata and whether a key confirmed it. */
  const newestAudit = async (tx: DbTx) => {
    const [row] = await tx.execute<{ action: string; actor_id: string; target_type: string | null; target_id: string | null; metadata: Record<string, unknown>; key_id: string | null; step_up: unknown }>(
      sql`select action, actor_id, target_type, target_id, metadata, key_id, step_up from public.audit_log where chain_seq = (select seq from public.audit_head where id = 1)`,
    );
    return row!;
  };
  /** The number a band names: 0, 5 for "1 to 9", or the rounded count. */
  const named = (count: string) => (count === "0" ? 0 : count === "1 to 9" ? 5 : Number(count.replace("about ", "")));
  /** Every string of a stored edition outside the order section, with its path. */
  const stringsOf = (value: unknown, path = ""): { path: string; text: string }[] => {
    if (typeof value === "string") return [{ path, text: value }];
    if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.flatMap((entry, at) => stringsOf(entry, `${path}[${at}]`));
    if (value !== null && typeof value === "object") {
      return Object.entries(value).flatMap(([key, entry]) => (path === "" && key === "orders" ? [] : stringsOf(entry, path === "" ? key : `${path}.${key}`)));
    }
    return [];
  };
  const LABELS = new Set(["label"]);

  /** LAB E's seven cells of 2025, in the year of this test: 216 restrictions, 143 decisions without a breach. */
  const LAB_E: YearCells = { restrictions: { R1: 61, R3: 94, R4: 35, R5: 12, R6: 7, R2: 3, law: 4 }, noBreach: 143 };

  test("LAB E1, E2 and E4 on the built code: seven cells print as five rows and a total, the cells under ten fold into other, and the rows do not give the total", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      await yearForTest(tx, YEAR, LAB_E, moderator);
      const f = await figuresOf(tx, YEAR);
      expect(f.restrictions.byGround).toEqual([
        { label: "R1", count: "about 60" },
        { label: "R3", count: "about 90" },
        { label: "R4", count: "about 40" },
        { label: "R5", count: "about 10" },
        // R2's 3, R6's 7 and the law's 4: 14, printed with its own band.
        { label: "other", count: "about 10" },
      ]);
      expect(f.restrictions.total).toBe("about 220");
      expect(f.restrictions.byMeasure).toEqual([{ label: "remove", count: "about 220" }]);
      expect(f.noBreach).toBe("about 140");
      // E4: the printed rows give 210, the printed total 220: a folded cell cannot be subtracted back.
      expect(f.restrictions.byGround.reduce((sum, row) => sum + named(row.count), 0)).toBe(210);
      expect(named(f.restrictions.total)).toBe(220);
      // The other tables of a year with none of their rows are empty, and the recipients not recorded.
      expect([f.intakes, f.appeals, f.reexaminations, f.accountMeasures, f.automated, f.recipients, f.orders]).toEqual([[], [], [], [], { findings: [], measures: [] }, "not recorded", undefined]);
      expect(TransparencyFigures.parse(f)).toEqual(f);
    });
  });

  test("LAB E3: edition_not_due before 1 March of the next year in UTC and for the running year, whatever instant is passed; nothing is written", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      await yearForTest(tx, YEAR, { restrictions: { R1: 12 } }, moderator);
      const lastMoment = new Date(Date.UTC(YEAR + 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay) - 1);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => figuresOf(sp, YEAR, lastMoment)))).toBe("edition_not_due");
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR, new Date(lastMoment.getTime() + 1))).restrictions.total).toBe("about 10");
      // The running year, also with an instant after its due day: the clock refuses it.
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => figuresOf(sp, NOW, new Date(Date.UTC(NOW + 1, 3, 1)))))).toBe("edition_not_due");
      expect(await publish(tx, NOW, "first")).toBeNull();
      expect(await editions(tx, NOW)).toEqual([]);
      // The migrator's correction of the running year is refused the same way; of a year that is due but has no edition
      // yet, as there is nothing to correct: the first version is the job's.
      expect(await publish(tx, NOW, "correction")).toBe("edition_not_due");
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "correction")).toBe("invalid_edition");
    });
  });

  test("LAB E5 and the order section: of two orders, one under a hold, the edition counts one; tco-counts still prints both, for the authority", async () => {
    const future = new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 86_400_000);
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const made = await yearForTest(tx, YEAR, { orders: [{ posts: 1, receivedBefore: 10 }, { posts: 1, receivedBefore: 20, heldUntil: future }] }, moderator);
      expect(made.orders).toHaveLength(2);
      const f = await figuresOf(tx, YEAR);
      expect(f.orders?.received).toEqual({ total: 1, crossBorder: 0 });
      expect(f.orders?.itemsDisabled).toBe(1);
      expect(f.orders?.minutes).toEqual({ list: [10], outside: 0, withoutReceipt: 0, open: 0 });
      const counts = await tcoCounts(tx, YEAR);
      expect(counts.received?.total).toBe(2);
      // An order decision is in no other table: the two disablings restrict nothing of korbat's own.
      expect([f.restrictions.total, f.restrictions.byMeasure, f.noBreach]).toEqual(["0", [], "0"]);
    });
    // Only the held order: no section, and nothing says one was left out.
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const made = await yearForTest(tx, YEAR, { orders: [{ posts: 1, receivedBefore: 5, heldUntil: future }] }, moderator);
      expect(made.orders).toHaveLength(1);
      const held = await figuresOf(tx, YEAR);
      expect(Object.keys(held)).not.toContain("orders");
      expect(JSON.stringify(held)).not.toMatch(/order|held|hold/i);
      expect((await tcoCounts(tx, YEAR)).received?.total).toBe(1);
    });
  });

  test("the order section is tco-counts' figures as numbers, without the issuing state, on the same rows", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {

      const { orders } = await yearForTest(

      await decideIn(tx, admin, a.items[0]!.caseId!, { kind: "correction", reviewsDecisionId: a.items[0]!.decisionId!, outcome: "reversed", actions: [{ kind: "reinstate_by_order", orderGround: "annulled" }] });
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_order_events set at = ${inYear}, effective_at = ${inYear} where order_id = ${a.id}::uuid and kind = 'reinstated'`);
      for (const [order, kind, ground] of [[b, "scrutiny_requested", null], [b, "scrutiny_decided", "upheld"], [c, "annex3_sent", "insufficient_information"]] as const) {

      await tx.execute(sql`update public.decisions set decided_at = ${inYear}, informed_at = ${inYear} where id = ${terrorist}::uuid`);

      const f = await figuresOf(tx, YEAR);

      expect(f.orders).toMatchObject({ received: { total: 3, crossBorder: 1 }, itemsDisabled: 4, authorityAccess: 1, terroristWithoutOrder: 1, referralsClosed: 0 });
      expect(f.orders?.minutes).toEqual({ list: [10, 125], outside: 1, withoutReceipt: 0, open: 1 });

  test("edition_publish: version 1 with the system's audit row; a held order absent, then a version hold_ended that changes the order section alone; only a correction counts the tables again; nothing updates a version", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const { orders, spareIds } = await yearForTest(
        tx,
        YEAR,
        { restrictions: { R1: 20, R3: 4 }, spare: 15, orders: [{ posts: 1, receivedBefore: 10 }, { posts: 1, receivedBefore: 20, heldUntil: new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 86_400_000) }] },
        moderator,
      );
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBe(1);
      const [first] = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect({ reason: first!.reason, method: first!.method, same: first!.computed_at === first!.published_at }).toEqual({ reason: "first", method: TRANSPARENCY_RULES.method, same: true });
      expect(first!.figures.orders?.received).toEqual({ total: 1, crossBorder: 0 });
      const audit = await newestAudit(tx);
      expect(audit).toEqual({
        action: "edition_published",
        actor_id: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID,
        target_type: "edition",
        target_id: `${YEAR}.1`,
        metadata: { year: YEAR, version: 1, reason: "first" },
        key_id: null,
        step_up: null,
      });
      // Asked again with nothing new: nothing.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBeNull();

      // In between, more decisions of the year come to light (the spare restrictions move into it), and the held
      // order's hold ends and its notice is told.
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.decisions set decided_at = make_timestamptz(${YEAR}::int, 7, 7, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC') where id = any(${`{${spareIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[])`);
      await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = clock_timestamp() where id = ${orders[1]!.id}::uuid`);
      const [told] = await tx.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select public.order_notices_release() as n`);
      expect(told!.n).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);

      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBe(2);
      const [, second] = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect(second!.reason).toBe("hold_ended");
      const { orders: firstOrders, ...firstTables } = first!.figures;
      const { orders: secondOrders, ...secondTables } = second!.figures;
      expect(secondTables).toEqual(firstTables);
      expect(firstOrders?.received?.total).toBe(1);
      expect(secondOrders?.received).toEqual({ total: 2, crossBorder: 0 });
      expect((await newestAudit(tx)).metadata).toEqual({ year: YEAR, version: 2, reason: "hold_ended" });
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBeNull();

      // A version is never changed, by any role, the migrator included.
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.transparency_editions set figures = '{}'::jsonb where year = ${YEAR} and version = 1`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.transparency_editions set reason = 'correction' where year = ${YEAR} and version = 2`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");

      // The migrator's correction counts every table again, as of the same due day: the spare restrictions now count.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "correction")).toBe(3);
      const [, , third] = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect(third!.reason).toBe("correction");
      expect(third!.figures.restrictions.total).toBe(band(39));
      expect(first!.figures.restrictions.total).toBe(band(24));
      expect(third!.figures.orders?.received).toEqual({ total: 2, crossBorder: 0 });
      // A reason the caller may not give.
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "hold_ended")).toBe("invalid_edition");
    });
  });

  test("the recipients of every version of a year are the six stored months before its due day, whatever the version's instant", async () => {
    await rolledBack(w.migrateDb, async (tx) => {
      const month = (y: number, m: number) => `${y}-${String(m).padStart(2, "0")}-01`;
      const insert = (y: number, m: number, signedIn: number, signedOutDays: number | null) =>
        tx.execute(sql`insert into public.recipient_months (month, signed_in, signed_out_days, method) values (${month(y, m)}::date, ${signedIn}, ${signedOutDays}, 1)`);
      // September to February: 100 to 150 accounts, 200 to 250 readers summed by day.
      const window: [number, number][] = [[YEAR, 9], [YEAR, 10], [YEAR, 11], [YEAR, 12], [YEAR + 1, 1], [YEAR + 1, 2]];
      for (const [at, [y, m]] of window.entries()) {
        if (at === 5) continue;
        await insert(y, m, 100 + at * 10, 200 + at * 10);
      }
      // Five months: not recorded.
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toBe("not recorded");
      await insert(YEAR + 1, 2, 150, 250);
      // Months after the due day count for nothing in this edition.
      for (let m = 3; m <= 12; m++) await insert(YEAR + 1, m, 9000, 9000);
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toEqual({ low: band(125), high: band(125 + 225) });
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "first")).toBe(1);
      expect(await publish(tx, YEAR, "correction")).toBe(2);
      const stored = await editions(tx, YEAR);
      expect(stored.map((row) => row.figures.recipients)).toEqual([
        { low: "about 130", high: "about 350" },
        { low: "about 130", high: "about 350" },
      ]);
      // A month that did not count signed-out readers: one bound, "at least".
      await tx.execute(sql`delete from public.recipient_months where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`);
      await insert(YEAR, 9, 100, null);
      expect((await figuresOf(tx, YEAR)).recipients).toEqual({ low: band(125) });
      // The API's role reads months and inserts one; it updates and deletes none, and computed_at is forced.
      const [row] = await tx.execute<{ fresh: boolean }>(sql`select computed_at = now() as fresh from public.recipient_months where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`);
      expect(row!.fresh).toBe(true);
      expect(await refusal(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update public.recipient_months set signed_in = 1 where month = ${month(YEAR, 9)}::date`)))).toBe("edition_frozen");
    });
  });

/** tco-counts' figures as the order section holds them: without the year and the issuing state. */
function withoutState(counts: TcoCounts): Record<string, unknown> {
  const { year: _year, received, ...rest } = counts;
  return { ...rest, received: received === null ? null : { total: received.total, crossBorder: received.crossBorder } };
}

### Create `apps/api/test/integration/transparency-fixtures.ts`

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { OrderView } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { hex64, imagePost, newRef, openCase, type TestStaff } from "./moderation-fixtures";
import { ageOrderForTest, effectParams, effectWith, orderForTest } from "./orders-fixtures";

/**
 * yearForTest (3d design, section 12; Task 4, grown in Task 6 for decisions without a decider and in Task 7 for refused
 * uploads): a past year of decisions, intakes, appeals, account measures and orders, written cell by cell as the migrator
 * inside the caller's transaction, which the caller rolls back. LAB E wrote its synthetic decisions with the triggers off
 * (`e-counts.sql`); so does this fixture, for the rows of the tables it fills by the hundred: the migrator owns them, and
 * `alter table ... disable trigger user` holds only until the transaction ends, so nothing it writes outlives the test.
 * It does that first, while the transaction has queued no trigger event on those tables, and switches the triggers on
 * again before the orders, which go through 3f's real flows (as cli-counts.test.ts writes its fixture year) and are then
 * moved back into the year by ageOrderForTest.
 *
 * Each row of a cell gets a time in the year (in UTC) spread over its months, as the lab spread them: the row's number
 * modulo 12 picks the month and modulo 28 the day, at noon. A row counted by its later fate (an appeal's answer) has
 * that fate in the year too.
 */

/** A rule's id, or the law: what a restriction cites. */
export type GroundLabel = "R1" | "R2" | "R3" | "R4" | "R5" | "R6" | "law";

/** One order of the year, given effect through 3f's real flows and moved back into the year. */
export interface OrderCell {
  /** How many posts the order names; it disables the first `effectOn` of them (all by default). */
  posts: number;
  effectOn?: number;
  memberState?: "DE" | "FR";
  /** The instant of its last disabling, in the year or after it; noon on 15 June of the year by default. */
  disabledAt?: Date;
  /** Its receipt this many minutes before its last disabling; none recorded when absent. */
  receivedBefore?: number;
  /**
   * A notice held under Section C: its order decisions stay untold, and its hold runs to this instant (written as the
   * hold's recorded end, the one way a past removal order's hold can still run; the test ends it the same way).
   */
  heldUntil?: Date;
}

/** The cells of a year. Every number is how many rows the cell holds. */
export interface YearCells {
  /** Final decisions that restrict, by what they cite, each with one ledger row of `measure` (remove by default). */
  restrictions?: Partial<Record<GroundLabel, number>>;
  measure?: "remove" | "withhold" | "remove_media" | "reset_bio";
  /** Interim decisions that restrict, each citing R4 with one withhold. */
  interim?: number;
  /** Final decisions that found no breach (no_violation). */
  noBreach?: number;
  /** Intakes by kind: a report under a rule, a notice of illegality, a moderator's finding. */
  intakes?: Partial<Record<"rules" | "illegal" | "finding", number>>;
  /** Appeals answered in the year, by their result; each appeals a decision of the year before, so no restriction of the year is added. */
  appeals?: Partial<Record<"kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed", number>>;
  /** 3e's account measures, each on a final decision of the year that restricts under R6 (which therefore counts as a restriction too). */
  accountMeasures?: Partial<Record<"strike" | "suspend" | "terminate" | "retire_handle" | "warn_reporting" | "restrict_reporting", number>>;
  orders?: OrderCell[];
  /** Restrictions under R3 dated in the year before, which a test may move into the year later: what a correction counts again. */
  spare?: number;
}

/** What the fixture made that a test reads again. */
export interface YearMade {
  caseId: string;
  orders: OrderView[];
  /** The decisions of `spare`. */
  spareIds: string[];
}

/** The tables the fixture fills with its triggers off. */
const BULK_TABLES = ["decisions", "decision_actions", "intakes", "appeals"] as const;

/** A row's time in the year: its number picks the month and the day, at noon UTC. */
const spread = (year: number) => sql`make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1 + (g::int % 12), 1 + (g::int % 28), 12, 0, 0, 'UTC')`;

export async function yearForTest(tx: DbTx, year: number, cells: YearCells, staff: TestStaff): Promise<YearMade> {
  // One post and its case, which every bulk decision names: the ledger needs a case, a snapshot and a decider.
  const { authorId, postId } = await imagePost(tx, 0);
  const caseId = await openCase(tx, "post", postId);
  const [snapshot] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
    insert into public.evidence_snapshots (case_id, target_type, target_id, author_handle, digest)
    values (${caseId}::uuid, 'post', ${postId}::uuid, 'author', ${hex64()}) returning id`);
  const spareIds: string[] = [];

  for (const table of BULK_TABLES) await tx.execute(sql.raw(`alter table public.${table} disable trigger user`));
  {
    /** Inserts `n` decisions with the columns given, each with one ledger row of `measure` when it restricts. */
    const decisions = async (n: number, d: { kind: "final" | "interim" | "review"; outcome: string; ground: "incompatible" | "illegal" | null; ruleId: string | null; at: ReturnType<typeof spread>; measure: string | null }) => {
      if (n <= 0) return [] as string[];
      const legal = d.ground === "illegal" ? hex64() : null;
      const restricted = d.outcome === "restricted";
      const rows = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
        insert into public.decisions (case_id, kind, seen_state_version, outcome, ground, rule_id, rules_version, redress_version, category, source,
                                      snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, facts_digest, reason_digest, legal_reference_digest, decided_by, decided_at, xact, puid,
                                      informed_at, suspect, needs_admin, ended_interim)
        select ${caseId}::uuid, ${d.kind}::public.decision_kind, 0, ${d.outcome}::public.decision_outcome, ${d.ground}::public.decision_ground, ${d.ruleId},
               3, 3, 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE', 'report', ${snapshot!.id}::uuid, ${hex64()}, ${restricted ? hex64() : null}, ${restricted ? hex64() : null}, ${legal},
               ${staff.id}::uuid, ${d.at}, '1'::xid8, md5(random()::text || g::text), ${d.at}, false, false, false
          from generate_series(1, ${n}::int) g
        returning id`);
      const ids = rows.map((row) => row.id);
      if (d.measure !== null) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into public.decision_actions (decision_id, kind, subject_account_id, post_id, created_at)
          select d.id, ${d.measure}::public.action_kind, ${authorId}::uuid, ${postId}::uuid, d.decided_at from public.decisions d where d.id = any(${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::uuid[])`);
      }
      return ids;
    };

    const measure = cells.measure ?? "remove";
    for (const [label, n] of Object.entries(cells.restrictions ?? {}) as [GroundLabel, number][]) {
      await decisions(n, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: label === "law" ? "illegal" : "incompatible", ruleId: label === "law" ? null : label, at: spread(year), measure });
    }
    await decisions(cells.interim ?? 0, { kind: "interim", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R4", at: spread(year), measure: "withhold" });
    await decisions(cells.noBreach ?? 0, { kind: "final", outcome: "no_violation", ground: null, ruleId: null, at: spread(year), measure: null });
    spareIds.push(...(await decisions(cells.spare ?? 0, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R3", at: spread(year - 1), measure })));
    for (const [kind, n] of Object.entries(cells.accountMeasures ?? {}) as [string, number][]) {
      await decisions(n, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R6", at: spread(year), measure: kind });
    }

    for (const [label, n] of Object.entries(cells.intakes ?? {}) as ["rules" | "illegal" | "finding", number][]) {
      const finding = label === "finding";
      const illegal = label === "illegal";
      await tx.execute(sql`
        insert into public.intakes (kind, ref, channel, finding_by, rule_id, alleges_illegal, category, explanation, bona_fide, received_at)
        select ${finding ? "finding" : "user"}::public.intake_kind, r.ref,
               ${finding ? "staff" : "signed_in"}::public.intake_channel, ${finding ? staff.id : null}::uuid, ${illegal ? null : finding ? "R3" : "R1"},
               ${illegal}, ${illegal ? "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH" : "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC"}, ${illegal ? "it is illegal" : null}, ${illegal},
               ${spread(year)}
          from unnest(${`{${Array.from({ length: n }, () => newRef()).join(",")}}`}::text[]) with ordinality as r(ref, g)`);
    }

    // An appeal answered in the year: the decision it appeals is of the year before (so no restriction of the year is
    // added), and the review that answers it is of the year, with the result the cell names.
    for (const [result, n] of Object.entries(cells.appeals ?? {}) as ["kept" | "partly_reversed" | "reversed", number][]) {
      const appealed = await decisions(n, { kind: "final", outcome: "restricted", ground: "incompatible", ruleId: "R1", at: spread(year - 1), measure });
      for (const decisionId of appealed) {
        const [appeal] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
          insert into public.appeals (decision_id, appellant_account_id, filed_at) values (${decisionId}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid, make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC')) returning id`);
        const [review] = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
          insert into public.decisions (case_id, kind, reviews_decision_id, appeal_id, seen_state_version, outcome, rules_version, redress_version, category, source,
                                        snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, reason_digest, decided_by, decided_at, xact, puid, informed_at, suspect, needs_admin, ended_interim)
          values (${caseId}::uuid, 'review', ${decisionId}::uuid, ${appeal!.id}::uuid, 0, ${result}::public.decision_outcome, 3, 3, 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE', 'report',
                  ${snapshot!.id}::uuid, ${hex64()}, ${hex64()}, ${staff.id}::uuid, make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC'), '1'::xid8, ${randomUUID().replaceAll("-", "")},
                  make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC'), false, false, false)
          returning id`);
        await tx.execute(sql`update public.appeals set answered_by = ${review!.id}::uuid, result = ${result}::public.appeal_result, answered_at = make_timestamptz(${year}::int, 3, 3, 12, 0, 0, 'UTC')
                              where id = ${appeal!.id}::uuid`);
      }
    }
  }
  // On again for what follows: a failure above aborted the transaction, which the caller rolls back with the switch.
  for (const table of BULK_TABLES) await tx.execute(sql.raw(`alter table public.${table} enable trigger user`));

  const orders: OrderView[] = [];
  for (const cell of cells.orders ?? []) orders.push(await orderOfYear(tx, year, cell, staff));
  return { caseId, orders, spareIds };
}

/**
 * One order of a year, as cli-counts.test.ts's fixture writes one: opened on new posts, its first `effectOn` items given
 * effect, its receipt recorded so many minutes before its last disabling, then every time of it moved back by whole
 * minutes so that its last disabling falls on `disabledAt`. A held one has Section C, so its order decisions are untold,
 * and its hold's recorded end at `heldUntil`.
 */
async function orderOfYear(tx: DbTx, year: number, cell: OrderCell, staff: TestStaff): Promise<OrderView> {
  const posts: string[] = [];
  for (let n = 0; n < cell.posts; n++) posts.push((await imagePost(tx, 1)).postId);
  const order = await orderForTest(tx, staff, { posts, memberState: cell.memberState ?? "DE", sectionC: cell.heldUntil !== undefined });
  const chosen = order.items.slice(0, cell.effectOn ?? order.items.length).map((item) => item.id);
  const view = chosen.length === 0 ? order : await effectWith(tx, staff, order.id, effectParams(order, { itemIds: chosen }));
  if (cell.receivedBefore !== undefined) {
    await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set received_at = coalesce((select max(disabled_at) from public.legal_order_items where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid), opened_at)
                                                                     - make_interval(mins => ${cell.receivedBefore}::int)
                          where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  }
  const target = cell.disabledAt ?? new Date(Date.UTC(year, 5, 15, 12));
  const [last] = await tx.execute<{ at: string }>(sql`select coalesce(max(disabled_at), (select opened_at from public.legal_orders where id = ${order.id}::uuid))::text as at
                                                       from public.legal_order_items where order_id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  await ageOrderForTest(tx, order.id, Math.round((new Date(last!.at).getTime() - target.getTime()) / 60_000));
  if (cell.heldUntil !== undefined) {
    await tx.execute(sql`update public.legal_orders set hold_ended_at = ${cell.heldUntil.toISOString()}::timestamptz, hold_end_reason = 'released_by_authority'
                          where id = ${order.id}::uuid`);
  }
  return view;
}

### Create `apps/api/test/transparency/count.test.ts`

```ts
import { createHmac } from "node:crypto";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { createMiddleware } from "hono/factory";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { PublicFacts, RECIPIENT_RULES, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { clientNetwork } from "../../src/auth";
import type { AuthDeps } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { resolveSession } from "../../src/auth/middleware";
import type { AppEnv } from "../../src/env";
import { publicTransparency, type TransparencyForAuth } from "../../src/transparency";
import { closeMonths, createRecipientCounter, isReadRoute, sketchKeys, type SketchStore } from "../../src/transparency/recipients";
import type { EditionRow } from "../../src/transparency/repo";
import { publicFacts } from "../../src/transparency/routes";

/**
 * The recipients' count and the public answers without a database (3d design, sections 5, 7.5, 7.6 and 10.6; Task 4;
 * invariants 22 and 23): what resolveSession hands the count, and only there; what the count writes to Valkey, a store
 * that keeps sets here, and nothing else; the month's close; the facts of a server with every tool off; and the shape of
 * the editions' answer. The same against the real Valkey and database is transparency-public.test.ts's.
 */

/** A store that keeps each sketch as the set of what was added, the salt as bytes, and every expiry asked for. */
function memoryStore() {
  const sketches = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
  const values = new Map<string, Buffer>();
  const expiries = new Map<string, number>();
  const calls: string[] = [];
  const store = {
    async pfadd(key: string, ...elements: string[]) {
      calls.push(`pfadd ${key}`);
      const set = sketches.get(key) ?? new Set<string>();
      const before = set.size;
      for (const element of elements) set.add(String(element));
      sketches.set(key, set);
      return set.size > before ? 1 : 0;
    },
    async pfcount(...keys: string[]) {
      return new Set(keys.flatMap((key) => [...(sketches.get(key) ?? [])])).size;
    },
    async expire(key: string, seconds: number, mode: string) {
      calls.push(`expire ${key} ${seconds} ${mode}`);
      if (mode === "NX" && expiries.has(key)) return 0;
      expiries.set(key, seconds);
      return 1;
    },
    async set(key: string, value: Buffer, ex: string, seconds: number, nx: string) {
      calls.push(`set ${key} ${ex} ${seconds} ${nx}`);
      if (nx === "NX" && values.has(key)) return null;
      values.set(key, value);
      expiries.set(key, seconds);
      return "OK";
    },
    async getBuffer(key: string) {
      return values.get(key) ?? null;
    },
    async exists(...keys: string[]) {
      return keys.filter((key) => sketches.has(key) || values.has(key)).length;
    },
    async del(...keys: string[]) {
      let n = 0;
      for (const key of keys) if (sketches.delete(key) || values.delete(key)) n++;
      return n;
    },
  };
  return { store: store as unknown as SketchStore, sketches, values, expiries, calls };
}

/** Lets the count's unwaited promises run. */
const settle = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
const log = pino({ level: "silent" });
const AT = new Date("2014-05-17T10:00:00.000Z");
/** A bearer token of the form the app sends, which the fake session store knows. */
const GOOD = `kb1_${"g".repeat(43)}`;
const FIREFOX = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64; rv:140.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/140.0";

describe("the recipients' count, as resolveSession hands it on (3d Task 4)", () => {
  /** The middleware alone, over a session store that knows one bearer token, and a client address set as clientIdentity sets it. */
  function app(handler: TransparencyForAuth | null) {
    const deps = {
      config: { allowedOrigins: ["http://localhost:8081"] },
      sessions: { resolve: async (token: string) => (token === GOOD ? { session: { userId: "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" }, slid: false } : null) },
    } as unknown as AuthDeps;
    const a = new Hono<AppEnv>();
    a.use(
      createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
        c.set("clientIp", "203.0.113.9");
        await next();
      }),
    );
    a.use(resolveSession(deps, () => handler));
    a.all("*", (c) => c.json({ ok: true }));
    return a;
  }
  function recording() {
    const calls: unknown[][] = [];
    const handler: TransparencyForAuth = {
      seen: (...args) => void calls.push(["seen", ...args]),
      seenSignedOut: (...args) => void calls.push(["seenSignedOut", ...args]),
    };
    return { calls, handler };
  }

  test("a request whose session resolved is seen by its account; a GET without one is seenSignedOut with the address, the agent and the path", async () => {
    const { calls, handler } = recording();
    const a = app(handler);
    expect((await a.request("/api/timeline/latest", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${GOOD}` } })).status).toBe(200);
    expect((await a.request("/api/timeline/latest", { headers: { "user-agent": FIREFOX } })).status).toBe(200);
    expect(calls).toEqual([
      ["seen", "a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"],
      ["seenSignedOut", "203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/timeline/latest"],
    ]);
  });

  test("a write without a session is not counted, nor is a token that resolves no session on a write", async () => {
    const { calls, handler } = recording();
    const a = app(handler);
    await a.request("/api/notices", { method: "POST" });
    await a.request("/api/notices", { method: "POST", headers: { authorization: `Bearer kb1_${"b".repeat(43)}` } });
    expect(calls).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("until a handler is registered nothing is counted, and a handler that throws never fails the request", async () => {
    expect((await app(null).request("/api/timeline/latest")).status).toBe(200);
    const throwing: TransparencyForAuth = {
      seen: () => {
        throw new Error("Valkey is down");
      },
      seenSignedOut: () => {
        throw new Error("Valkey is down");
      },
    };
    expect((await app(throwing).request("/api/timeline/latest")).status).toBe(200);
    expect((await app(throwing).request("/api/timeline/latest", { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${GOOD}` } })).status).toBe(200);
  });

  test("seen adds the account to the UTC month's sketch, which lives 70 days from its first write", async () => {
    const m = memoryStore();
    const count = createRecipientCounter({ store: m.store, signedOut: true, log, now: () => AT });
    count.seen("account-1");
    count.seen("account-1");
    count.seen("account-2");
    await settle();
    expect([...m.sketches.keys()]).toEqual(["mau:in:2014-05"]);
    expect(m.sketches.get("mau:in:2014-05")!.size).toBe(2);
    expect(m.expiries.get("mau:in:2014-05")).toBe(RECIPIENT_RULES.sketchDays * 86_400);
    expect(m.calls.filter((call) => call.startsWith("expire")).every((call) => call.endsWith(" NX"))).toBe(true);
  });

  test("seenSignedOut adds HMAC-SHA-256(the day's salt, network LF agent cut at 256 bytes) to the day's sketch, and nothing else is kept", async () => {
    const m = memoryStore();
    const count = createRecipientCounter({ store: m.store, signedOut: true, log, now: () => AT });
    const long = `${FIREFOX}${"x".repeat(400)}`;
    count.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/posts/3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a");
    // The same reader on another public read, and on another address of the same IPv6 /64, is one value.
    count.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/profiles/someone/replies");
    count.seenSignedOut("2001:db8:1:2:aaaa::1", long, "/api/timeline/explore");
    count.seenSignedOut("2001:db8:1:2:bbbb::2", `${long}yyyy`, "/api/timeline/latest");
    await settle();
    expect([...m.sketches.keys()]).toEqual(["mau:out:2014-05-17"]);
    expect([...m.values.keys()]).toEqual(["mau:salt:2014-05-17"]);
    const salt = m.values.get("mau:salt:2014-05-17")!;
    expect(salt.length).toBe(32);
    expect(m.expiries.get("mau:salt:2014-05-17")).toBe(RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours * 3_600);
    const digest = (address: string, agent: string) =>
      createHmac("sha256", salt)
        .update(Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(clientNetwork(address), "utf8"), Buffer.from([10]), Buffer.from(agent, "utf8").subarray(0, RECIPIENT_RULES.userAgentBytes)]))
        .digest("hex");
    expect([...m.sketches.get("mau:out:2014-05-17")!].sort()).toEqual([digest("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX), digest("2001:db8:1:2::", long)].sort());
    // The salt was set once, with SET NX and its 26 hours, and read back: the process keeps it for the day.
    expect(m.calls.filter((call) => call.startsWith("set "))).toEqual([`set mau:salt:2014-05-17 EX ${RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours * 3_600} NX`]);
  });

  test("seenSignedOut counts none of a crawler that names itself, another path, or anything while RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT is off", async () => {
    const m = memoryStore();
    const on = createRecipientCounter({ store: m.store, signedOut: true, log, now: () => AT });
    on.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; Googlebot/2.1)", "/api/timeline/latest");
    for (const path of ["/api/media/x/small.webp", "/api/posts/x/status", "/api/health", "/api/me", "/api/timeline/following", "/api/posts/x/explore", "/api/profiles/a/followers"]) on.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, path);
    const off = createRecipientCounter({ store: m.store, signedOut: false, log, now: () => AT });
    off.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/timeline/latest");
    await settle();
    expect(m.calls).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a store that fails or throws is swallowed: the calls return at once and throw nothing", async () => {
    const failing = new Proxy({}, { get: () => () => Promise.reject(new Error("Valkey is down")) }) as unknown as SketchStore;
    const throwing = new Proxy({}, {
      get: () => () => {
        throw new Error("Valkey is gone");
      },
    }) as unknown as SketchStore;
    for (const store of [failing, throwing]) {
      const count = createRecipientCounter({ store, signedOut: true, log, now: () => AT });
      expect(() => count.seen("account-1")).not.toThrow();
      expect(() => count.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/timeline/latest")).not.toThrow();
    }
    await settle();
  });

  test("the seven public reads are counted, and their neighbours are not", () => {
    for (const path of ["/api/posts/p1", "/api/posts/p1/thread", "/api/timeline/latest", "/api/timeline/explore", "/api/profiles/h", "/api/profiles/h/posts", "/api/profiles/h/replies"]) {
      expect([path, isReadRoute(path)]).toEqual([path, true]);
    }
    for (const path of ["/api/posts", "/api/posts/p1/status", "/api/posts/p1/like", "/api/profiles/h/follow", "/api/timeline/latest/x", "/api/public/facts"]) {
      expect([path, isReadRoute(path)]).toEqual([path, false]);
    }
  });

  test("source: the count writes nothing to PostgreSQL and logs no salt, digest, address or agent", () => {
    const source = readFileSync(new URL("../../src/transparency/recipients.ts", import.meta.url), "utf8");
    const counter = source.slice(source.indexOf("export function createRecipientCounter"), source.indexOf("const CLOSE_MONTHS"));
    expect(counter).not.toMatch(/repo|apiDb|execute|insert/);
    expect([...counter.matchAll(/log[.][a-z]+[(]([^;]*)[)]/g)].map((m) => m[1])).toEqual(['{ err }, "recipients: a count was not recorded"']);
  });
});

describe("the month's close (3d Task 4)", () => {
  function repoOf(stored: string[]) {
    const rows: { month: string; signedIn: number; signedOutDays: number | null; method: number }[] = [];
    return {
      rows,
      repo: {
        monthStored: async (month: string) => stored.includes(month) || rows.some((row) => row.month === month),
        storeMonth: async (row: (typeof rows)[number]) => {
          rows.push(row);
          return true;
        },
      },
    };
  }

  test("the month before stores the month's sketch's count and the sum of its days' counts, then its keys go", async () => {
    const m = memoryStore();
    const april = new Date("2014-04-10T08:00:00.000Z");
    const count = createRecipientCounter({ store: m.store, signedOut: true, log, now: () => april });
    count.seen("a");
    count.seen("b");
    count.seenSignedOut("203.0.113.9", FIREFOX, "/api/timeline/latest");
    await settle();
    const { repo, rows } = repoOf([]);
    expect(await closeMonths({ store: m.store, repo, signedOut: true }, AT)).toEqual(["2014-04"]);
    expect(rows).toEqual([{ month: "2014-04", signedIn: 2, signedOutDays: 1, method: RECIPIENT_RULES.method }]);
    expect([...m.sketches.keys()]).toEqual([]);
    // Again: nothing to close.
    expect(await closeMonths({ store: m.store, repo, signedOut: true }, AT)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("with RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT off the second number is null; a month without a sketch gets no row; a stored month only loses its keys", async () => {
    const m = memoryStore();
    await m.store.pfadd(sketchKeys.month("2014-03"), "a");
    await m.store.pfadd(sketchKeys.month("2014-04"), "b");
    const { repo, rows } = repoOf(["2014-03"]);
    expect(await closeMonths({ store: m.store, repo, signedOut: false }, AT)).toEqual(["2014-04"]);
    expect(rows).toEqual([{ month: "2014-04", signedIn: 1, signedOutDays: null, method: RECIPIENT_RULES.method }]);
    expect(m.sketches.has(sketchKeys.month("2014-03"))).toBe(false);
    // The running month is never closed.
    await m.store.pfadd(sketchKeys.month("2014-05"), "c");
    expect(await closeMonths({ store: m.store, repo, signedOut: false }, AT)).toEqual([]);
    expect(m.sketches.has(sketchKeys.month("2014-05"))).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("the public answers' shape (3d Task 4)", () => {
  test("the facts of a server with every tool off, the edge as its adapter, and the setting", () => {
    const off = publicFacts({ EDGE_PURGE: "off", RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: "on" });
    expect(PublicFacts.parse(off)).toEqual(off);
    expect([off.r1.state, off.match.state, off.edge, off.witness, off.recipientsSignedOut]).toEqual(["off", "off", { on: false, test: false }, { on: false, test: false }, true]);
    expect(publicFacts({ EDGE_PURGE: "test", RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: "off" })).toMatchObject({ edge: { on: true, test: true }, recipientsSignedOut: false });
    expect(publicFacts({ EDGE_PURGE: "cloudflare", RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: "on" }).edge).toEqual({ on: true, test: false });
  });

  test("the editions' answer: each year's newest version, newest year first, with its older versions and the day each was replaced", () => {
    const figures = { restrictions: { byGround: [], byMeasure: [], total: "0" }, noBreach: "0", intakes: [], appeals: [], reexaminations: [], accountMeasures: [], automated: { findings: [], measures: [] }, recipients: "not recorded" } as TransparencyFigures;
    const row = (year: number, version: number, at: string, reason: EditionRow["reason"]): EditionRow => ({ year, version, publishedAt: new Date(at), method: 1, reason, figures });
    const answer = publicTransparency([

    expect(answer.editions.map((edition) => [edition.year, edition.version, edition.publishedOn, edition.reason, edition.older.map((older) => [older.version, older.publishedOn, older.replacedOn, older.reason])])).toEqual([
      [2014, 3, "2016-01-05", "correction", [[1, "2015-03-01", "2015-05-02", "first"], [2, "2015-05-02", "2016-01-05", "hold_ended"]]],
      [2013, 1, "2014-03-01", "first", []],
    ]);
  });
});

### Create `apps/api/test/transparency/route-table.test.ts`

```ts
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { createDb } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AppEnv } from "../../src/env";
import { MemoryStore } from "../../src/middleware/rate-limit";
import { createSocial } from "../../src/social";

/**
 * The route table of the recipients' count (3d design, sections 7.5 and 10.1; Task 4): RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES are exactly
 * the reads of the social module that answer without a session, so a signed-out read added later fails here until it is
 * listed there or refused below by name. The database pool is created and never connects: only the table is read.
 */
describe("RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES and the social module's signed-out reads (3d Task 4)", () => {
  /** Signed-out reads that are deliberately not counted, each with why. */
  const NOT_COUNTED: Record<string, string> = {
    // Caddy asks it for every view of a post's page (3f): the page's own read is what a person makes.
    "GET /api/posts/:id/status": "the page status, which Caddy asks",
  };

  function signedOutReads(): string[] {
    const guard: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv> = async (_c, next) => next();
    const fresh: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv> = async (_c, next) => next();
    const social = createSocial({ apiDb: createDb("postgres://a:b@localhost:55432/k", { max: 1 }), rateLimitStore: new MemoryStore(), logger: pino({ level: "silent" }), requireSession: guard, requireFreshAuth: fresh });
    const chains = new Map<string, unknown[]>();
    for (const router of [social.routes, social.statusRoutes]) {
      for (const route of router.routes) {
        if (route.method !== "GET") continue;
        const key = `GET /api${route.path}`;
        chains.set(key, [...(chains.get(key) ?? []), route.handler]);
      }
    }
    return [...chains.entries()].filter(([, handlers]) => !handlers.includes(guard)).map(([key]) => key);
  }

  test("every GET of the social module without the session guard is a counted read or refused by name, and every counted read is one", () => {
    const reads = signedOutReads();
    const counted = reads.filter((route) => !(route in NOT_COUNTED));
    expect(counted.sort()).toEqual([...RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES].sort());
    for (const route of Object.keys(NOT_COUNTED)) expect(reads).toContain(route);
  });

  test("the check reads the guard: a guarded read such as the Following timeline is no signed-out read", () => {
    const reads = signedOutReads();
    expect(reads).not.toContain("GET /api/timeline/following");
    expect(reads).not.toContain("GET /api/me/likes");
    expect(reads).toContain("GET /api/timeline/latest");
  });
});
```

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { cloneElement, type ReactElement } from "react";
import { renderToStaticMarkup } from "react-dom/server";
import { describe, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";
import { EDGE_CACHE, EDGE_WORDS, RECIPIENT_RULES, TRANSPARENCY_RULES, type PublicFacts, type PublicTransparency, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { RULES, RULES_CHANGES, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";

vi.mock("expo-router", () => ({
  Link: ({ href, children }: { href: string; children: ReactElement }) => cloneElement(children, { href } as object),
  Redirect: () => null,
  router: { push: () => undefined, replace: () => undefined },
  useLocalSearchParams: () => ({}),
  usePathname: () => "/rules",
}));
vi.mock("@/lib/session", () => ({ useSession: () => ({ state: { status: "signed-out" }, refresh: async () => undefined }) }));
vi.mock("react-native-reanimated", () => ({ useReducedMotion: () => false }));

import { RulesView } from "../src/app/rules";
import { TransparencyView } from "../src/app/transparency";
import { PAGE_DOWN, RULES_PAGE, TOOL_TEXTS, TRANSPARENCY_PAGE, toolBlocks, type AutomationLimits } from "../src/lib/public-pages";
import { MEASURES_PARAGRAPH, TERMS_SECTIONS, termsParagraphs } from "../src/lib/terms";

/**
 * The two public pages (3d design, sections 9.1 to 9.3, 10.8 and 12.2; W.1 and W.2; Task 4): server-rendered checks of
 * both pages with every tool off, with the route down and with stored editions; TOOL_TEXTS in every state a tool can be
 * in; the rules page and the terms printing their numbered sentences with the same builders; every number of the words
 * held to its constant; and the smoke test's two lead sentences held to the pages' own.
 */

const html = (element: ReactElement): string => renderToStaticMarkup(element);
/** The markup's text as a reader sees it: tags dropped, the entities React writes decoded, spaces collapsed. */
const textOf = (markup: string): string =>
  markup
    .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")
    .replaceAll("&#x27;", "'")
    .replaceAll("&quot;", '"')
    .replaceAll("&gt;", ">")
    .replaceAll("&lt;", "<")
    .replaceAll("&amp;", "&")
    .replace(/ +/g, " ");

const OFF: PublicFacts = {
  r1: { state: "off", test: false, model: null, digest: null, threshold: null, thresholdVersion: null, publisherClaim: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
  match: { state: "off", test: false, source: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
  edge: { on: false, test: false },
  witness: { on: false, test: false },
  recipientsSignedOut: true,
};
const LIMITS: AutomationLimits = { decisionsPerHour: 20, decisionsPerDay: 100, r2DecisionsPerHour: 21, r2DecisionsPerDay: 101, unansweredMax: 22, unansweredHours: 72, refusalsPerHour: 23, objectionTargetHours: 24 };

describe("the rules page (3d Task 4)", () => {
  test("every rule with its text and its lists, the law, the measures and the numbered sections, every tool off, and the change log newest first", () => {
    const markup = html(<RulesView facts={OFF} />);
    const text = textOf(markup);
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.lead);
    for (const rule of RULES) {
      expect(text).toContain(`${rule.id}: ${rule.title}`);
      expect(text).toContain(rule.text);
      for (const item of [...rule.allowed, ...rule.notAllowed]) expect(text).toContain(item);
    }
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.law);
    expect(text).toContain(MEASURES_PARAGRAPH);
    for (const tool of [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off, TOOL_TEXTS.match.off, TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off, TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off, RULES_PAGE.autoNone]) expect(text).toContain(tool);
    expect(text).not.toContain(PAGE_DOWN);
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.version(RULES_VERSION));
    const changes = [...RULES_CHANGES].reverse().map((change) => text.indexOf(RULES_PAGE.change(change)));
    expect(changes.every((at) => at > -1)).toBe(true);
    expect([...changes].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(changes);
    // The headings, each a header of its level, and the links to the other page and to How Explore works.
    for (const heading of [RULES_PAGE.rulesHeading, RULES_PAGE.measuresHeading, RULES_PAGE.automationHeading, RULES_PAGE.versionHeading]) expect(markup).toContain(`aria-level="2"`);
    expect(markup).toContain('href="/transparency"');
    expect(markup).toContain('href="/explore/about"');
  });

  test("the numbered sentences are the terms' own: the same builders print Strikes, Suspension, Reporting in bad faith and Terrorist content in both", () => {
    const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={OFF} />));
    for (const title of ["Strikes", "Suspension and termination", "Reporting in bad faith", "Terrorist content"]) {
      const section = TERMS_SECTIONS.find((candidate) => candidate.title === title);
      expect(section, title).toBeDefined();
      for (const paragraph of termsParagraphs(section!.body)) expect(text).toContain(paragraph);
    }
    const decide = TERMS_SECTIONS.find((section) => section.title === "How moderators decide")!;
    expect(termsParagraphs(decide.body)).toContain(MEASURES_PARAGRAPH);
  });

  test("while the facts are read the automation section holds its lead alone; when the route does not answer it reads [page.down] and prints no tool as off or on", () => {
    for (const [facts, down] of [["loading", false], ["down", true]] as const) {
      const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={facts} />));
      expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoLead);
      expect(text.includes(PAGE_DOWN)).toBe(down);
      for (const tool of [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off, TOOL_TEXTS.match.off, TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off, TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off, RULES_PAGE.autoNone]) expect(text).not.toContain(tool);
      expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.lead);
    }
  });

  test("with a tool that rates or compares images on, the caps and the target from the limits, and no [rules.auto.none]", () => {
    const on = { ...OFF, match: { state: "alerts", test: true, source: "test", dpia: "2026-10-01", dpiaActs: null } } as PublicFacts;
    const text = textOf(html(<RulesView facts={on} limits={LIMITS} />));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS));
    expect(text).toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoTarget(LIMITS.objectionTargetHours));
    expect(text).not.toContain(RULES_PAGE.autoNone);
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("at most 20 measures an hour and 100 a day under rule R1, and at most 21 an hour and 101 a day under rule R2");
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("while 22 of its measures");
    expect(RULES_PAGE.autoCap(LIMITS)).toContain("refuses at most 23 uploads an hour");
  });
});

describe("TOOL_TEXTS in each state (3d Task 4, W.1)", () => {
  const blockOf = (facts: PublicFacts, tool: string) => toolBlocks(facts).find((block) => block.tool === tool)!;

  test("every tool off, as the facts route answers until the tasks that build them: each block its off text alone", () => {
    expect(toolBlocks(OFF).map((block) => [block.tool, block.on, block.paragraphs])).toEqual([
      ["r1", false, [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off]],
      ["match", false, [TOOL_TEXTS.match.off]],
      ["edge", false, [TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off]],
      ["witness", false, [TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off]],
    ]);
  });

  test("the R1 check flagging, withholding and on a test adapter; its model's facts; its own dates, the measure's only while it acts", () => {
    const model = { model: "Marqo/nsfw-image-detection-384", digest: "ab".repeat(32), threshold: 0.9, thresholdVersion: 2, publisherClaim: "a claim" };
    const flags = blockOf({ ...OFF, r1: { ...OFF.r1, ...model, state: "flags", dpia: "2026-10-01", dpiaActs: "2026-10-02" } }, "r1");
    expect(flags.paragraphs).toEqual([TOOL_TEXTS.r1.flags, TOOL_TEXTS.r1.facts(model), RULES_PAGE.dpia("2026-10-01")]);
    const withholds = blockOf({ ...OFF, r1: { ...OFF.r1, ...model, state: "withholds", dpia: "2026-10-01", dpiaActs: "2026-10-02" } }, "r1");
    expect(withholds.paragraphs).toEqual([TOOL_TEXTS.r1.withholds, TOOL_TEXTS.r1.facts(model), RULES_PAGE.dpia("2026-10-01"), RULES_PAGE.dpiaActs("2026-10-02")]);
    const test = blockOf({ ...OFF, r1: { ...OFF.r1, state: "flags", test: true } }, "r1");
    expect(test.paragraphs).toEqual([TOOL_TEXTS.r1.flags.replace(": on.", ": on (test adapter).")]);
    expect(TOOL_TEXTS.r1.facts(model)).toContain('Its publisher states: "a claim".');
    // A date set for one tool never stands over another.
    expect(blockOf({ ...OFF, r1: { ...OFF.r1, state: "flags", dpia: "2026-10-01" } }, "match").paragraphs).toEqual([TOOL_TEXTS.match.off]);

      reinstated: Object.fromEntries(ORDER_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, 0])),

      terroristWithoutOrder: 1,
      referralsClosed: 0,

    const erased = { ...orders, received: null, itemsDisabled: null, minutes: null, annex3: null, scrutiny: null, reinstated: null, authorityAccess: null };
    expect(TransparencyFigures.safeParse({ ...figures, orders: erased }).success).toBe(true);
    // No issuing state: the page prints none (section 2, row 4).
    expect(TransparencyFigures.safeParse({ ...figures, orders: { ...orders, received: { total: 1, crossBorder: 0, byState: [["DE", 1]] } } }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  /**
   * The schema test of 10.6: walks both answers' schemas and holds that no member could carry an id of a post, a case, a
   * decision or an account, a handle, a day of a decision, a place in the chain, a hash or a score, and that every number
   * and every free string outside the order section is one the design names: a year, a version, a method, an edition's
   * day, an impact assessment's day, or the facts' model, digest and claim.
   */
  test("no public answer has a member that could hold an id, a handle, a decision's day or a number under ten outside the order section", () => {
    const leaves: { path: string; type: string }[] = [];
    walk(PublicFacts, "facts", leaves);
    walk(PublicTransparency, "transparency", leaves);
    const forbidden = /(^|[.])(id|[a-z]*Id|handle|decidedAt|day|chainSeq|seq|place|hash|score|sha256|pdq|file|post|case|decision|account)$/;
    for (const leaf of leaves) expect([leaf.path, forbidden.test(leaf.path.replaceAll("[]", ""))]).toEqual([leaf.path, false]);
    const outsideOrders = leaves.filter((leaf) => !leaf.path.includes(".orders"));
    const numbers = outsideOrders.filter((leaf) => leaf.type === "number").map((leaf) => leaf.path);
    expect(numbers.sort()).toEqual(
      [
        "facts.r1.threshold",
        "facts.r1.thresholdVersion",
        "transparency.editions[].method",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].version",
        "transparency.editions[].version",
        "transparency.editions[].year",
      ].sort(),
    );
    const strings = outsideOrders.filter((leaf) => leaf.type === "string").map((leaf) => leaf.path);
    expect(strings.sort()).toEqual(
      [
        "facts.match.dpia",
        "facts.match.dpiaActs",
        "facts.match.source",
        "facts.r1.digest",
        "facts.r1.dpia",
        "facts.r1.dpiaActs",
        "facts.r1.model",
        "facts.r1.publisherClaim",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].publishedOn",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].replacedOn",
        "transparency.editions[].publishedOn",
      ].sort(),
    );

/** Collects the leaves of a zod schema with their paths: a band (a string under the band's pattern), an enum, a literal, a string, a number or a boolean. */
function walk(schema: z.ZodType, path: string, out: { path: string; type: string }[]): void {
  const def = (schema as unknown as { def: { type: string } & Record<string, unknown> }).def;
  switch (def.type) {
    case "object":
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(def.shape as Record<string, z.ZodType>)) walk(value, `${path}.${key}`, out);
      return;
    case "array":
      walk(def.element as z.ZodType, `${path}[]`, out);
      return;
    case "union":
      for (const option of def.options as z.ZodType[]) walk(option, path, out);
      return;
    case "optional":
    case "nullable":
      walk(def.innerType as z.ZodType, path, out);
      return;
    case "record":
      walk(def.valueType as z.ZodType, `${path}.*`, out);
      return;
    case "string": {
      const checks = (def.checks as { _zod: { def: { check: string; pattern?: RegExp } } }[] | undefined) ?? [];
      const banded = checks.some((check) => check._zod.def.pattern?.source === BAND_SOURCE);
      out.push({ path, type: banded ? "band" : "string" });
      return;
    }
    default:
      out.push({ path, type: def.type });
  }
}

/** The pattern a banded string is held to. */
const BAND_SOURCE = "^(0|1 to 9|about [1-9][0-9]*0)$";

### Replace `apps/admin/test/readme.test.ts` (whole file)

````ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_RULES, ALERT_TEXTS, EDGE_CACHE, EDGE_RULES, ORDER_RULES, RECIPIENT_RULES, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, RETENTION, STANDING_RULES, TRANSPARENCY_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AUTOMATION_WORDS } from "../src/messages";
import { ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK, RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK } from "../src/screens/Home";

/**
 * The README's moderation runbook and the console's home screen say the same thing (3c design, section 13, Task 12).
 * When decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes, or an erasure is more than a day late, the
 * home screen shows the count with the runbook's sentence for it, and each sentence is a constant of the screen. This
 * test reads README.md from the repository's root and holds the runbook to the same two constants, word for word, so
 * that what staff are told on the screen is what the operator reads in the runbook: whoever changes one changes both.
 */
const README = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md");

/** Markdown's code mark. The README sets a log line or a setting in code marks; the console shows the same words as plain text. */
const CODE_MARK = "`";

/** A text as its reader sees it: without the code marks. Nothing else is changed, so every word and every sign must agree. */
const withoutCodeMarks = (text: string): string => text.split(CODE_MARK).join("");

/** The README's lines, as written. */
function readmeLines(): string[] {
  return readFileSync(README, "utf8").split("\n");
}

/** The lines of the README's section "Moderation": from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function moderationSection(): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf("## Moderation");
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}

/** The section's runbook as its reader sees it: every line after "The runbook:", without the code marks. */
function moderationRunbook(): string {
  const section = moderationSection();
  const start = section.indexOf("The runbook:");
  return start === -1 ? "" : withoutCodeMarks(section.slice(start + 1).join("\n"));
}

/** How often `part` stands in `text`. */
const count = (text: string, part: string): number => text.split(part).length - 1;

describe("the README's moderation runbook says what the home screen says", () => {
  const sentences: [string, string][] = [
    ["decisions not released", RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
    ["late erasures", ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
  ];

  test("the README has a section Moderation, and the section has a runbook", () => {
    expect(readmeLines()).toContain("## Moderation");
    expect(moderationSection()).toContain("The runbook:");
    expect(moderationRunbook().trim()).not.toBe("");
  });

  test("neither constant holds a code mark or a line break, so reading the README without its code marks hides no difference", () => {
    for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain(CODE_MARK);
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain("\n");
      // A whole sentence: it opens with "A count of" and ends in a full stop, as the runbook's bullet writes it.
      expect(sentence.startsWith("A count of "), name).toBe(true);
      expect(sentence.endsWith("."), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
    test(`the runbook holds the home screen's sentence for ${name}, word for word`, () => {
      expect(moderationRunbook()).toContain(sentence);
    });

    test(`the sentence for ${name} stands once in the README, in that runbook: no second copy can drift from it`, () => {
      expect(count(withoutCodeMarks(readmeLines().join("\n")), sentence)).toBe(1);
      expect(count(moderationRunbook(), sentence)).toBe(1);
    });
  }

  test("both sentences stand in one bullet of the runbook, the release's first, as the home screen orders its two lines", () => {
    const bullets = moderationRunbook()
      .split("\n")
      .filter((line) => line.includes(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK) || line.includes(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
    expect(bullets).toHaveLength(1);
    const bullet = bullets[0] ?? "";
    expect(bullet.startsWith("- ")).toBe(true);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
  });
});

/**
 * The README's account sanctions (3e design, section 13, Task 7) and the constants they print. The section Moderation
 * describes 3e in a paragraph that opens with ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD and a bullet for each title below, and its runbook
 * gains the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h). Every number in that text is a number of STANDING_RULES or
 * REPLY_AIM_HOURS: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused, so the README cannot
 * keep a number the constants changed. A bullet added to 3e's text joins its list here.
 */
const ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD = "Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;";
const STANDING_TITLES = [
  "Strikes.",
  "The ladder.",
  "Announced suspensions and the reply.",
  "Suspensions at once.",
  "While suspended.",
  "Termination.",
  "The restriction of reporting.",
  "Handle retirement.",
  "What is kept of them.",
  "The Standing screen.",
  // The runbook's bullets (a) to (h).
  "Account sanctions each working day.",
  "Answering a reply.",
  "A protective suspension.",
  "A breach that lies only in a handle",
  "A notice a person did not get by mail.",
  "A measure at once while an announced suspension waits.",
  "A mark that was wrong.",
  "Reports before an account measure.",
] as const;

/** The lines of 3e's text in Moderation, without code marks: the lead paragraph and each bullet by its bold title. */
function standingLines(): { lead: string | undefined; bullets: Map<string, string[]> } {
  const section = moderationSection().map(withoutCodeMarks);
  const bullets = new Map(STANDING_TITLES.map((title) => [title as string, section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`))]));
  return { lead: section.find((line) => line.startsWith(ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD)), bullets };
}
const standingText = (): string => {
  const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
  return [lead ?? "", ...[...bullets.values()].flat()].join("\n");
};

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const S = STANDING_RULES;
const STANDING_NUMBERS: { constant: string; phrase: string }[] = [

  { constant: "ladderMemoryDays", phrase: `the ladder suspensions decided in the last ${S.ladderMemoryDays} days` },
  { constant: "replyWindowHours", phrase: `The suspension starts ${S.replyWindowHours} hours after korbat's relay accepted the notice mail` },
  { constant: "undeliveredHours", phrase: `or ${S.undeliveredHours} hours after the decision` },
  { constant: "threatDays", phrase: `(up to ${S.threatDays} days), terrorist content` },
  { constant: "terroristDays", phrase: `likewise (up to ${S.terroristDays} days)` },
  { constant: "floodPosts", phrase: `at least ${S.floodPosts} posts in the last` },
  { constant: "floodMinutes", phrase: `posts in the last ${S.floodMinutes} minutes` },
  { constant: "floodDays", phrase: `minutes (up to ${S.floodDays} days)` },
  { constant: "basisAgeDays", phrase: `at most ${S.basisAgeDays} days old` },
  { constant: "protectiveDays", phrase: `once for that seal (up to ${S.protectiveDays} days)` },
  { constant: "protectiveDays", phrase: `for at most ${S.protectiveDays} days, never worded as a finding` },
  { constant: "reportWarnMarks", phrase: `At least ${S.reportWarnMarks} marked reports in ${S.reportFrameDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictMarks", phrase: `${S.reportRestrictMarks} marked reports sent after it, while it counts (${S.reportFrameDays} days)` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictDays", phrase: `open a restriction of at most ${S.reportRestrictDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportFrameDays", phrase: `the marks and the daily tallies ${S.reportFrameDays} days after their report's UTC day` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `korbat aims to answer a reply to one within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `answer within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
];

describe("the README's account sanctions say what the constants say (3e design, section 13, Task 7)", () => {
  test("Moderation opens 3e's part with its paragraph, and each of its bullets stands there once", () => {
    const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
    expect(lead).toBeDefined();

    for (const title of STANDING_TITLES.slice(STANDING_TITLES.indexOf("Account sanctions each working day."))) expect(runbook.some((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`)), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3e's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {

    for (const row of STANDING_NUMBERS) expect(text, `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);

    const outside = standingText()
      .replace(/docs\/superpowers\/specs\/[0-9a-z-]+\.md/g, " ")
      .replace(/\b[0-9][a-f]\b/g, " ")
      .replace(/\bR[1-6]\b/g, " ")
      .replace(/Art\. [0-9]+(\([0-9]+\))?(\([a-z]\))?/g, " ");
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("the lines 3e made false are gone: the handle left open for 3e, formula version 1 and the mails that name 3e", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join("\n");

    expect(all).not.toContain("Until sub-project 3e's formula version 2");
    expect(all).not.toContain("EXPLORE_V1");
    expect(all).not.toContain("still names sub-project 3e");
    // The hard gate names 3f's order path and 3d's handling of sealed images, as it did since 3e's design; since 3d Task 2
    // in W.11's words, its quarantine and release.
    expect(all).toContain("until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's quarantine and release have shipped");
