### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/editions.ts`

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { PublicTransparency } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { EditionRow, TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The yearly edition (3d design, sections 2 rows 2 to 5, 6.4 and 7.6). Once a day, after the dispatch hour, the
 * transparency job asks edition_publish(year, 'first') for the last closed year and for every earlier year that has an
 * edition; the database decides, under an advisory lock on the year, whether to write version 1 (once the year is due on
 * 1 March of the next one), a version hold_ended (an order whose hold ended since), or nothing. Each call is idempotent
 * by the table's key, so a round that asks again writes nothing; a correction is the command line's alone.
 */

/** What one daily pass wrote: each year with the version stored, and the years asked. */
export interface EditionPass {
  asked: number[];
  published: { year: number; version: number }[];
}

export async function publishEditions(deps: { repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "publish" | "yearsWithEdition">; log: Logger }, now: Date): Promise<EditionPass> {
  const last = now.getUTCFullYear() - 1;
  const asked = [last, ...(await deps.repo.yearsWithEdition(last))];
  const published: EditionPass["published"] = [];
  for (const year of asked) {
    const version = await deps.repo.publish(year);
    if (version !== null) {
      published.push({ year, version });
      deps.log.info({ job: "transparency", year, version }, "transparency: an edition was published");
    }
  }
  return { asked, published };
}

/** A day as the public pages print it, in UTC. */
const dayOf = (at: Date) => at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/**
 * GET /api/public/transparency's answer (10.6): every year's newest version, newest year first, with the older versions of
 * that year, oldest first, each with the day the next version replaced it. The rows come newest year and version first.
 */
export function publicTransparency(rows: readonly EditionRow[]): PublicTransparency {
  const byYear = new Map<number, EditionRow[]>();
  for (const row of rows) byYear.set(row.year, [...(byYear.get(row.year) ?? []), row]);
  return {
    editions: [...byYear.entries()]
      .sort(([a], [b]) => b - a)
      .map(([year, versions]) => {
        const sorted = [...versions].sort((a, b) => a.version - b.version);
        const newest = sorted.at(-1)!;
        return {
          year,
          version: newest.version,
          publishedOn: dayOf(newest.publishedAt),
          method: newest.method,
          reason: newest.reason,
          figures: newest.figures,
          older: sorted.slice(0, -1).map((older, at) => ({
            version: older.version,
            publishedOn: dayOf(older.publishedAt),
            replacedOn: dayOf(sorted[at + 1]!.publishedAt),
            reason: older.reason,
            figures: older.figures,
          })),
        };
      }),
  };
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/index.ts`

```ts
/**
 * The transparency module (3d design, sections 4 row 4, 5, 7.5, 7.6 and 7.14; Task 4): the public figures and the
 * public answers. The only file outside src/transparency/ may import; it reads no session and no table of a person, and
 * the architecture test holds every file of it to the names of @korbat/db's schema/transparency.ts and the audit head.
 *
 *   - the recipients' count: the two calls the auth module's resolveSession makes (forAuth, registered with auth.onSeen
 *     once both modules exist) and the month's close;
 *   - the yearly edition: the daily call of edition_publish() for the last closed year and every earlier year with one;
 *   - GET /api/public/facts and GET /api/public/transparency;
 *   - one job, `transparency`, every ten minutes under the jobs' shared lock: the month's close each round, and once a
 *     day after MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR the editions. Each daily part is idempotent by its table's key, so a round after a
 *     restart that runs it again writes nothing.
 */
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import { publishEditions } from "./editions";
import { closeMonths, createRecipientCounter, type RecipientCounter, type SketchStore } from "./recipients";
import { createTransparencyRepo } from "./repo";
import { publicFacts, transparencyRoutes } from "./routes";

export type { SketchStore } from "./recipients";
export { publicTransparency } from "./editions";
export { isReadRoute, sketchKeys } from "./recipients";

/**
 * What the auth module needs from this one (section 5, `auth.onSeen`): resolveSession calls `seen` when a session
 * resolved and `seenSignedOut` for a GET when none did. Both return at once; neither throws, and a failure of Valkey is
 * swallowed: counting never fails or slows a request.
 */
export type TransparencyForAuth = RecipientCounter;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:transparency`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const TRANSPARENCY_JOB = "transparency";
/** Ten minutes between the end of one round and the start of the next (7.14). */
export const TRANSPARENCY_ROUND_MS = 10 * 60_000;

export interface CreateTransparencyOptions {
  apiDb: Db;
  /** Valkey, for the sketches and the salt. */
  redis: SketchStore;
  config: Pick<Config, "EDGE_PURGE" | "RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT" | "MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR">;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The clock of the counts and of the job's rounds; tests move it. */
  now?: () => Date;
}

/** What one round of the job did: the months it closed, and the editions it published once a day. */
export interface TransparencyRound {
  months: string[];
  editions: { year: number; version: number }[] | null;
}

export function createTransparency(options: CreateTransparencyOptions) {
  const now = options.now ?? (() => new Date());
  const log = options.logger;
  const repo = createTransparencyRepo(options.apiDb);
  const signedOut = options.config.RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT === "on";
  const forAuth: TransparencyForAuth = createRecipientCounter({ store: options.redis, signedOut, log, now });
  // The UTC day of this process's last daily pass: one a day, after the dispatch hour. A restart runs it again, which
  // the editions' key makes harmless.
  let lastDaily: string | null = null;

  async function round(): Promise<TransparencyRound> {
    const at = now();
    const months = await closeMonths({ store: options.redis, repo, signedOut }, at);
    if (months.length > 0) log.info({ job: TRANSPARENCY_JOB, months }, "transparency: the recipients' months were stored");
    const day = at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
    if (lastDaily === day || at.getUTCHours() < options.config.MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR) return { months, editions: null };
    const pass = await publishEditions({ repo, log }, at);
    lastDaily = day;
    return { months, editions: pass.published };
  }

  return {
    /** The interface the auth module calls, registered with auth.onSeen in index.ts. */
    forAuth,
    /** The two public routes, mounted by app.ts at /api before the session's resolution. */
    routes: transparencyRoutes({ repo, facts: publicFacts(options.config) }),
    /** One round of the job, as the timer runs it; for tests. */
    round,
    /** Starts the job `transparency` and returns the function that stops it. */
    startJobs: (lock: JobLock) => createJob({ name: TRANSPARENCY_JOB, intervalMs: TRANSPARENCY_ROUND_MS, lockTtlMs: TRANSPARENCY_ROUND_MS * 2, lock, log, run: round }).start(),
  };
}

export type Transparency = ReturnType<typeof createTransparency>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/recipients.ts`

```ts
import { createHmac, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import type Redis from "ioredis";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES, RECIPIENT_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { clientNetwork } from "../auth";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The recipients' count (3d design, section 2 row 8 and section 7.5), method 1. It counts in sketches that hold no
 * member: a HyperLogLog in Valkey answers "about how many different values were added" and cannot give one back.
 *
 *   A, signed in: every request whose session resolved adds the account's id to `mau:in:<yyyy-mm>`, the UTC month's sketch.
 *   B, signed out (only while RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT is on): a GET of one of the seven public reads of the social module
 *      without a session adds HMAC-SHA-256(the day's salt, network LF user agent) to `mau:out:<yyyy-mm-dd>`, the network
 *      being clientNetwork(address) and the agent cut at 256 bytes. The salt, `mau:salt:<yyyy-mm-dd>`, is 32 random bytes
 *      set once with SET NX and 26 hours to live, kept in memory for its UTC day and written nowhere else, so after 26
 *      hours nobody, korbat included, can compute a digest again. An agent that names itself a crawler is left out; nothing
 *      else is guessed about a reader.
 *
 * Neither call is waited for, and every failure of Valkey is swallowed: counting never fails or slows a request. Every
 * sketch dies 70 days after its first write if the month's close never took it. The close, the transparency job's step on
 * its first round after a UTC month ended, stores two numbers in recipient_months and deletes the month's keys.
 */

/** The part of the Valkey client the sketches use. */
export type SketchStore = Pick<Redis, "pfadd" | "pfcount" | "expire" | "set" | "getBuffer" | "exists" | "del">;

/** What the auth module's resolveSession calls (section 5, `auth.onSeen`); both return at once and never throw. */
export interface RecipientCounter {
  /** A request whose session resolved. */
  seen(accountId: string): void;
  /** A request without a session: counted only for a GET of one of RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES, and only while the setting is on. */
  seenSignedOut(address: string, userAgent: string, path: string): void;
}

/** The UTC month of an instant, yyyy-mm. */
const monthOf = (at: Date) => at.toISOString().slice(0, 7);
/** The UTC day of an instant, yyyy-mm-dd. */
const dayOf = (at: Date) => at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** The three kinds of key the count writes, and no other (invariant 23). */
export const sketchKeys = {
  month: (month: string) => `mau:in:${month}`,
  day: (day: string) => `mau:out:${day}`,
  salt: (day: string) => `mau:salt:${day}`,
};

/**
 * The seven reads as patterns of a GET's path: a parameter matches one segment. Built once from the contracts' list,
 * which names the routes with their method.
 */
const READ_PATHS: readonly RegExp[] = RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES.map((route) => {
  const path = route.slice(route.indexOf(" ") + 1);
  const pattern = path
    .split("/")
    .map((segment) => (segment.startsWith(":") ? "[^/]+" : segment))
    .join("/");
  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);
});

/** Whether a GET of this path is one of the seven public reads. */
export const isReadRoute = (path: string) => READ_PATHS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(path));

const LF = Buffer.from([10]);
const SKETCH_SECONDS = RECIPIENT_RULES.sketchDays * 86_400;
const SALT_SECONDS = RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours * 3_600;

export interface RecipientsDeps {
  store: SketchStore;
  /** RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: whether signed-out readers are counted. */
  signedOut: boolean;
  log: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

/** The two calls the auth module makes, over the store; each failure is logged at debug and dropped. */
export function createRecipientCounter(deps: RecipientsDeps): RecipientCounter {
  const now = deps.now ?? (() => new Date());
  // The day's salt, read or set once a UTC day and kept as a promise, so the requests of a new day's first moment share
  // one SET NX. A failure forgets it, and the next request asks again.
  let salt: { day: string; value: Promise<Buffer> } | null = null;
  const daySalt = (day: string): Promise<Buffer> => {
    if (salt?.day === day) return salt.value;
    const value = (async () => {
      const key = sketchKeys.salt(day);
      await deps.store.set(key, randomBytes(32), "EX", SALT_SECONDS, "NX");
      const stored = await deps.store.getBuffer(key);
      if (stored === null || stored.length !== 32) throw new Error("the day's salt could not be read back");
      return stored;
    })();
    salt = { day, value };
    value.catch(() => {
      if (salt?.value === value) salt = null;
    });
    return value;
  };
  /** Adds one value to a sketch and gives the sketch its days to live from its first write. */
  const add = async (key: string, value: string) => {
    await deps.store.pfadd(key, value);
    await deps.store.expire(key, SKETCH_SECONDS, "NX");
  };
  const swallow = (err: unknown) => deps.log.debug({ err }, "recipients: a count was not recorded");
  return {
    seen(accountId) {
      try {
        add(sketchKeys.month(monthOf(now())), accountId).catch(swallow);
      } catch (err) {
        swallow(err);
      }
    },
    seenSignedOut(address, userAgent, path) {
      if (!deps.signedOut || !isReadRoute(path) || RECIPIENT_RULES.crawler.test(userAgent)) return;
      try {
        const day = dayOf(now());
        const agent = Buffer.from(userAgent, "utf8").subarray(0, RECIPIENT_RULES.userAgentBytes);
        const network = Buffer.from(clientNetwork(address), "utf8");
        daySalt(day)
          .then((key) => add(sketchKeys.day(day), createHmac("sha256", key).update(Buffer.concat([network, LF, agent])).digest("hex")))
          .catch(swallow);
      } catch (err) {
        swallow(err);
      }
    },
  };
}

/** The months before the current one that a close looks at: two, since a sketch lives 70 days. */
const CLOSE_MONTHS = 2;

/** The first day of the month `back` months before the instant's own, as yyyy-mm. */
function monthBefore(at: Date, back: number): string {
  return monthOf(new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), at.getUTCMonth() - back, 1)));
}

/** Every day of a month (yyyy-mm), as yyyy-mm-dd. */
function daysOf(month: string): string[] {
  const [year, monthNumber] = month.split("-").map(Number) as [number, number];
  const last = new Date(Date.UTC(year, monthNumber, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return Array.from({ length: last }, (_, at) => `${month}-${String(at + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`);
}

/**
 * The month's close (7.5 step 3): for each of the two months before the current one whose signed-in sketch exists and
 * that recipient_months does not hold yet, the sketch's count and, while the setting is on, the sum of its days' counts
 * are stored, and then the month's keys are deleted. A month without a sketch gets no row: it reads as not recorded.
 * Answers the months it stored.
 */
export async function closeMonths(deps: { store: SketchStore; repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "monthStored" | "storeMonth">; signedOut: boolean }, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
  const closed: string[] = [];
  for (let back = CLOSE_MONTHS; back >= 1; back--) {
    const month = monthBefore(at, back);
    const monthKey = sketchKeys.month(month);
    if ((await deps.store.exists(monthKey)) === 0) continue;
    const dayKeys = daysOf(month).map(sketchKeys.day);
    // A row stored by an earlier round that stopped before its delete: the keys go now, and the row stays as it was.
    if (!(await deps.repo.monthStored(month))) {
      const signedIn = await deps.store.pfcount(monthKey);
      let signedOutDays: number | null = null;
      if (deps.signedOut) {
        signedOutDays = 0;
        for (const key of dayKeys) signedOutDays += await deps.store.pfcount(key);
      }
      if (await deps.repo.storeMonth({ month, signedIn, signedOutDays, method: RECIPIENT_RULES.method })) closed.push(month);
    }
    // The row is stored: the sketches are no longer needed, and the days' salts died after their 26 hours.
    await deps.store.del(monthKey, ...dayKeys);
  }
  return closed;
}
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/repo.ts`

```ts
import { desc, eq, lt, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import type { EditionReason, TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { recipientMonths, transparencyEditions, type Db } from "@korbat/db";

/**
 * The transparency module's statements (3d design, sections 6.4, 7.5 and 7.6). It names the two tables of public record
 * and nothing of a person (the architecture test holds every file of the module to the names of schema/transparency.ts
 * and the audit head): the editions it reads and has edition_publish() write, and the months it reads and inserts.
 */

/** One stored version of a year's edition, as the public route reads it. */
export interface EditionRow {
  year: number;
  version: number;
  publishedAt: Date;
  method: number;
  reason: EditionReason;
  figures: TransparencyFigures;
}

/** One month of the recipients' count. */
export interface MonthRow {
  month: string;
  signedIn: number;
  signedOutDays: number | null;
  method: number;
}

/** How long a statement of the job waits for a lock: the job's other rounds are minutes away. */
const LOCK_TIMEOUT = sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`;

export function createTransparencyRepo(apiDb: Db) {
  return {
    /** Every stored version of every year, newest year first and, inside a year, newest version first. */
    async editions(): Promise<EditionRow[]> {
      const rows = await apiDb
        .select({
          year: transparencyEditions.year,
          version: transparencyEditions.version,
          publishedAt: transparencyEditions.publishedAt,
          method: transparencyEditions.method,
          reason: transparencyEditions.reason,
          figures: transparencyEditions.figures,
        })
        .from(transparencyEditions)
        .orderBy(desc(transparencyEditions.year), desc(transparencyEditions.version));
      return rows.map((row) => ({ ...row, reason: row.reason as EditionReason, figures: row.figures as TransparencyFigures }));
    },

    /** The years before `before` that have an edition: a hold that ends after its year closed still gives it a version. */
    async yearsWithEdition(before: number): Promise<number[]> {
      const rows = await apiDb
        .selectDistinct({ year: transparencyEditions.year })
        .from(transparencyEditions)
        .where(lt(transparencyEditions.year, before))
        .orderBy(desc(transparencyEditions.year));
      return rows.map((row) => row.year);
    },

    /**
     * edition_publish(year, 'first') in a transaction of its own, since its audit row holds the chain's head until the
     * commit: the version it wrote, or null when nothing was due or new. The function decides; the job only asks.
     */
    publish(year: number): Promise<number | null> {
      return apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(LOCK_TIMEOUT);
        const [row] = await tx.execute<{ version: number | null }>(sql`select public.edition_publish(${year}::int, 'first') as version`);
        return row?.version ?? null;
      });
    },

    /** Whether a month (yyyy-mm) is stored already. */
    async monthStored(month: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.select({ month: recipientMonths.month }).from(recipientMonths).where(eq(recipientMonths.month, `${month}-01`)).limit(1);
      return row !== undefined;
    },

    /** Stores a month's two numbers once; false when another round stored it first. computed_at is the database's. */
    async storeMonth(month: MonthRow): Promise<boolean> {
      // The API's role may insert these four columns and no other: the insert trigger forces computed_at.
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ month: string }>(sql`
        insert into public.recipient_months (month, signed_in, signed_out_days, method)
        values (${`${month.month}-01`}::date, ${month.signedIn}::int, ${month.signedOutDays}::int, ${month.method}::smallint)
        on conflict (month) do nothing returning month::text`);
      return rows.length > 0;
    },
  };
}

export type TransparencyRepo = ReturnType<typeof createTransparencyRepo>;
```

### Create `apps/api/src/transparency/routes.ts`

```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { PublicFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { publicTransparency } from "./editions";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The public answers (3d design, sections 9.1 and 10.6), mounted at /api after the global rate limit and before the
 * session's resolution (app.ts), as the page status is: neither reads a session, a cookie or a table of a person.
 *
 *   GET /api/public/facts         what is switched on now, read from memory, Cache-Control: no-cache, so /rules prints
 *                                 what runs now, also in the minute after a restart;
 *   GET /api/public/transparency  every year's editions from transparency_editions, Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600:
 *                                 nothing in it changes within a day.
 *
 * GET /api/public/head is Task 5's.
 */

/**
 * The facts of the running server (10.6): booleans, names, days and numbers, never a token, a zone, a host or an address.
 * The R1 check, the comparison with known material and the head's witness are built by later tasks and print off until
 * then; the edge prints its adapter (Task 3). A test adapter prints "on" and says it is one.
 */
export function publicFacts(config: Pick<Config, "EDGE_PURGE" | "RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT">): PublicFacts {
  return {
    r1: { state: "off", test: false, model: null, digest: null, threshold: null, thresholdVersion: null, publisherClaim: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
    match: { state: "off", test: false, source: null, dpia: null, dpiaActs: null },
    edge: { on: config.EDGE_PURGE !== "off", test: config.EDGE_PURGE === "test" },
    witness: { on: false, test: false },
    recipientsSignedOut: config.RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT === "on",
  };
}

export function transparencyRoutes(deps: { repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "editions">; facts: PublicFacts }) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  r.get("/public/facts", (c) => {
    c.header("Cache-Control", "no-cache");
    return c.json(deps.facts);
  });
  r.get("/public/transparency", async (c) => {
    const answer = publicTransparency(await deps.repo.editions());
    c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600");
    return c.json(answer);
  });
  return r;
}
```

### Create `apps/app/src/app/rules.tsx`

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { ScrollView, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { PublicFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { RULES, RULES_CHANGES, RULES_VERSION } from "@korbat/rules";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { TextLink } from "@/components/ui";
import { api } from "@/lib/api";
import { PAGE_DOWN, RULES_PAGE, toolBlocks, type AutomationLimits } from "@/lib/public-pages";
import { MEASURES_PARAGRAPH, REPORTING_IN_BAD_FAITH, STRIKES, SUSPENSION, TERRORIST_CONTENT, termsParagraphs } from "@/lib/terms";

/** A heading of the page: level 2 under the page's title, level 3 under a section. */
function Heading({ level, children }: { level: 2 | 3; children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text accessibilityRole="header" aria-level={level} className={level === 2 ? "mt-8 text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-100" : "mt-5 text-base font-semibold text-zinc-100"}>
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
const Paragraph = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => <Text className="mt-2 text-base leading-7 text-zinc-300">{children}</Text>;

/** One list of the page, its items read one by one. */
function List({ label, items }: { label: string; items: readonly string[] }) {
  return (
    <View role="list" aria-label={label} className="mt-1">
      {items.map((item) => (
        <Text key={item} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
          {`- ${item}`}
        </Text>
      ))}
    </View>
  );
}

/** The sections the terms build from STANDING_RULES and ORDER_RULES, which this page prints with the same builders. */
const NUMBERED_SECTIONS: { title: string; body: string }[] = [
  { title: "Strikes", body: STRIKES },
  { title: "Suspension and termination", body: SUSPENSION },
  { title: "Reporting in bad faith", body: REPORTING_IN_BAD_FAITH },
  { title: "Terrorist content", body: TERRORIST_CONTENT },
];

/**
 * The rules page as it reads with the facts it was given (3d design, section 9.2; W.1): the rules in force, what korbat
 * can do and when, what each automated tool does in the state the running server reports, and the change log. While the
 * facts are on their way the automation section holds its lead alone; when the route did not answer (`"down"`) the fixed
 * texts stand and it reads [page.down]: the page never prints a tool as off or on without the route's answer. `limits` are the program's caps, printed once a tool that rates or
 * compares images is on (their constant comes with the automated decision, Task 6).
 */
export function RulesView({ facts, limits = null }: { facts: PublicFacts | "loading" | "down"; limits?: AutomationLimits | null }) {
  const blocks = typeof facts === "string" ? [] : toolBlocks(facts);
  const anyImageTool = blocks.some((block) => (block.tool === "r1" || block.tool === "match") && block.on);
  return (
    <View>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-zinc-50">
        {RULES_PAGE.title}
      </Text>
      <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.lead}</Paragraph>

      <Heading level={2}>{RULES_PAGE.rulesHeading}</Heading>
      {RULES.map((rule) => (
        <View key={rule.id}>
          <Heading level={3}>{`${rule.id}: ${rule.title}`}</Heading>
          <Paragraph>{rule.text}</Paragraph>
          <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.allowed}</Paragraph>
          <List label={`${rule.id}: ${RULES_PAGE.allowed}`} items={rule.allowed} />
          <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.notAllowed}</Paragraph>
          <List label={`${rule.id}: ${RULES_PAGE.notAllowed}`} items={rule.notAllowed} />
        </View>
      ))}
      <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.law}</Paragraph>

      <Heading level={2}>{RULES_PAGE.measuresHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{MEASURES_PARAGRAPH}</Paragraph>
      {NUMBERED_SECTIONS.map((section) => (
        <View key={section.title}>
          <Heading level={3}>{section.title}</Heading>
          {termsParagraphs(section.body).map((paragraph, index) => (
            <Paragraph key={index}>{paragraph}</Paragraph>
          ))}
        </View>
      ))}

      <Heading level={2}>{RULES_PAGE.automationHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.autoLead}</Paragraph>
      {facts === "loading" ? null : facts === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View>
          {blocks.map((block) => (
            <View key={block.tool} role="group" className="mt-3 rounded-lg border border-zinc-800 px-3 pb-3">
              {block.paragraphs.map((paragraph, index) => (
                <Paragraph key={index}>{paragraph}</Paragraph>
              ))}
            </View>
          ))}
          {anyImageTool ? (
            limits === null ? null : (
              <>
                <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.autoCap(limits)}</Paragraph>
                <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.autoTarget(limits.objectionTargetHours)}</Paragraph>
              </>
            )
          ) : (
            <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.autoNone}</Paragraph>
          )}
        </View>
      )}

      <Heading level={2}>{RULES_PAGE.versionHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{RULES_PAGE.version(RULES_VERSION)}</Paragraph>
      {[...RULES_CHANGES].reverse().map((change) => (
        <Paragraph key={change.version}>{RULES_PAGE.change(change)}</Paragraph>
      ))}

      <TextLink label={RULES_PAGE.transparencyLink} href="/transparency" />
      <TextLink label={RULES_PAGE.exploreLink} href="/explore/about" />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * /rules (3d design, sections 9.1 and 9.2), public, signed in or out: it reads no session for its content and sends one
 * GET, /api/public/facts, which the API answers no-cache, so the page prints what is switched on now.
 */
export default function RulesPage() {
  const [facts, setFacts] = useState<PublicFacts | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    api("/api/public/facts", { schema: PublicFacts })
      .then((answer) => {
        if (live) setFacts(answer);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setFacts("down");
      });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);
  return (
    <AppShell>
      <ScrollView className="flex-1 bg-zinc-950" contentContainerClassName="px-4 pb-16 pt-6">
        <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
          <RulesView facts={facts} />
        </View>
      </ScrollView>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

### Create `apps/app/src/app/transparency.tsx`

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Pressable, ScrollView, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS, PublicTransparency, type OrderFigures, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { TextLink } from "@/components/ui";
import { api } from "@/lib/api";
import { PAGE_DOWN, TRANSPARENCY_PAGE, recipientsMonth } from "@/lib/public-pages";

const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;
type Edition = PublicTransparency["editions"][number];
type Row = { label: string; count: string };

/** A heading of the page: level 2 a year or a fixed section, level 3 a table inside a year. */
function Heading({ level, children }: { level: 2 | 3; children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text accessibilityRole="header" aria-level={level} className={level === 2 ? "mt-8 text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-100" : "mt-5 text-base font-semibold text-zinc-100"}>
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
const Paragraph = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => <Text className="mt-2 text-base leading-7 text-zinc-300">{children}</Text>;

/**
 * One table: its heading and its rows, each read as "label: value" and laid out as a block, never a chart (9.1); a table
 * with no row is its "none" sentence.
 */
function Table({ title, rows }: { title: string; rows: Row[] }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{title}</Heading>
      {rows.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.tableNone}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View role="list" aria-label={title}>
          {rows.map((row) => (
            <Text key={row.label} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
              {`${row.label}: ${row.count}`}
            </Text>
          ))}
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** A table's stored rows with the page's labels: `other` by the table's own word. */
const labelled = (rows: readonly { label: string; count: string }[], label: (key: string) => string, other: string): Row[] =>
  rows.map((row) => ({ label: row.label === "other" ? other : label(row.label), count: row.count }));

/** An order figure as the page prints it: a number, or "not recorded", never 0, for a figure the rows can no longer give. */
const figure = (n: number | null) => (n === null ? T.notRecorded : String(n));
const byGround = (grounds: readonly string[], counts: Record<string, number> | null) =>
  counts === null ? T.notRecorded : grounds.map((ground) => `${T.grounds[ground] ?? ground} ${counts[ground]}`).join(", ");

/**
 * The section on authorities' orders (9.3 item 4): [tr.orders], then the yearly report's headings with tco-counts'
 * figures as numbers, without the issuing state. It stands only in a year that has the section.
 */
function OrdersSection({ orders }: { orders: OrderFigures }) {
  const L = T.orderLines;
  const minutes = orders.minutes;
  const minutesList = minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : minutes.list.length === 0 ? "none" : minutes.list.map((n) => figure(n)).join(", ");
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.ordersHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.orders}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.received}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.received === null ? L.received(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.received(String(orders.received.total), String(orders.received.crossBorder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.disabled}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.itemsDisabled(figure(orders.itemsDisabled))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.minutes(minutesList)}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.late}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.outside(minutes === null || minutes.withoutReceipt > 0 ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.outside))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.open(minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.open))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.annex3(byGround(ANNEX3_GROUNDS, orders.annex3))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.scrutiny}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.scrutiny === null ? L.scrutiny(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.scrutiny(String(orders.scrutiny.requested), String(orders.scrutiny.annulled), String(orders.scrutiny.upheld))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.reinstated(byGround(ORDER_GROUNDS, orders.reinstated))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.own}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.terrorist(String(orders.terroristWithoutOrder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.access(figure(orders.authorityAccess))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.referrals(String(orders.referralsClosed))}</Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** The tables of one version's figures, in W.2's order, then the order section, the standing sentence and the recipients. */
export function FiguresView({ year, figures }: { year: number; figures: TransparencyFigures }) {
  const r = figures.restrictions;
  const findings = labelled(figures.automated.findings, T.labels.findings, T.labels.other);
  const programs = [...findings, ...labelled(figures.automated.measures, T.labels.measures, T.labels.other)];
  const month = recipientsMonth(year);
  const recipients = figures.recipients;
  return (
    <View>
      <Table
        title={T.tables.byGround}
        rows={r.byGround.length === 0 ? [] : [...labelled(r.byGround, (key) => (key === "law" ? T.labels.law : T.labels.ground(key)), T.labels.otherGrounds), { label: T.labels.allRestrictions, count: r.total }]}
      />
      <Table title={T.tables.byMeasure} rows={labelled(r.byMeasure, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.noBreach} rows={[{ label: T.labels.noBreach, count: figures.noBreach }]} />
      <Table title={T.tables.intakes} rows={labelled(figures.intakes, (key) => T.labels.intakes[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.appeals} rows={labelled(figures.appeals, (key) => T.labels.appeals[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.reexaminations} rows={labelled(figures.reexaminations, (key) => T.labels.reexaminations[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.accountMeasures} rows={labelled(figures.accountMeasures, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.automated} rows={programs} />
      {figures.automated.r1 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoRate(figures.automated.r1.base, figures.automated.r1.restricted)}</Paragraph> : findings.length > 0 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoFew}</Paragraph> : null}
      {figures.uploads ? <Table title={T.tables.uploads} rows={labelled(figures.uploads, (key) => T.labels.uploads[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} /> : null}
      {figures.orders ? <OrdersSection orders={figures.orders} /> : null}
      <Paragraph>{T.ordersHeld}</Paragraph>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.recipientsHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        {recipients === "not recorded" ? T.recipientsNotYet : recipients.high === undefined ? T.recipientsOff(month, recipients.low) : T.recipients(month, recipients.low, recipients.high)}
      </Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** An older version of a year: its line, and its figures opened in place. */
function OlderVersion({ year, older }: { year: number; older: Edition["older"][number] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <View>
      <Paragraph>{T.versionLine(older.version, older.publishedOn, older.replacedOn)}</Paragraph>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => setOpen(!open)} className="mt-1 self-start">
        <Text className="text-sm text-sky-400 underline">{open ? T.hideVersion : T.showVersion}</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <FiguresView year={year} figures={older.figures} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/** One year's section (9.3 item 2): its newest version, why that version was made, and its older versions. */
function EditionView({ edition, newest }: { edition: Edition; newest: boolean }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={2}>{String(edition.year)}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.edition(edition.year, edition.version, edition.publishedOn, edition.method)}</Paragraph>
      {edition.reason === "hold_ended" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.hold_ended}</Paragraph> : null}
      {edition.reason === "correction" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.correction(edition.publishedOn)}</Paragraph> : null}
      <FiguresView year={edition.year} figures={edition.figures} />
      {edition.older.length > 0 ? (
        <View>
          <Paragraph>{T.versions}</Paragraph>
          {edition.older.map((older) => (
            <OlderVersion key={older.version} year={edition.year} older={older} />
          ))}
        </View>
      ) : null}
      {newest ? <Paragraph>{T.method(edition.method)}</Paragraph> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * The transparency page as it reads with the editions it was given (3d design, section 9.3, without the audit head's
 * section, which is Task 5's; W.2). It shows what the stored editions hold and never a live count: no year section for
 * the running year, and [tr.none] while no edition exists. When the route did not answer, the fixed texts stand and the
 * editions' place reads [page.down].
 */
export function TransparencyView({ answer }: { answer: PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down" }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-zinc-50">
        {T.title}
      </Text>
      <Paragraph>{T.lead}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.read}</Paragraph>
      {answer === "loading" ? null : answer === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : answer.editions.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.none}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        answer.editions.map((edition, index) => <EditionView key={edition.year} edition={edition} newest={index === 0} />)
      )}
      <Heading level={2}>{T.tdbHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.tdb}</Paragraph>
      <TextLink label={T.rulesLink} href="/rules" />
      <TextLink label={T.exploreLink} href="/explore/about" />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * /transparency (3d design, sections 9.1 and 9.3), public, signed in or out: it reads no session for its content and
 * sends one GET, /api/public/transparency, which may be an hour old: nothing in it changes within a day.
 */
export default function TransparencyPage() {
  const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    api("/api/public/transparency", { schema: PublicTransparency })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setAnswer(read);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setAnswer("down");
      });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);
  return (
    <AppShell>
      <ScrollView className="flex-1 bg-zinc-950" contentContainerClassName="px-4 pb-16 pt-6">
        <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
          <TransparencyView answer={answer} />
        </View>
      </ScrollView>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

import { EDGE_CACHE, EDGE_WORDS, MEASURES, RECIPIENT_RULES, TRANSPARENCY_RULES, type MeasureKind, type PublicFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { RULES } from "@korbat/rules";
import { numberWord } from "./moderation-words";

/**
 * The fixed texts of the two public pages (3d design, sections 9.1 to 9.3 and 18, W.1 and W.2; Task 4): the rules page's
 * (RULES_PAGE), what it says of each tool in each state (TOOL_TEXTS), and the transparency page's (TRANSPARENCY_PAGE).
 * Every number is printed from its constant. The words hold the design's nine rules for every text of 3d: a public page
 * points at no person, says no more of a tool than is true in every state the design builds, and names the order
 * section as the one place a figure is a number.
 */

/** [page.down], in place of the part a page could not fetch: the fixed texts stand, and nothing says a tool is on or off. */
export const PAGE_DOWN = "korbat could not load this part right now. Try again in a minute.";

/** A count of minutes as a sentence prints it. */
const minutes = (n: number) => `${n} ${n === 1 ? "minute" : "minutes"}`;

/** The numbers the rules page prints in its automation section once a tool that rates or compares images is on. */
export interface AutomationLimits {
  decisionsPerHour: number;
  decisionsPerDay: number;
  r2DecisionsPerHour: number;
  r2DecisionsPerDay: number;
  unansweredMax: number;
  unansweredHours: number;
  refusalsPerHour: number;
  objectionTargetHours: number;
}

/** The rules page's words (W.1). */
export const RULES_PAGE = {
  title: "The rules",
  lead: "These are all of korbat's rules. korbat restricts content when it breaks one of them, or when it is illegal under EU law or the law of an EU country and korbat is told about it in a notice. Opinions are never a reason. Every decision names one of these rules or the law, and its statement shows the rule as it read on the day of the decision.",
  rulesHeading: "The rules",
  allowed: "Allowed",
  notAllowed: "Not allowed",
  law: "Illegal content. Anyone can tell korbat that something on it is illegal (Report). An authority or a court can order korbat to act (Terms, Authorities' orders). korbat cannot restrict for one country alone, so a restriction for illegality applies everywhere korbat is available.",
  measuresHeading: "What korbat can do, and when",
  automationHeading: "Automation",
  autoLead: `korbat's moderators are people. A program may do the few things listed here and nothing else. It never removes anything, never judges text, and never suspends or restricts an account. What a program does to a post lasts only until a person decides; the person a measure concerns is told at once, and can put it before a person with "Ask for a person". An upload that a program does not accept stays not accepted: a person decides what happens to the held file, and nobody at korbat can accept it, since nobody opens it. This list is printed by the running server: it says what is switched on today.`,

It takes no new measure under a rule while ${l.unansweredMax} of its measures under that rule wait for a person, and none under either rule while a request for a person has waited longer than ${l.unansweredHours} hours. It refuses at most ${l.refusalsPerHour} uploads an hour. Over a limit it only reports to korbat's staff.`,
  autoTarget: (hours: number) => `When you ask for a person, korbat's target is an answer within ${hours} hours. It is a target that korbat publishes, not a time after which a measure ends.`,

} as const;

/** What the facts route says of the R1 check's model, printed under its text while it is on. */
type R1Facts = Pick<PublicFacts["r1"], "model" | "digest" | "threshold" | "thresholdVersion" | "publisherClaim">;

/** The text of match.alerts, up to and with the sentence after which match.seals goes its own way (W.1). */
const matchAlerts = (source: string) =>
  `Comparing uploads with known child sexual abuse material: on, with ${source}. korbat computes fingerprints of every uploaded image, keeps them with the image, and sends them, and nothing else, to ${source}: never the image, an address or an account. Only a match that ${source} reports as exact, with an entry it classifies as child sexual abuse material, lets a program refuse or seal. Such an upload is not accepted, now or later, and is held unseen until an admin has decided what happens to the file.`;

/**
 * TOOL_TEXTS (W.1): one text a tool and state. `{source}` and the model's facts come from the facts route; the edge's

export const TOOL_TEXTS = {

    flags:
      "Rating images against rule R1: on. A program rates every uploaded image and korbat keeps the rating with the image. An image it rates at or above the threshold is put before a moderator, who decides. The program hides nothing, and the image's author hears of it only if the moderator's decision restricts the post.",
    withholds:
      "Rating images against rule R1: on. A program rates every uploaded image and korbat keeps the rating with the image. The post's text stays, and its author still sees the image, is told at once and can ask for a person.",
    facts: (f: R1Facts) =>
      `The model: ${f.model}. SHA-256 of its weights: ${f.digest}. Threshold: ${f.threshold}, version ${f.thresholdVersion}. Its publisher states: "${f.publisherClaim}". korbat has not measured its error rate and claims none. The publisher does not disclose the training data, and korbat found no outside evaluation of bias. A rating says nothing about rule R2.`,
  },
  match: {
    off: "Comparing uploads with known child sexual abuse material: off. korbat computes no fingerprint of any upload, compares nothing, and keeps no fingerprint from a time when it did, except the one in the record of a match (Terms, Your data).     alerts: (source: string) =>
      `${matchAlerts(source)} A match with such an entry, exact or not, on an image that is already on a post is put before an admin at once; the program seals nothing, and from then on korbat keeps that post's images, also if their author deletes the post or the account, until the admin has answered. A match with an entry of any other class only flags the image for a person: no upload is refused and no image is held, sealed or kept because of it. korbat's staff do not open an image that a match names.`,
    seals: (source: string) =>
      `${matchAlerts(source)} When an image that is already on a post matches in that way, korbat seals that post's images at once, for everyone, until an admin has answered; it keeps them until then, also if their author deletes the post or the account. The author is told at once and can ask for a person. A match with such an entry that ${source} does not report as exact is put before an admin at once too: the program seals nothing on it, and korbat keeps that post's images until the admin has answered. A match with an entry of any other class only flags the image for a person: no upload is refused and no image is held, sealed or kept because of it. korbat's staff do not open an image that a match names, before the admin's answer or after it, and the admin's answer is a person's decision.`,
  },
  edge: {
    off: `Dropping cached copies: off. When an image stops being public, a copy at korbat's network provider can be served for up to ${minutes(EDGE_WORDS.edgeMinutes)}, and a copy in a browser for up to ${minutes(EDGE_CACHE.browserSeconds / 60)}.`,
    on: `Dropping cached copies: on. When an image stops being public, korbat asks its network provider to drop its copy at once. The request can fail, so the bound korbat states is the same: up to ${minutes(EDGE_WORDS.edgeMinutes)} at the provider, up to ${minutes(EDGE_CACHE.browserSeconds / 60)} in a browser.`,
  },
  witness: {
    off: "Outside timestamp for the audit log's daily value: off. The value stands on korbat's Transparency page and in a mail to a person who does not run the server.",
    on: "Outside timestamp for the audit log's daily value: on. The Transparency page offers each day's proof and says how to check it.",
  },
} as const;

/** "(test adapter)" after a tool's "on": a test adapter can run only while the app's site is closed (W.1). */
const testAdapter = (text: string) => text.replace(": on", ": on (test adapter)");

/** One tool's block on the rules page, as the facts give it: its paragraphs, in order. */
export interface ToolBlock {
  tool: "r1" | "match" | "edge" | "witness";
  on: boolean;
  paragraphs: string[];
}

/**
 * The automation section's four blocks, in the state the facts route gives each tool (9.2 item 4): a tool's text, its
 * model's facts while the R1 check is on, and inside the block of each of the two tools that rate or compare images,
 * while it is on, its own impact assessment's day and, while its measure is on, the day of the one that covers it. A date
 * is never printed over a tool it was not set for.
 */
export function toolBlocks(facts: PublicFacts): ToolBlock[] {
  const dates = (tool: { dpia: string | null; dpiaActs: string | null }, acts: boolean) => [
    ...(tool.dpia === null ? [] : [RULES_PAGE.dpia(tool.dpia)]),
    ...(acts && tool.dpiaActs !== null ? [RULES_PAGE.dpiaActs(tool.dpiaActs)] : []),
  ];
  const marked = (text: string, test: boolean) => (test ? testAdapter(text) : text);
  const { r1, match, edge, witness } = facts;
  const r1On = r1.state !== "off";
  const matchOn = match.state !== "off";
  const source = match.source ?? "its source";
  return [
    {
      tool: "r1",
      on: r1On,
      paragraphs: r1On
        ? [marked(TOOL_TEXTS.r1[r1.state === "withholds" ? "withholds" : "flags"], r1.test), ...(r1.model === null ? [] : [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.facts(r1)]), ...dates(r1, r1.state === "withholds")]
        : [TOOL_TEXTS.r1.off],
    },
    {
      tool: "match",
      on: matchOn,
      paragraphs: matchOn ? [marked(match.state === "seals" ? TOOL_TEXTS.match.seals(source) : TOOL_TEXTS.match.alerts(source), match.test), ...dates(match, match.state === "seals")] : [TOOL_TEXTS.match.off],
    },
    { tool: "edge", on: edge.on, paragraphs: [edge.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.edge.on, edge.test) : TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off] },
    { tool: "witness", on: witness.on, paragraphs: [witness.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.witness.on, witness.test) : TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off] },
  ];
}

/** The six full months before an edition's due day end with this month (yyyy-mm), the same in every version of the year. */
export function recipientsMonth(year: number): string {
  return new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1, 0)).toISOString().slice(0, 7);
}

const MONTHS = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"];
/** The day a year's edition is due, as a sentence names it: 1 March, from TRANSPARENCY_RULES. */
const DUE = `${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay} ${MONTHS[TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1]}`;
/** The floor and the rounding of a banded count, as a sentence names them. */
const FLOOR = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor);
const UNDER_FLOOR = `1 to ${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor - 1}`;
const ROUND_TO = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.roundTo);

/** The labels of a measure in the tables: the ledger's own. */
const measureLabel = (kind: string) => (kind in MEASURES ? MEASURES[kind as MeasureKind].label : kind);
/** A rule's title in force, for the table by ground. */
const ruleTitle = (id: string) => RULES.find((rule) => rule.id === id)?.title ?? id;

    `Average monthly active recipients of korbat (Article 24(2) of the Digital Services Act), over the six months to ${month}: at least ${low}; korbat does not count readers without an account.`,
  recipientsNotYet: "korbat has not counted six full months yet.",
  method: (method: number) =>
    `How korbat counts (method ${method}). An account that was used while signed in during a month is counted once for that month. A reader without an account is counted once for each day they read korbat: korbat cannot tell whether Tuesday's reader is Monday's, because it keeps nothing that could tell. So the true number lies between the first figure, accounts alone, and the second, accounts plus the sum of each day's readers. To count, korbat feeds a counting sketch: a small summary that cannot list who was counted. For a reader without an account it is fed with a keyed digest of the network address and the browser's name, under a random key that exists for ${RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours} hours in korbat's short-lived store and is written nowhere else. Until a month's sketch is deleted at the month's end, whoever runs korbat's server could still ask it whether one given account was probably counted in that month; after that korbat keeps two numbers and nothing else. A crawler is left out only when it names itself. korbat does not record where a reader is, so readers outside the European Union are counted too.`,
  tdbHeading: "The Transparency Database",
  tdb: "korbat does not send its statements of reasons to the European Commission's DSA Transparency Database. That duty (Article 24(5) of the Digital Services Act) does not apply to micro and small enterprises (Article 19(1)), which korbat is, and a statement sent there cannot be taken back. Should korbat outgrow the exemption, this page will say from which day it sends them.",
  rulesLink: "The rules",
  exploreLink: "How Explore works",
} as const;

### Create `packages/contracts/src/transparency.ts`

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { MEASURE_KINDS, RULE_IDS } from "./moderation";
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS } from "./orders";

// The public figures (3d design, sections 2 rows 1 to 3 and 8, 6.4, 7.5, 7.6, 10.1 and 10.6; Task 4). This module
// imports moderation.ts and orders.ts for closed lists alone, and nothing imports it but the index, so it loads last.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the numbers

/**
 * The mirror of the SQL function transparency_rules(), which a database test holds member for column: the floor under
 * which a count prints as "1 to 9" and a row is folded into "other", the rounding of every other count, the day on which
 * a year's edition is due (1 March of the next year, in UTC) and the method's version. Each is the owner's to change
 * (section 2, rows 2 and 3), in that function and here.
 */
export const TRANSPARENCY_RULES = {
  floor: 10,
  roundTo: 10,
  dueMonth: 3,
  dueDay: 1,
  method: 1,
} as const;

/**
 * A count as the public reads it, exactly as the SQL function band() prints it (a table test holds the two equal over 0
 * to 200): 0 for zero, "1 to 9" under the floor, otherwise "about" and the count rounded to the nearest ten, halves
 * upward. It is the only place a count becomes public text.
 */
export function band(n: number): string {
  if (!Number.isInteger(n) || n < 0) throw new Error(`band takes a count, not ${n}`);
  if (n === 0) return "0";
  if (n < TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor) return "1 to 9";
  const step = TRANSPARENCY_RULES.roundTo;
  return `about ${Math.floor((n + step / 2) / step) * step}`;
}

/**
 * The recipients' count (7.5), method 1: a month's sketch of signed-in accounts and a day's sketch of signed-out readers,
 * the day's salt living `saltHours`, every sketch dying `sketchDays` after its first write if the month's close never
 * took it, the user agent cut at `userAgentBytes` before it is digested, and the figure the average of `months` full
 * months. A crawler is left out only by its own words: one pattern on the agent, nothing guessed about a reader.
 */
export const RECIPIENT_RULES = {
  method: 1,
  months: 6,
  saltHours: 26,
  sketchDays: 70,
  userAgentBytes: 256,
  crawler: /bot|crawl|spider|slurp/i,
} as const;

/**
 * The seven routes of the social module that answer without a session (7.5): a post, its thread, the two public
 * timelines, a profile, its posts and its replies. A signed-out GET of one of them feeds the day's sketch. The image
 * route and the page status are not counted. A route-table test fails when the social module gains a signed-out read
 * that is neither here nor refused by name in that test.
 */
export const RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES = [
  "GET /api/posts/:id",
  "GET /api/posts/:id/thread",
  "GET /api/timeline/latest",
  "GET /api/timeline/explore",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle/posts",
  "GET /api/profiles/:handle/replies",
] as const;

/** Why a version of a year's edition was stored (the CHECK of transparency_editions.reason): version 1 alone is `first`. */
export const EDITION_REASONS = ["first", "hold_ended", "correction"] as const;
export type EditionReason = (typeof EDITION_REASONS)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the public answers

/** A banded count, as band() prints it: never a number under ten, never an exact one. */
const Band = z.string().regex(/^(0|1 to 9|about [1-9][0-9]*0)$/);
/** A day, as the public pages print one: 2026-03-01. */
const Day = z.string().regex(/^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$/);

/** One row of a table split by a label from a closed list: what is folded under the floor is the row `other`. */
const rows = <const L extends readonly [string, ...string[]]>(labels: L) => z.array(z.strictObject({ label: z.enum([...labels, "other"]), count: Band }));

/**
 * The labels of each table (6.4): a rule's id or `law` for the ground; a measure's kind; an intake's kind, a user's
 * report under the rules and a notice of illegality apart; an appeal's result; a re-examination's answer; one of 3e's six
 * account measures; an upload's end (from Task 7).
 */
export const FIGURE_LABELS = {
  grounds: [...RULE_IDS, "law"],
  measures: MEASURE_KINDS,
  intakes: ["rules", "illegal", "finding", "automated"],
  appeals: ["kept", "partly_reversed", "reversed"],
  reexaminations: ["action", "no_action"],
  accountMeasures: ["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"],
} as const;

/**
 * The order section (6.4 step 5): the figures F 7.18 lists for tco-counts, as numbers and without the issuing state,
 * since the Regulation asks for numbers (section 2, row 4). A figure the rows can no longer give is null, which the page
 * prints as "not recorded", as tco-counts does, and never as 0.
 */
export const OrderFigures = z.strictObject({
  received: z.strictObject({ total: z.number().int().min(0), crossBorder: z.number().int().min(0) }).nullable(),
  itemsDisabled: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  minutes: z
    .strictObject({
      list: z.array(z.number().int().nullable()),
      outside: z.number().int().min(0),
      withoutReceipt: z.number().int().min(0),
      open: z.number().int().min(0),
    })
    .nullable(),
  annex3: z.strictObject(Object.fromEntries(ANNEX3_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, z.number().int().min(0)])) as Record<(typeof ANNEX3_GROUNDS)[number], z.ZodNumber>).nullable(),
  scrutiny: z.strictObject({ requested: z.number().int().min(0), annulled: z.number().int().min(0), upheld: z.number().int().min(0) }).nullable(),
  reinstated: z.strictObject(Object.fromEntries(ORDER_GROUNDS.map((ground) => [ground, z.number().int().min(0)])) as Record<(typeof ORDER_GROUNDS)[number], z.ZodNumber>).nullable(),
  authorityAccess: z.number().int().min(0).nullable(),
  terroristWithoutOrder: z.number().int().min(0),
  referralsClosed: z.number().int().min(0),
});
export type OrderFigures = z.infer<typeof OrderFigures>;

/**
 * A stored edition's figures, as transparency_figures() computes them (6.4): banded strings only, but the order section's
 * numbers. `uploads` comes with Task 7 and stays optional for good: an edition stored before it never changes, so it
 * never gains the member. `orders` is absent when no countable order exists, and nothing says whether one was left out.
 * `recipients` is two bounds, one while signed-out readers are not counted, or "not recorded" before six months are.
 */
export const TransparencyFigures = z.strictObject({
  restrictions: z.strictObject({ byGround: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.grounds), byMeasure: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.measures), total: Band }),
  noBreach: Band,
  intakes: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.intakes),
  appeals: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.appeals),
  reexaminations: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.reexaminations),
  accountMeasures: rows(FIGURE_LABELS.accountMeasures),
  automated: z.strictObject({
    findings: rows(RULE_IDS),
    measures: rows(RULE_IDS),
    /** Of the findings under R1, how many a person's final decision had restricted by the due day: only on a base of ten or more. */
    r1: z.strictObject({ base: Band, restricted: Band }).optional(),
  }),
  uploads: rows(["refused", "report", "no_report", "open"]).optional(),
  orders: OrderFigures.optional(),
  recipients: z.union([z.literal("not recorded"), z.strictObject({ low: Band, high: Band.optional() })]),
});
export type TransparencyFigures = z.infer<typeof TransparencyFigures>;

/** One stored version of a year's edition, as GET /api/public/transparency answers it. */
const EditionVersion = z.strictObject({
  version: z.number().int().min(1),
  publishedOn: Day,
  /** The day the next version was published, which replaced this one. */
  replacedOn: Day,
  reason: z.enum(EDITION_REASONS),
  figures: TransparencyFigures,
});

/**
 * GET /api/public/transparency (10.6): every year's newest version, newest year first, with its older versions. It reads
 * transparency_editions alone (the recipients' bounds are inside the figures) and nothing of a person.
 */
export const PublicTransparency = z.strictObject({
  editions: z.array(
    z.strictObject({
      year: z.number().int(),
      version: z.number().int().min(1),
      publishedOn: Day,
      method: z.number().int(),
      reason: z.enum(EDITION_REASONS),
      figures: TransparencyFigures,
      older: z.array(EditionVersion),
    }),
  ),
});
export type PublicTransparency = z.infer<typeof PublicTransparency>;

/**
 * GET /api/public/facts (10.6): what is switched on now, read from the API's settings: booleans, names, days and numbers,
 * never a token, a zone, a host or an address. Until the tasks that build them, the R1 check, the comparison with known
 * material and the head's witness print off; the edge prints its adapter (Task 3). `dpia` and `dpiaActs` are each a
 * tool's own impact assessment and the one that covers its measure, so no date of one tool stands over another.
 */
export const PublicFacts = z.strictObject({
  r1: z.strictObject({
    state: z.enum(["off", "flags", "withholds"]),
    test: z.boolean(),
    model: z.string().nullable(),
    digest: z.string().nullable(),
    threshold: z.number().nullable(),
    thresholdVersion: z.number().int().nullable(),
    publisherClaim: z.string().nullable(),
    dpia: Day.nullable(),
    dpiaActs: Day.nullable(),
  }),
  match: z.strictObject({
    state: z.enum(["off", "alerts", "seals"]),
    test: z.boolean(),
    source: z.string().nullable(),
    dpia: Day.nullable(),
    dpiaActs: Day.nullable(),
  }),
  edge: z.strictObject({ on: z.boolean(), test: z.boolean() }),
  witness: z.strictObject({ on: z.boolean(), test: z.boolean() }),
  /** Whether signed-out readers are counted (RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT). */
  recipientsSignedOut: z.boolean(),
});
export type PublicFacts = z.infer<typeof PublicFacts>;
```

-- a row is folded into "other", the rounding of every other count, the due day of a year's edition (1 March of the next
-- year, in UTC) and the method's version. Each is the owner's (section 2, rows 2 and 3).
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_rules"() RETURNS TABLE (floor integer, round_to integer, due_month integer, due_day integer, method integer)
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT 10, 10, 3, 1, 1
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 5. band(n): the only place a count becomes public text (section 2, row 3): 0 for zero; "1 to 9" under the floor;
-- otherwise "about" and the count rounded to the nearest round_to, halves upward. The contracts' band() prints the same,
-- which a table test over 0 to 200 holds. A negative count is no count: null.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."band"(n bigint) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN band.n IS NULL OR band.n < 0 THEN NULL
           WHEN band.n = 0 THEN '0'
           WHEN band.n < r.floor THEN '1 to ' || (r.floor - 1)::text
           ELSE 'about ' || ((band.n + r.round_to / 2) / r.round_to * r.round_to)::text
         END
    FROM public.transparency_rules() r
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 6. transparency_fold(counted): one table of an edition from its exact counts, given as a JSON array of
-- {label, n} in the order the table prints them. A row of zero is dropped; a row under the floor is folded into the
-- row "other", printed last with its own band; every other row keeps its label and is banded. So the printed rows do
-- not give the printed total, and no folded cell can be subtracted back (LAB E4). Nobody but the definer functions below
-- calls it.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_fold"(counted jsonb) RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH r AS (SELECT t.floor FROM public.transparency_rules() t),
  given AS (SELECT e.value->>'label' AS label, (e.value->>'n')::bigint AS n, e.ordinality AS at
              FROM jsonb_array_elements(coalesce(transparency_fold.counted, '[]'::jsonb)) WITH ORDINALITY e
             WHERE (e.value->>'n')::bigint > 0),
  folded AS (SELECT sum(g.n)::bigint AS n FROM given g, r WHERE g.n < r.floor)
  SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(x.line ORDER BY x.at), '[]'::jsonb)
    FROM (SELECT jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'count', public.band(g.n)) AS line, g.at FROM given g, r WHERE g.n >= r.floor
          UNION ALL
          SELECT jsonb_build_object('label', 'other', 'count', public.band(f.n)), 9223372036854775807 FROM folded f WHERE f.n IS NOT NULL) x
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 7. transparency_order_held(order, as_of): whether an order is left out of the public figures at an instant (section 2,
-- row 5; 6.4 step 5): one of its decisions was untold then (taken by then, and not told by then) and its hold, as
-- order_hold_until() reads it now, lies after that instant. Read at the present it is "untold now and held now"; read at
-- an older version's own instant it says which orders that version left out, from the same rows by the same times, so an
-- order received in the year and disabled or told later is not lost between the section and the test of its new version.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_order_held"(order_id uuid, as_of timestamptz) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.decisions d JOIN public.legal_order_items i ON i.id = d.order_item_id
                  WHERE i.order_id = transparency_order_held.order_id
                    AND d.decided_at <= transparency_order_held.as_of
                    AND (d.informed_at IS NULL OR d.informed_at > transparency_order_held.as_of))
     AND coalesce(public.order_hold_until(transparency_order_held.order_id) > transparency_order_held.as_of, false)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 8. transparency_order_ids(year, as_of): the removal orders the order section of a year counts at an instant: recorded
-- by then, not held then, and with a row of the year that a figure counts (received in it, or without a receipt opened
-- in it; an item disabled in it; an Annex III, a scrutiny or a reinstatement that took effect in it; an authority's
-- access to its preserved content opened in it). The section is printed when this is not empty, and a year gains a
-- version hold_ended when it names an order that it did not name at the newest version's own instant.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_order_ids"(year integer, as_of timestamptz) RETURNS SETOF uuid
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH y AS (SELECT make_timestamptz(transparency_order_ids.year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC') AS f, make_timestamptz(transparency_order_ids.year + 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC') AS t)
  SELECT o.id FROM public.legal_orders o, y
   WHERE o.kind::text = 'tco_removal' AND o.opened_at <= transparency_order_ids.as_of
     AND NOT public.transparency_order_held(o.id, transparency_order_ids.as_of)
     AND ((coalesce(o.received_at, o.opened_at) >= y.f AND coalesce(o.received_at, o.opened_at) < y.t)
          OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_items t WHERE t.order_id = o.id AND t.disabled_at >= y.f AND t.disabled_at < y.t)
          OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.legal_order_events e
                      WHERE e.order_id = o.id AND e.kind::text IN ('annex3_sent', 'scrutiny_requested', 'scrutiny_decided', 'reinstated')
                        AND coalesce(e.effective_at, e.at) >= y.f AND coalesce(e.effective_at, e.at) < y.t)
          OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.productions p
                      WHERE p.order_id = o.id AND p.instrument = 'preserved_access' AND p.purpose::text = 'authority' AND p.opened_at >= y.f AND p.opened_at < y.t))
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
