A figure it can no longer give, because the retention job erased the rows it rests on or nobody recorded a receipt, prints "not recorded", never a zero, and the edition prints it the same way. The one heading of the report the server cannot count, complaints and court proceedings, stays the operator's, from their own notes, for the authority that asks. Then the state's own filing, where `STATE_FACTS` names one.

````markdown
## Quarantine

The files of images sealed for good leave the image store: the one-shot service `quarantine` moves them into the volume `media-quarantine`, which neither the API nor the image worker mounts, and back when a seal for good is lifted (sub-project 3d). A seal taken while deciding leaves its files in the store. Nothing moves a file by itself: the home screen's line "Files to move or return" and the daily alert "Sealed files are waiting to be moved" say when the steps below are due, after every seal for good, after every lifted seal for good, and after every release.

1. `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js quarantine-list > list`. Read the line it prints beside it: how many files move in, return, are destroyed, are for the operator. A post it leaves out is named there; the other posts' lines stand.
2. `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt`. It copies, compares digests, renames and only then removes; a `destroy` line takes the digest first and removes the file in the quarantine and, where the store holds one of the same name, there too. One bad line never stops it: it prints the line, goes on, and exits 1 at the end. If it is cut short, run steps 1 and 2 again: a file is never in neither place.
3. `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js quarantine-record < receipt`, then delete `list` and `receipt`: they name files. The record takes each line by itself and never refuses the others. A line that no longer fits the plan (a seal was lifted, or taken again, between the list and the move) is recorded where the file now is and printed, and the next list moves it back: run steps 1 to 3 again.
4. Nobody opens a file of the quarantine, on the server or off it. The volume is on the encrypted disk and is in no backup: a lost disk loses the sealed files, and no backup can bring a destroyed file back. Its owner and mode (uid 1000, mode 0700) come from the path `/media/quarantine` that the API's image creates; check them once after the first run, from inside the service: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm --entrypoint stat quarantine -c '%u %a' /media/quarantine` prints `1000 700`.
5. **A file in neither place** (`missing` on the receipt). Nothing is recorded for it yet, and the daily alert goes on. Look for it first: the disk, a run that was cut short, another volume. Only if it is gone, run step 2 again with `--lost` appended, then step 3: the file is recorded as lost and every staff account is alerted. An image whose seal was lifted then reads "korbat lost this image" for its author, who is mailed once. If the file was kept for an authority, tell the authority, and note it.
6. **A file without a record** (a receipt that was lost before step 3, or a restore). `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine --inventory > have`, then step 3 with `have`: every file the quarantine holds has its record again, and the next list returns it, destroys it, or prints it for the operator.

### A release

An authority's assessment is not leave to destroy. Record it as Authorities' orders says (`notification-answer --answer illegal`): it releases nothing, and it is a reason the authority may want the files kept. If the authority asks for the files, hand them over (Notifications and hand-overs) and wait for its word. A release is possible only after the report is recorded (`notification-sent`), the files are in the quarantine, and an authority or a court has given korbat leave or an instruction to destroy them, in writing, with a reference. Record that as a fact of its own, with the day the leave bears and your name: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js release-leave <seal> --by <authority|court> --reference <text> --day <yyyy-mm-dd> --operator <name>`, where `<seal>` is the seal's ledger row as its case shows it. If the authority asked that the person is not told, record that before any release: with the leave (`--untold`, with `--until <instant>` or without an end; `release-leave --end-untold <leave>` ends an open one later), or, when the request came apart from the leave, on the report's record as Authorities' orders says (`notification-event`, with its end or without one). The author's notice then waits for the end of every such mark. A recorded leave is never rewritten or deleted: check the seal and the reference before you record it. A leave that you recorded by mistake all the same is withdrawn, `release-leave --withdraw <leave> --operator <name>`: it then supports no release, and the right leave, if there is one, is recorded as a new one. Withdraw it at once: a leave that a release already rests on cannot be withdrawn, and nothing takes a release back.

Then an admin confirms the release on the case ("Release and destroy", with the key), and every staff account is mailed that it happened. Then run the Quarantine steps above, whose list prints the released files as `destroy` lines, and `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js release-show <release>`: it prints each destroyed file's digest and the day after which no backup that is deleted on time holds the files. On an instruction to destroy at once, destroy the backups of the image store taken before the move too, and note it; a backup kept for an authority is destroyed by hand when that authority releases it. An answer "not illegal" is no release: an admin lifts the seal and the Quarantine steps return the files. Silence ends nothing, and korbat promises nobody a destruction.

## The yearly edition

The public figures (sub-project 3d; design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-transparency-automation-3d-design.md`): `/rules` prints every rule, what korbat can do and when, what each automated tool does today as the running server reports it, and the rulebook's change log; `/transparency` prints one edition a calendar year, in counts that point at nobody: 0, "1 to 9", or rounded to ten, and a line under ten folded into "other", but for the authorities' orders, which the law asks for as numbers.

**The yearly edition and the monthly count.** The edition publishes itself on or after 1 March: once a day after `API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR`, the API's job `transparency` asks for the last closed year's edition, and for every earlier year that has one, which gains a marked version only when an order whose hold has ended can now be counted; no figure of the running year exists anywhere. `staff.js edition <year>` prints the newest stored version, and `--correct` computes every table again and stores the result as a corrected version beside it, which its line on the page says; no version is ever changed or deleted. Each month the job stores two numbers of the month before, the accounts seen signed in and the sum of each day's readers without an account, and the counting sketches in Valkey go; `staff.js recipients` prints the exact figure, the average of the six full months before today, for an authority that asks (DSA Art. 24(3)); `tco-counts` stays for the authority too. Whether readers without an account are counted is `API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT` in `infra/.env` (on unless set to off; then the pages say "at least"), which the API reads at its start: set it, then `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`.

```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js edition <year>             # the newest stored version, a line a figure
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js edition <year> --correct   # every table counted again, as a new version
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js recipients                 # the six full months before today, exactly
```

## Profile and account
Signed-in accounts manage themselves under Settings; every route below needs the session and, where it says fresh, a re-authentication within five minutes (the app opens its panel when the API answers `reauth_required`).
- **Profile.** `PATCH /api/me/profile` sets the display name (up to 50 characters) and the bio (one line, up to 160). `POST /api/me/handle` (fresh) changes the handle once every 30 days; every handle an account ever had stays reserved for it in `handle_history`, so nobody else can take an old handle and the account can go back to it, except a handle korbat retired, which is nobody's, its former holder's included; a retirement lifts the 30-day wait (Moderation, Handle retirement). There is no redirect from an old handle.
- **Email.** `POST /api/auth/email/change/start` (fresh) sends a code to the new address; `POST /api/auth/email/change/verify` moves the account there and tells the old address, whose notice carries a link (`/email-revert/<token>`, `POST /api/auth/email/revert`, valid 24 hours, once) that moves the account back and runs the lockdown described under Passkeys and fresh authentication (every session and device signed out, the password removed, passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the change removed). Sessions stay signed in after a change.
- **Verified badge.** Proof of holding a phone number, kept only as a keyed hash; one number per account. `VERIFY_PROVIDER` picks who sends the text: `off` (default; the badge is hidden), `dev` (the code is always `000000`; refused in production) or `vonage` (Vonage Verify v2 with `VONAGE_API_KEY`, `VONAGE_API_SECRET` and `VERIFY_BRAND`; the runbook is section 13 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-account-lifecycle-1b-design.md`, and `node scripts/verify-badge.mjs +4479xxxxxxxx` checks live credentials without touching an account). Routes: `POST /api/auth/badge/start`, `POST /api/auth/badge/verify`, `DELETE /api/auth/badge` (all fresh); starts are limited per account, per number, per IP and instance-wide (200 texts a day), and a flow takes at most five codes. The web build shows the badge section only with `WEB_BADGE=on` in `infra/.env` (the default is off, matching `API_VERIFY_PROVIDER=off`); set both together.
- **Data export.** `POST /api/account/export` (fresh, once a day) streams a ZIP with `export.json` (the account with its passkeys' names and dates, profile, posts, likes, reposts, bookmarks, following, blocks, mutes, sessions, devices and security events, and last the member `moderation`: the decisions about the account as its Cases screen lists them, with their statements while korbat holds them, and the reports the account sent, with their outcomes once released; since account sanctions also its strikes, suspensions, terminations and reporting measures, its replies to them and its own reporting counts, and in the profile the handles korbat retired) and every image the account uploaded under `media/`, except sealed images, images of posts it deleted and images whose content was erased, which are in neither the list nor the files. It never holds another person's report, a reporter, a notifier or a staff handle. Nothing is kept on the server: the archive is written entry by entry (ZIP64 when it passes 4 GiB or 65,535 entries), `export.json` is read in pages and streamed last, image files go through the media module's checked open, a request that fails before the first byte gives the day's export back, and one that fails midway breaks the download instead of saving a truncated archive.
- **Deletion.** `POST /api/account/delete/start` (fresh) mails a code; `POST /api/account/delete/confirm` with the code and the handle typed by the owner deletes the account at once: every session is revoked, posts become tombstones with their images and any pending uploads deleted from disk, likes, reposts, bookmarks, follows, blocks and mutes go with their counters, the profile is anonymised and keeps its handle, and the auth row is anonymised. The `account-purge` job (every five minutes) finishes any deletion the process did not, and takes down a terminated account once its decision is final for the person (Moderation, Termination). Nothing can be undone. A suspension, a termination or a seal never refuses or delays a person's own deletion. Moderation outlives a deletion: images that a case holds as evidence, or that an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material or a seal freezes, keep their rows and files, served to nobody, until nothing retains them; open cases about the account or its posts go on and are decided on their snapshots; the reports the account sent are still decided, with nothing left that says who sent them; and the statements of decisions about the account are erased 12 months after the deletion (Moderation, Evidence and retention).
## Passkeys and fresh authentication
An account can sign in and confirm sensitive changes with a passkey (WebAuthn), beside the emailed code, the password and two-factor codes. The API verifies through `@simplewebauthn/server`, which only `apps/api/src/auth/passkeys/webauthn.ts` imports; that module pins korbat's settings and adds its own checks.
- **Settings.** `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` is the domain passkeys are bound to (default: the host of `API_APP_ORIGIN`) and `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME` the name a browser shows (default `korbat`). Production refuses `localhost`, an IP address and anything that is not the origin's host or a parent domain of it. Browsers offer passkeys only on `https` or on `http://localhost`, never on an IP address.
- **Adding.** `POST /api/auth/passkeys/register/options` and `/verify`. Up to 10 passkeys, 5 added a day. User verification (fingerprint, face or PIN) is asked for and never required; only the attestation formats `none` and self-attested `packed` are accepted, so nothing is fetched from an authenticator's maker. The owner is mailed a link (`/passkey-remove/<token>`, valid 7 days, once) that removes the passkey and locks the account down.
- **Managing.** `GET /api/auth/passkeys` lists them (name, dates, synced, the device that added it, new, suspended); `PATCH /api/auth/passkeys/:id` renames and `DELETE` removes, the last one too. "This wasn't me" on a passkey of the last 7 days (`POST /api/auth/passkeys/:id/not-mine`) runs the lockdown.
- **Signing in.** `POST /api/auth/passkey/signin/options` and `/verify` need no email: the browser offers the passkeys it holds for the domain, from the button or from the email field's autofill. A sign-in whose passkey verified the user counts as two factors; one that did not is followed by the two-factor code on an account that has two-factor authentication, and staff who have it always give the code. A signature counter that goes backwards switches the passkey off, mails the owner and refuses the sign-in.
- **Fresh authentication has two levels.** A session records what it proved and when. Level 1 is any factor in the last five minutes; level 2 is a user-verified passkey, or a two-factor or recovery code beside an email code, a password or a passkey. An account with two-factor authentication needs level 2 to add or remove a passkey, change its password or email, set up, turn off or re-issue two-factor codes, and delete itself; every other account needs level 1. A refusal is `reauth_required` with `details: { level, have }`, and `POST /api/auth/reauth` (password, emailed code, two-factor code, recovery code or passkey) answers the level reached and rotates the session's token in place, so a copy of the old token stops working. Sessions are listed and revoked by an id that survives the rotation.
- **Lockdown.** Every "this wasn't me" runs one routine: the new-device alert's link, the passkey mail's remove link, the button on a new passkey, and the email change's undo. It signs out every session and device, removes the password, and removes the passkeys and two-factor authentication set up since the day before the event, in one transaction; the owner gets back in with a code sent to their email. A mailed link is tied to the address it went to: it does nothing while the account is at another address and works again once the address is restored.
- **What is kept.** The public key, the credential's id, its counter, whether it is synced and was registered with user verification, its name, and the device that added it; nothing about a fingerprint or a face ever leaves the person's device. The export lists names and dates only, and deleting the account deletes the passkeys.
- **After restoring a backup** the counters in the database are older than the authenticators': run `update auth.passkeys set counter = 0, suspect_at = null where suspect_at is null or suspect_at > '<restore time>';` so no passkey is refused as a copy (section 11 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-25-passkeys-1c-design.md`).
- **Tests.** A software authenticator (`apps/api/test/auth/soft-authenticator.ts`) runs whole ceremonies in the unit and integration suites. The API prints two `ExperimentalWarning`s at start, from the library's probe of Node 24's ML-DSA support; they are expected.
## Before going public
**The hard gate.** korbat is not opened to the public and sign-up is not opened to people the operator does not know until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's quarantine and release have shipped and the list below is done, and no authorities' contact point is published before then. The TCO Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2021/784) applies to a host insofar as it disseminates information to the public (Art. 1(2)) and its removal orders must be executed within one hour (Art. 3); DSA Art. 9 and 10 orders presuppose a service offered in the Union. Sub-project 3f receives both, carries them out from a phone at night, records every report to an authority and everything handed to one, and takes what korbat did again after a restore. 3c can seal images reported as child sexual abuse material, 3f hands them over to an authority, and 3d moves them out of the image store and releases them, only on an authority's or a court's leave or instruction to destroy (Quarantine, A release). Moving sub-project 4 before 3f or before 3d reopens this. The designs are `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md` (the order path, the alert channel, the records of reports to authorities and the recovery after a restore) and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md` (strikes, suspensions and handle retirement); the order of work is 3c, 3e, 3f, 3d.

**The owner's list (sub-project 3f).** korbat is not opened, and `API_CONTACT_POINT` stays empty, until every line is done. It holds everything the 3f design assumes the owner has done: a line that is missing here is a thing nobody does.

1. **The Member State.** Set `API_HOME_STATE` and the web build's `WEB_HOME_STATE`; fill the state's entry of `STATE_FACTS` (`packages/contracts/src/orders.ts`: the authorities and their register entries, the address for the copies of Annex II and III, the intake for notifications, the contact point's languages, the yearly filing, and the state's rule for telling a person of an order to provide information). Germany's entry is the worked example; any member the console prints as "not filled in" is yours.
2. **The mailbox.** A mailbox at an EU mail host that offers IMAP over TLS with an application password that can only read mail, tells you the junk folder's name, stores mail in the EU and forces no other sign-in for IMAP. Two more requirements, each checked with the host and with a test mail: no rule, filter or quarantine of the host moves or deletes mail before it reaches the inbox or the junk folder (a folder korbat does not watch is an order nobody sees), and the date the host stamps on a message is the time of its final delivery. Switch off remote content. Put the four `NOTIFY_IMAP_*` values, `KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD` and `NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN` in `infra/.env`, switch the services on with `COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify`, and set `API_NOTIFY=on`.
3. **The people's own access to the mailbox.** Every person on call reads orders in the mail host's own app and sends Annex II and III from the mailbox, so each needs the mailbox's own sign-in, which is not `notify`'s read-only password: decide who holds it, with which second factor, on which devices; write the list down; and change the password the day a person leaves. It is the one credential that can answer an authority in korbat's name.
4. **Registering.** Register the contact point with the competent authority and ask the eight questions of the research (OL E9.4): the channel and sender, whether other states use the same address, which time counts as receipt, how Annex II and III go back, whether a small host needs a portal account, how removal is checked and whether a "not found" page is read correctly, a test transmission, and whether referrals come to the same address. Register with the national intake for notifications and ask how files are delivered.
5. **The push hostname and ntfy's users.** The tunnel itself, which is still the Foundation's open task. A third public hostname on it for the push site, set as `API_PUSH_ORIGIN`. `infra/ntfy/server.yml`, made from its example: the publisher's token (the same value as `NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN`) and one user a phone, each with a password hash and a token made with ntfy's own commands; no example value left in it.
6. **The phones.** One Android phone a person on call, ntfy from F-Droid, the checks P1 to P8 each noted, and check M: the mail host's app signed in to the contact-point mailbox, ringing through Do Not Disturb, tried with a test mail while `notify` is stopped. The hand-over between people on call practised; the daily test looked at for a week; one night drill.
7. **The keys.** A security key with a PIN that works on each on-call phone, over NFC and over USB: sign in and confirm twice at night speed, and note the phone models that work.
8. **The papers, and counsel.** An offline copy of the Commission's register of competent authorities, refreshed each month; the texts of Annex II and III; this runbook, printed. Counsel who has agreed to answer inside two days, and the same day for a removal order from another Member State (the 48 hours for scrutiny), who reads every DSA Article 9 and Article 10 order before korbat acts on it; counsel's number, and a second one for the nights the first does not answer.
9. **The contact address.** The notice, the terms and the deletion mail send people to the address under Contact for a copy of an order, for korbat's own mistake and about a held address. Decide who reads that mailbox every working day and answers within two working days, from the runbook's two entries ("A person asks about a missing post", "An author writes about an order's notice").
10. **The page for the yearly report.** Nothing to create: since sub-project 3d the yearly report is the edition on `/transparency`, which korbat publishes itself on or after 1 March and the terms page links. Read it once after the first 1 March after korbat opened, and decide `API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT` (The yearly edition) before then.
11. **The keeper, and the two places files rest.** The daily copy kept off the server with the head, on an encrypted device, since it names every order, held ones included; one restore drill with it, from `restore-import` to the app's site open again. And the directory a hand-over's archive is written into: on an encrypted volume of the server, owned by uid 1000, emptied after every hand-over.
12. **Decide**, each with its cost in section 2 of the 3f design: korbat serves its home state only (row 6); a page that is not public answers "not found" (row 17); Android only, no voice call (rows 19 and 20); every message at the public contact address rings the on-call phone, so anyone who knows the address can cost a night, bounded only by the quiet period of 15 minutes, which is one constant and can be zero (row 20); a watcher or a database that stops at night wakes nobody, and the hour then depends on the mail host's app (row 22); a console tick holds the notice with no shorter cap (row 25); a DSA order's silence lasts as long as its authority states, with no end while it names none (rows 24 and 46); the author's view during a hold, and that korbat's own decisions and appeal answers about the post wait with it (rows 26 and 47); account data is not held for an order (row 30); an order against an account as such is not built, and its hour depends on the operator (row 43); the hand-over's way and the address hold (rows 34 and 35); when the yearly report is published (row 40); the periods, and that a message nobody handled is never deleted (row 42); the known limits (row 45).
13. **Counsel**, with the questions as the research words them: OL E9.4 (receipt under national law; an order in a language not declared), OL E12.4 questions 1 to 7, OL E15.4, OL E20.4 and OL E21.4; AU E16.4 questions 1 to 7, AU E17.4 and AU E22.4 questions 1 to 6. The first to answer: whether sealed files go with a notification. And six that the design's review added: a DSA Article 9 order whose silence has no end ("until further notice"); whether a statement of korbat's own about the same post, sent during a hold, would itself be "information on the removal"; whether an earlier decision's copy of a post's text may still be shown to its author while Article 6 preserves the post; when and how a person is told of an order to provide information (DSA Art. 10(5)) and what the home state's law says instead; whether sign-in times are produced for such an order; and the words of the deletion mail while nobody has judged the report, with whether GDPR Art. 21 gives a right to object there.

Set these in `infra/.env`:
- `API_APP_ORIGIN` to the public origin, for example `https://korbat.example`; the API refuses a plain-http origin in production.
- `API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` and `WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` to the keys of one Turnstile widget; the API and the web build refuse Cloudflare's test keys in production.
- `API_SMTP_URL` and `API_MAIL_FROM` to the EU mail relay; a plain `smtp://` relay must offer STARTTLS, which the API requires in production.
- `API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID` before the first passkey is registered, when it should differ from the host of `API_APP_ORIGIN`; changing it afterwards strands every passkey. The staff console does not use it: staff keys are bound to the console's own relying party ID.
- `API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN` to the staff console's public origin, for example `https://korbat-staff.example`, preferably on a registrable domain of its own so browsers treat the app and the console as different sites (a subdomain of the app's domain works too), and `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` left empty, so staff keys are bound to that hostname. Production refuses a plain-http console, an IP address or `localhost`, the app's hostname on any port, a console on a parent domain of the app's hostname, and a relying party ID other than the console's hostname or equal to the app's; no environment accepts the console's origin in `API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`. Empty, the console is off. From sub-project 3c only the console decides reports and notices; with it off they are taken and wait, and staff are alerted to them.
- `WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL` to the users' contact address, which the report form names when the human check fails or the limits are reached and which the terms page shows; the web image refuses to build without one, and a production build refuses a placeholder (a domain ending in `.local`, `.localhost`, `.test`, `.invalid` or `.example`, or `example.com`, `example.org` or `example.net`). Its mailbox is set to load no remote content, and to keep deleted mail no longer than its host's shortest setting; a person reads it every working day (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on the users' contact mailbox). Since sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well, as `API_CONTACT_POINT` for the API and `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` for the web build, with korbat's state as `API_HOME_STATE` and `WEB_HOME_STATE`, the last step of the owner's list below: with the languages it may be addressed in, among them an official language of korbat's home state (DSA Art. 11(3), TCO Art. 15(2)), and notified to the national authorities where the home state requires it.
- `API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR` to the hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
- `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` generated (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills a placeholder), backed up off the server and rotated as the paragraph below says; `API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off` and `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, their defaults (Moderation says when each is changed).
- `KORBAT_ENV=production` before building the images; it is the API's `NODE_ENV` too, so the guards above are on.
- `TUNNEL=on` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=cloudflare` when cloudflared is the only way in (the app's public hostname points at `http://caddy:8080`, and the console's at `http://caddy:8090`, below); `TUNNEL=off` and `API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy` when Caddy's port is reachable directly. With `on`, Caddy keeps `CF-Connecting-IP` for the API; with `off` it drops it, so nobody can claim an address.
- In Cloudflare, set Browser Cache TTL to "Respect Existing Headers", or browsers keep images for four hours whatever the server says.

Keep `API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY`, `API_IP_HASH_KEY`, `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` and `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` secret and backed up. Losing `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY` breaks every enrolled authenticator. To rotate it, put the old key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_TOTP_ENC_KEY`; each secret is re-encrypted with the new key when it is next used. Without `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY` korbat can neither mail a signed-out notifier nor say who sent a notice. To rotate `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`, put the old key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS` and a new `v2:` key in `API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY`. Contacts are never re-encrypted, so the old key stays listed until no contact made under it remains, that is until `select count(*) from auth.notifier_contacts where name_enc like 'v1:%' or email_enc like 'v1:%'` answers 0. A contact can outlive 13 months while its notice is still owed a decision or a mail. Keep the old key off the server for as long as any backup holds such a contact.

Before the first report can concern a threat to someone's life or safety, obtain and record the channels for a notification under DSA Art. 18: the national police's, and Europol's for when the Member State concerned cannot be identified, each asked for beforehand from the national police or the Digital Services Coordinator (Moderation, the runbook's bullet on Art. 18).

A post that a decision withholds or removes leaves Explore at the next read, as it leaves every list; nothing acts on Explore alone. Since formula version 2 (account sanctions) a post that a later decision restores gets back the hours it was hidden, and a suspended account's posts and approvals leave the round while the suspension runs. Explore's cold start lasts about two days: only accounts at least 48 hours old count, so on a new instance Explore stays empty until the first accounts are that old.

The staff console's final hostname is chosen before the first enrolment. Staff keys are bound to it, since `API_CONSOLE_RP_ID` equals it, so moving the console later strands every staff key and means a new enrolment for every person; this includes a move to a domain of its own or behind a gate at another hostname. The tunnel gets a second public hostname, the console's, pointing at `http://caddy:8090`, with its HTTP Host Header setting left empty, so the API sees the console's hostname. Cloudflare Access in front keeps the hostname and the keys. A WireGuard or Tailscale gate keeps them only if it serves the same hostname over https with a certificate of its own, because Caddy runs with `auto_https off` while TLS ends at Cloudflare. Rocket Loader, Zaraz and Web Analytics stay off for the console's hostname, through a configuration rule for that hostname: the console's policy would block every script they add. Each staff member enrols two keys.

Who can rewrite the audit log: the PostgreSQL superuser, the owner `korbat_migrate` (its password is in `infra/.env`, and the migrate service uses it at every start), and anyone with Docker access on the host (psql inside the postgres container is the superuser without a password). Any of them can change a row, recompute every later hash and move the head, and a plain `audit-verify` then passes; only a place kept before the change, by someone other than the person who made it, shows the change. Until sub-project 3d publishes the head, that is the kept-head practice of the runbook under Staff console: each day the keeper, the staff member who does not run the server, copies the newest place and hash from the console's audit page and opens the place kept on the previous visit with "Go to place" to check its hash, and after each deploy and each week the operator runs `audit-verify` with every place the keeper has kept. In 3a the keeper's check is the only one independent of the operator, and it still reads through the operator's API, so it detects a change made in the database, not one that also changes the API's code to show the kept hashes. With one person, nothing detects the operator's own changes until 3d. Run `audit-verify` before and after every PostgreSQL major upgrade: the chain's text embeds PostgreSQL's print of the stored JSON, and a version that printed it differently would fail every row with metadata, never pass a forged one.

Counsel's list, to be answered before the gate above opens. From moderation cases: the period for which the draft of an access request's answer is kept; whether a removal of terrorist content on a notice makes korbat a provider that has taken action under TCO Art. 7(2); whether a final decision on content its author already deleted is mailed; whether, and under which national law, an access request may be restricted or deferred for a case korbat reported to an authority under DSA Art. 18 or for images it sealed for good, or that an authority's order concerns (GDPR Art. 23(1)(d)), what the answer and any extension under Art. 12(3) then say, and whether it names those authorities as recipients (Art. 15(1)(c)); whether 30 days suits the content backups hold; and every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-moderation-cases-3c-design.md` flags for counsel on the path for child sexual abuse material (its rows Suspected child sexual abuse material, Evidence, What the author sees of removed content, and Case targets and measures). From account sanctions: every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md` flags for counsel, among them the reply window and what counts as sent, the protective suspension on images nobody assessed, termination, the restriction of reporting and its counts, how long the ledger's rows are kept, the handle retired under R4, and that korbat holds no account against its deletion. From authorities' orders: item 13 of the owner's list above, and every question that section 2 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md` flags for counsel, among them what the author is told and when, the address kept while a report is owed, and the yearly report.

## Dependency audit

`pnpm audit --audit-level high` runs in CI. Two lower advisories are accepted, both in build-time tools that never see untrusted input here: `esbuild` 0.18 under drizzle-kit's config loader (its development server, which nothing starts) and `uuid` 7 under Expo's Xcode config plugin. Renovate moves them with their parents.
````

### Replace `apps/api/src/app.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { MeResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Hono } from "hono";
import { bodyLimit } from "hono/body-limit";
import { cors } from "hono/cors";
import { HTTPException } from "hono/http-exception";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { AccountError, type Account } from "./account";
import { AuthError, type Auth } from "./auth";
import type { Config } from "./config";
import type { AppEnv } from "./env";
import { errorBody } from "./lib/errors";
import { MediaError, type Media } from "./media";
import { observability } from "./middleware/observability";
import { clientIpKey, rateLimit, type RateLimitStore } from "./middleware/rate-limit";
import { noStore, securityHeaders } from "./middleware/security-headers";
import { ModerationError, type Moderation } from "./moderation";
import { healthRoutes, type HealthChecks } from "./routes/health";
import { SocialError, type Social } from "./social";
import type { Staff } from "./staff";
import type { Transparency } from "./transparency";

/** JSON requests are small; the one raw upload route counts its own bytes and is exempt. */
export const JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES = 64 * 1024;

/**
 * The staff console's paths (3a design, section 5): /api/staff and everything under it, never a path that merely begins
 * with the same letters. The app's CORS and session resolution pass over them, so a staff route never meets the app's
 * credentialed CORS, its Origin allow-list, its session or its CSRF check: the staff gate and the staff session are the
 * only origin and session logic there. Everything else in the chain (request id, access log, client identity, security
 * headers, no-store, the body limit, the global rate limit) applies to them as to any path.
 */
const isStaffPath = (path: string) => path === "/api/staff" || path.startsWith("/api/staff/");

export interface AppDeps {
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  healthChecks: HealthChecks;
  auth: Auth;
  /** Posting and feed. Optional so auth-only tests need no database for it; the server always wires it. */
  social?: Social;
  /** Image uploads. Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  media?: Media;
  /** The account lifecycle (the data export). Optional for the same reason; the server always wires it. */
  account?: Account;
  /** The staff console's API. Mounted only while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is set; optional as the other modules are. */
  staff?: Staff;
  /** Reports and notices. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it, whether the console is on or off. */
  moderation?: Moderation;
  /** Checks that report a part being down without marking the API unhealthy, the image worker for one. */
  advisoryChecks?: HealthChecks;
  /** 3d: the public figures' two routes. Optional as the other modules are; the server always wires it. */
  transparency?: Transparency;
}

export function createApp({ config, logger, rateLimitStore, healthChecks, auth, social, media, account, staff, moderation, advisoryChecks, transparency }: AppDeps) {
  const app = new Hono<AppEnv>();

  app.use(observability(logger));
  app.use(auth.clientIdentity);
  app.use(securityHeaders, noStore);
  const appCors = cors({ origin: config.TRUSTED_ORIGINS, credentials: true });
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : appCors(c, next)));
  const jsonBodies = bodyLimit({
    maxSize: JSON_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES,
    onError: (c) => c.json(errorBody("payload_too_large", "The request body is too large", (c as typeof c & { get(key: "requestId"): string }).get("requestId")), 413),
  });
  app.use((c, next) => (c.req.method === "POST" && c.req.path === "/api/media" ? next() : jsonBodies(c, next)));
  // Image files come before the global limit and session resolution: they have their own bucket,
  // and a public image needs no session. Everything else under /api/media falls through to below.
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.fileRoutes);
  app.use(rateLimit({ name: "global", store: rateLimitStore, limit: 300, windowMs: 60_000, key: clientIpKey }));
  // 3f (design, section 7.12): the status of a post's page, which Caddy asks for every view of /post/*, with the visitor's
  // cookies: after the global limit, which counts it against the visitor, and before the session's resolution, so it
  // reads no session. Every other path falls through to below.
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.statusRoutes);
  // 3d (design, sections 9.1 and 10.6): GET /api/public/facts and /api/public/transparency, at the same place and for the
  // same reasons: counted against the visitor by the global limit, and answered before any session is read. Each sets its
  // own Cache-Control, which noStore leaves alone.
  if (transparency) app.route("/api", transparency.routes);
  app.use((c, next) => (isStaffPath(c.req.path) ? next() : auth.resolveSession(c, next)));

  app.route("/api/health", healthRoutes(healthChecks, config.KORBAT_VERSION, advisoryChecks));
  app.route("/api/auth", auth.routes);
  // 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me from the auth module's meFor and the moderation module's standingFor, read at
  // every request; null without the moderation module (an app built for some tests) or without a profile.
  app.get("/api/me", auth.requireOnboarding, async (c) => {
    const session = c.get("session")!;
    const base = await auth.meFor(session);
    const standing = moderation && base.profile !== null ? await moderation.standingFor(session.userId) : null;
    return c.json({ ...base, standing } satisfies MeResponse);
  });
  if (media) app.route("/api/media", media.routes);
  if (account) app.route("/api/account", account.routes);
  // The console is off while CONSOLE_ORIGIN is unset: nothing is mounted, and every staff path is the unknown route below.
  if (staff && config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN !== undefined) app.route("/api/staff", staff.routes(config.CONSOLE_ORIGIN));
  // Reports and notices are taken, kept and given receipts whether or not the console is on: anyone may send one, signed
  // in or not, so these routes stand after session resolution and behind no session guard of their own.
  if (moderation) app.route("/api", moderation.routes);
  if (social) app.route("/api", social.routes);

  app.notFound((c) => c.json(errorBody("not_found", "No such route", c.get("requestId")), 404));
  app.onError((err, c) => {
    if (err instanceof AuthError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    if (err instanceof HTTPException) return c.json(errorBody("invalid_request", err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    if (err instanceof MediaError) return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    if (err instanceof SocialError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // The account routes render nothing themselves: their own errors and those of the three modules they call all land here.
    if (err instanceof AccountError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId")), err.status);
    }
    // A moderation flow's refusal, from the app's routes or from the console's case routes.
    if (err instanceof ModerationError) {
      if (err.retryAfterSeconds) c.header("Retry-After", String(err.retryAfterSeconds));
      return c.json(errorBody(err.code, err.message, c.get("requestId"), err.details), err.status);
    }
    c.get("log").error({ err }, "unhandled error");
    return c.json(errorBody("internal", "Internal error", c.get("requestId")), 500);
  });

  return app;
}
```

```ts
 */
import type {
  DeleteConfirmRequest,
  DeleteStartResponse,
  StaffEnrollOptionsRequest,
  StaffEnrollVerifyRequest,
  StaffEnrollVerifyResponse,
  StaffKeysResponse,
  StaffMe,
  StaffSessionsResponse,

  StaffStepUpOptionsRequest,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { Context, MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type Redis from "ioredis";
import type { Logger } from "pino";

/**
 * What the account module needs from this one (1b design, section 5): the auth side of a deletion
 * (the code, the confirmation that takes the account down, the purge's list and its last step), the
 * auth side of the data export, and the event log for what the account module does.
 */
export interface AuthForAccount {
  /** Mails the deletion code to the account's own address and answers the flow id. */
  startDeletion(session: Session, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<DeleteStartResponse>;
  /** Checks the typed handle and the code, then marks the account deleted and revokes every session, in one transaction: from here the account is gone. */
  confirmDeletion(session: Session, input: DeleteConfirmRequest): Promise<void>;
  /** Deleted accounts whose auth row is not anonymised yet, oldest deletion first. */
  pendingPurges(): Promise<string[]>;
  /**
   * Finishes step 1's rows if a take-down stopped after the mark, then anonymises the auth row and marks it purged; a
   * no-op when it already is. 3f: `held` while the account's address is held for a report (the credentials are gone).
   */
  finishPurge(userId: string): Promise<"purged" | "held" | "none">;
  /**
   * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.8): the take-down of an account whose termination is final, as the system: the account
   * marked deleted and every session revoked in one transaction, then termination_final to the address read before it,
   * after that commit and best effort. True only for the take-down it made; false, with nothing written or sent, for an
   * account already marked deleted.
   */
  takeDownTerminated(userId: string, facts: { decidedAt: Date; imagesSealed: boolean }): Promise<boolean>;
  /** The account's facts, its passkeys (without their keys), its live sessions, its devices and its own events. */
  exportAccount(userId: string): Promise<AccountExport>;
  appendEvent(userId: string, type: AuthEventType, metadata?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>;
}

/**
 * What the staff module needs from this one (3a design, section 5): the credential side of the staff routes, which the
 * staff module mounts behind its gate. Staff keys, staff sessions and enrolments are credentials, so their flows and
 * tables stay here, and the staff module reaches them only through this interface.
 */
export interface AuthForStaff {
  /** Registration options for the key an enrolment link's holder is about to create. */
  enrollOptions(input: StaffEnrollOptionsRequest): Promise<StaffEnrollOptions>;
  /** Checks the browser's answer and stores the staff key, spending the link; the owner is mailed. */
  enrollVerify(input: StaffEnrollVerifyRequest, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<StaffEnrollVerifyResponse>;
  /** Discoverable-credential options for a staff sign-in. */
  signInOptions(): Promise<{ options: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON }>;
  /** Checks a staff key's assertion and opens a staff session; the route sets its cookies with setStaffCookies. */
  signInVerify(input: StaffSignInVerifyRequest, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<StaffSignedIn>;
  /** Stands before every staff route that needs a session: reads it and sets `staffSession` on the context. */
  requireStaff: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The session's account and both its ends, with the seconds left. */
  me(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffMe>;
  /** The person's own live staff sessions. */
  sessions(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffSessionsResponse>;
  /** The person's own live staff keys. */
  keys(session: ActiveStaffSession): Promise<StaffKeysResponse>;
  /** Ends the session, on the record; the route clears its cookies with clearStaffCookies. */
  signOut(session: ActiveStaffSession, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<void>;
  /** Options for confirming one action with the session's key: a challenge bound to the session and to exactly that action. */
  stepUpOptions(session: ActiveStaffSession, request: StaffStepUpOptionsRequest): Promise<{ options: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON }>;
  /**
   * Stands before every staff route that changes something, behind requireStaff: verifies the body's `stepUp` against the
   * action, the target `target` reads from the request and the body's params, and sets `staffStepUp` on the context.
   */
  requireStaffStepUp(action: StaffStepUpAction, target: (c: Context<AppEnv>) => string | undefined): MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** Revokes one of the person's own live staff sessions, on the record with its confirmation; false when the handle names none. */
  revokeSession(session: ActiveStaffSession, confirmed: StaffStepUpConfirmed, ctx: StaffRequestContext): Promise<boolean>;
}

/**
 * What the moderation module needs from this one (3c design, section 5): the human check of a signed-out notice, a
 * signed-out notifier's contact, which is stored here, encrypted, out of the API role's reach, and every mail to an
 * account, a notifier or staff. The moderation module names a contact by the id it chose and an account by its id; it
 * never sees an address or a mail token, and a message is a typed union over the templates, so no caller passes free
 * text. `mailNotifier` and `mailAccount` answer "refused" when the relay refused the recipient for good and throw
 * MailUnavailable for any other failure, so the caller records the one and tries the other again.
 */
export interface AuthForModeration {
  /** Turnstile's answer for the token of a signed-out notice; every failure is false. */
  verifyHuman(token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Stores a signed-out notifier's name and address under the id the notice carries, with a fresh mail token when an address is given. */
  storeNotifierContact(contactId: string, contact: { name?: string; email?: string }): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Sends a signed-out notifier's receipt, with its page link. "suppressed" for a stopped address, "folded" for a
   * second receipt in 24 hours to an address that is not confirmed, "no_address" for a contact without one, "forgotten"
   * for an id no contact has (it was never stored, or the janitor has deleted it).
   */
  mailNotifier(contactId: string, message: NotifierMessage): Promise<NotifierMailResult>;
  /**
   * Sends a mail to an account's own address, with neither the cap nor a confirmation: the receipt and the daily update
   * of its reports, which a stop of that address holds back ("suppressed"), and the statement of a decision about it,
   * which nothing holds back. "no_address" for a deleted account.
   */
  mailAccount(userId: string, message: AccountMessage): Promise<AccountMailResult>;
  /**
   * The daily update to signed-out notifiers: one notice_update for each address the parts' contacts gave, with every
   * part's lines, every carried receipt and the page link of each other notice. It applies a stop of the address and
   * neither the confirmation nor the cap, answers for each contact, and throws for none: "unavailable" when the relay
   * could not take that address's mail or the contact could not be read.
   */
  mailNotifierUpdates(parts: readonly NotifierUpdatePart[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>>;
  /** Sends a staff alert to every live staff account, best effort; answers how many addresses the relay took, and never throws for a failed send. */
  mailStaff(message: StaffMessage): Promise<number>;
  /** For each id, whether a contact has it, whether a name and an address were given, and whether the address is confirmed or stopped. */
  notifierFacts(contactIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, NotifierFacts>>;
  /** The name a notifier gave, or null: for a confirmed reveal only. */
  notifierName(contactId: string): Promise<string | null>;
  /** Whether the token is the contact's mail token, compared in constant time; false when it has none. */
  notifierMailTokenMatches(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** With the contact's mail token: the address is confirmed for 30 days and any stop of it lifted. False for any other token. */
  confirmNotifier(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** With the contact's mail token: no more report mails to the address. False for any other token. */
  stopNotifier(contactId: string, token: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Whether the account's own address said stop. */
  accountReportMailStopped(userId: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Lifts a stop of the account's own address; true when there was one. */
  resumeAccountReportMail(userId: string): Promise<boolean>;
  /** Sets the day each of these contacts is forgotten. */
  forgetNotifierAfter(contactIds: readonly string[], at: Date): Promise<void>;
  /** Command line only: the contacts that gave an address, with the names they gave, for an access request. */
  findNotifierContacts(email: string): Promise<{ id: string; name: string | null }[]>;
  /** How many contacts and confirmations should have been removed more than a day ago: a count only. */
  overdueContacts(): Promise<number>;
}

export interface CreateAuthOptions {
  config: Config;
  logger: Logger;
  /** The korbat_auth pool. The auth module never receives the API pool. */
  authDb: Db;
  mailer: Mailer;
  profiles: ProfileStore;
  /** Either a Redis client or a ready key-value store (tests use an in-memory store). */
  redis?: Redis;
  kv?: KeyValueStore;
  turnstile?: TurnstileVerifier;
  breachChecker?: BreachChecker;
  /**
   * The phone verification provider behind the verified badge. Absent or null, the badge routes answer
   * badge_unavailable; the server passes verificationProviderFrom(config), tests the development provider.
   */
  verify?: VerificationProvider | null;
  now?: () => Date;
}

/**
 * The provider VERIFY_PROVIDER names: none for `off` (the badge is hidden), the fixed-code one for `dev`,
 * Vonage Verify with the configured credentials and brand for `vonage`. `fetchFn` is for tests only.
 */
export function verificationProviderFrom(config: Config, fetchFn?: typeof fetch): VerificationProvider | null {
  switch (config.VERIFY_PROVIDER) {
    case "off":
      return null;
    case "dev":
      return devProvider();
    case "vonage":
      // Production refuses this configuration in config.ts; development gets the same refusal here, at start-up, rather than a failing first request.
      if (!config.VONAGE_API_KEY || !config.VONAGE_API_SECRET) throw new Error("VERIFY_PROVIDER=vonage needs VONAGE_API_KEY and VONAGE_API_SECRET");
      return vonageProvider({ apiKey: config.VONAGE_API_KEY, apiSecret: config.VONAGE_API_SECRET, brand: config.VERIFY_BRAND, fetch: fetchFn });
  }
}

export function createAuth(options: CreateAuthOptions) {
  const kv = options.kv ?? (options.redis ? redisKv(options.redis) : undefined);
  if (!kv) throw new Error("createAuth needs a Redis client or a key-value store");
  const now = options.now ?? (() => new Date());
  const repo = createAuthRepo(options.authDb);
  const sessions = createSessions({ repo, kv, now });
  const deps: AuthDeps = {
    repo,
    kv,
    sessions,
    lockout: createLockout({ repo, kv, now }),
    mailer: options.mailer,
    turnstile: options.turnstile ?? cloudflareTurnstile(options.config.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY),
    breachChecker: options.breachChecker ?? hibpChecker(),
    profiles: options.profiles,
    verify: options.verify ?? null,
    config: authConfigFrom(options.config),
    log: options.logger,
    now,
  };
  /** A security event about an account, for the modules that own no auth table (the social module's profile and handle changes, the account module's export). */
  const appendEvent = (userId: string, type: AuthEventType, metadata?: Record<string, unknown>) => repo.appendEvent({ userId, type, metadata });
  const forAccount: AuthForAccount = {
    startDeletion: (session, ctx) => startDeletion(deps, session, ctx),
    confirmDeletion: (session, input) => confirmDeletion(deps, session, input),
    pendingPurges: () => repo.pendingPurges(),
    finishPurge: (userId) => finishPurge(deps, userId),
    takeDownTerminated: (userId, facts) => takeDownTerminated(deps, userId, facts),
    exportAccount: (userId) => exportAccount(deps, userId),
    appendEvent,
  };
  // 3d (design, sections 5 and 7.5): the recipients' count, which the transparency module keeps. This module is built
  // first, so the wiring hands it the handler once both exist (onSeen); until then resolveSession counts nothing.
  let seenBy: TransparencyForAuth | null = null;
  const staffGuard = requireStaff(deps);
  const forStaff: AuthForStaff = {
    enrollOptions: (input) => enrollOptions(deps, input),
    enrollVerify: (input, ctx) => enrollVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    signInOptions: () => signInOptions(deps),
    signInVerify: (input, ctx) => signInVerify(deps, input, ctx),
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    me: (session) => staffMe(deps, session),
    sessions: (session) => listStaffSessions(deps, session),
    keys: (session) => listStaffKeys(deps, session),
    signOut: (session, ctx) => signOutStaff(deps, session, ctx),
    stepUpOptions: (session, request) => stepUpOptions(deps, session, request),
    requireStaffStepUp: (action, target) => requireStaffStepUp(deps, action, target),
    revokeSession: (session, confirmed, ctx) => revokeStaffSession(deps, session, confirmed, ctx),
  };
  const forModeration: AuthForModeration = {
    verifyHuman: (token) => deps.turnstile.verify(token),
    storeNotifierContact: (contactId, contact) => storeNotifierContact(deps, contactId, contact),
    mailNotifier: (contactId, message) => mailNotifier(deps, contactId, message),
    mailAccount: (userId, message) => mailAccount(deps, userId, message),
    mailNotifierUpdates: (parts) => mailNotifierUpdates(deps, parts),
    mailStaff: (message) => mailStaff(deps, message),
    notifierFacts: (contactIds) => notifierFacts(deps, contactIds),
    notifierName: (contactId) => notifierName(deps, contactId),
    notifierMailTokenMatches: (contactId, token) => notifierMailTokenMatches(deps, contactId, token),
    confirmNotifier: (contactId, token) => confirmNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    stopNotifier: (contactId, token) => stopNotifier(deps, contactId, token),
    accountReportMailStopped: (userId) => accountReportMailStopped(deps, userId),
    resumeAccountReportMail: (userId) => resumeAccountReportMail(deps, userId),
    forgetNotifierAfter: (contactIds, at) => forgetNotifierAfter(deps, contactIds, at),
    findNotifierContacts: (email) => findNotifierContacts(deps, email),
    overdueContacts: () => overdueContacts(deps),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    routes: authRoutes(deps),
    me: meHandler(deps),
    /** 3e (design, section 7.12): /api/me's answer without the standing, which the app adds from the moderation module. */
    meFor: (session: Session) => me(deps, session),
    appendEvent,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the staff module uses. */
    forStaff,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses. */
    forModeration,
    /** Runs first on every request: resolves the client address the way TRUST_PROXY says and hashes it, and its network with it. */
    clientIdentity: clientIdentity({ trust: deps.config.trustProxy, ipHashKey: deps.config.ipHashKey }),
    resolveSession: resolveSession(deps, () => seenBy),
    /** 3d: registers the transparency module's count, which resolveSession calls from then on (index.ts, once both exist). */
    onSeen: (handler: TransparencyForAuth) => {
      seenBy = handler;
    },
    requireSession,
    requireOnboarding,
    requireFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** Level 2 within the window on an account with TOTP, level 1 otherwise: for the routes of the 1c design's section 10. */
    requireStrongFreshAuth: (maxAgeSeconds?: number) => requireStrongFreshAuth(deps, maxAgeSeconds),
    /** A staff session from the staff cookie, read from the database at every request (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaff: staffGuard,
    /** A fresh confirmation by the staff session's key, bound to the action a route is about to execute (3a design, section 7). */
    requireStaffStepUp: forStaff.requireStaffStepUp,
    /** Starts the retention pass (dead codes, old sessions and staff sessions, spent enrolment links, device address hashes, old events, forgotten notifier contacts and their confirmations) and returns the function that stops it. */
    startJanitor: (lock: JobLock) => createJanitor(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Auth = ReturnType<typeof createAuth>;
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/auth/middleware.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { Context } from "hono";
import { createMiddleware } from "hono/factory";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { errorBody } from "../lib/errors";
import type { TransparencyForAuth } from "../transparency";
import { authErrorMessage, type AuthDeps } from "./context";
import { bearerToken, checkCsrf, readSessionCookie, refreshSessionCookies } from "./cookies";
import { SESSION_IDLE_MS, type ReauthNeeded } from "./sessions";

const SAFE_METHODS = new Set(["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS"]);

/**
 * Runs on every request. Refuses state-changing requests whose Origin is not allowed, resolves the
 * session from a bearer token (native) or the `__Host-` cookie (web), and requires the CSRF token on
 * cookie-authenticated state changes. Sets `session` and `authVia` on the context.
 *
 * 3d (design, sections 5 and 7.5): it is also where the recipients are counted, and the only place: the global limit runs
 * before a session can resolve. `seenBy` answers the handler that auth.onSeen was given, or null until index.ts has
 * registered one (and in every test that registers none), and then nothing is counted. A request with a session is
 * `seen`; a GET without one is `seenSignedOut`, which counts it only for the public reads. Neither call is waited for, and
 * whatever either throws is dropped: counting never fails or slows a request.
 */
export function resolveSession(deps: AuthDeps, seenBy: () => TransparencyForAuth | null = () => null) {
  return createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
    c.set("session", null);
    c.set("authVia", null);
    const stateChanging = !SAFE_METHODS.has(c.req.method);
    const origin = c.req.header("origin");
    if (stateChanging && origin && !deps.config.allowedOrigins.includes(origin)) {
      return c.json(errorBody("csrf_failed", authErrorMessage("csrf_failed"), c.get("requestId")), 403);
    }

    const bearer = bearerToken(c);
    const token = bearer ?? readSessionCookie(c);
    if (token) {
      const resolved = await deps.sessions.resolve(token);
      if (resolved) {
        if (!bearer && stateChanging && !checkCsrf(c, deps.config.allowedOrigins)) {
          return c.json(errorBody("csrf_failed", authErrorMessage("csrf_failed"), c.get("requestId")), 403);
        }
        c.set("session", resolved.session);
        c.set("authVia", bearer ? "bearer" : "cookie");
        if (resolved.slid && !bearer) refreshSessionCookies(c, token, Math.floor(SESSION_IDLE_MS / 1000));
      }
    }
    countRecipient(c, seenBy);
    await next();
  });
}

/** Hands the request to the recipients' count, as resolveSession says; never throws. */
function countRecipient(c: Context<AppEnv>, seenBy: () => TransparencyForAuth | null): void {
  try {
    const handler = seenBy();
    if (handler === null) return;
    const session = c.get("session");
    if (session) handler.seen(session.userId);
    else if (c.req.method === "GET") handler.seenSignedOut(c.get("clientIp") ?? "", c.req.header("user-agent") ?? "", c.req.path);
  } catch {
    // Counting never fails a request.
  }
}

/** Any signed-in session, including one whose account has not chosen a handle yet. */
export const requireOnboarding = createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
  if (!c.get("session")) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", "Sign in required", c.get("requestId")), 401);
  await next();
});

/** A signed-in session whose account has finished onboarding. */
export const requireSession = createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
  const session = c.get("session");
  if (!session) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", "Sign in required", c.get("requestId")), 401);
  if (!session.onboarded) return c.json(errorBody("onboarding_required", authErrorMessage("onboarding_required"), c.get("requestId")), 403);
  await next();
});

/** The refusal both freshness guards answer: the level the route asks for and the factors proven in time, so the app can ask for what is missing. */
const reauthRequired = (c: Context<AppEnv>, needed: ReauthNeeded) => c.json(errorBody("reauth_required", authErrorMessage("reauth_required"), c.get("requestId"), needed), 403);

/** The session proved a factor within the last `maxAgeSeconds` (300, five minutes, by default): level 1. */
export function requireFreshAuth(deps: AuthDeps, maxAgeSeconds?: number) {
  const windowMs = maxAgeSeconds === undefined ? undefined : maxAgeSeconds * 1000;
  return createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
    const session = c.get("session");
    if (!session) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", "Sign in required", c.get("requestId")), 401);
    const needed = deps.sessions.reauthNeeded(session, 1, windowMs);
    if (needed) return reauthRequired(c, needed);
    await next();
  });
}

/**
 * Level 2 within the window when the account has TOTP (a second factor beside a first, or a user-verified passkey), and
 * level 1 otherwise: what the routes of the 1c design's section 10 ask for.
 */
export function requireStrongFreshAuth(deps: AuthDeps, maxAgeSeconds?: number) {
  const windowMs = maxAgeSeconds === undefined ? undefined : maxAgeSeconds * 1000;
  return createMiddleware<AppEnv>(async (c, next) => {
    const session = c.get("session");
    if (!session) return c.json(errorBody("unauthenticated", "Sign in required", c.get("requestId")), 401);
    const needed = deps.sessions.reauthNeeded(session, deps.sessions.requiredLevel(session), windowMs);
    if (needed) return reauthRequired(c, needed);
    await next();
  });
}
```

```ts
export const STAFF_USAGE = [

  "  alert-test [--on-call]                 write a test push to every staff phone, or to the phone on call alone,",

  ...RESTORE_USAGE,

  // 3d Task 1 (design, section 8.10): the quarantine's list and record, as the migrator in the migrate service.

/** A place in the chain and the hash it had when someone kept it, as audit-head printed it. */
export interface KeptPlace {
  seq: number;
  hash: string;
}

export type StaffCommand =
  | { command: "enroll"; email: string }
  | { command: "keys"; email: string | null }
  | { command: "audit-head" }
  | { command: "audit-verify"; kept: KeptPlace[] }
  | { command: "revoke"; email: string; key: string | "all" }
  | { command: "text-verify" }
  | { command: "access-request"; who: { handle: string } | { email: string } }
  | { command: "link"; email: string; handle: string }
  | { command: "unlink"; email: string; handle: string }
  | { command: "limits"; limits: StaffLimits }
  // 3f's review: a test push, to every staff phone or to the phone on call alone.
  | { command: "alert-test"; onCall: boolean }
```
