### Replace `infra/.env.example` (whole file)

```text
# Copy to infra/.env and change every password. Never commit infra/.env.
POSTGRES_USER=postgres
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me-superuser
POSTGRES_DB=korbat
KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-migrate
KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-api
KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-auth
# The database role of the contact point's watcher, notify (3f). infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh makes it on a new data
# directory; on one that exists the README's Upgrading makes it once. notify's own settings are below, under 3f.
KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD=change-me-notify
# Valkey (the session cache and rate-limit counters) refuses every command without it.
REDIS_PASSWORD=change-me-redis

# Images. The formats korbat accepts: remove one to refuse it and keep its decoder blocked, for
# example after a security advisory against that decoder, then restart api and worker.
MEDIA_FORMATS=jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif
# Uploads are refused while a media volume has less free space than this many bytes (2 GiB). The
# volumes share a disk with Postgres, and a full disk stops the database.
MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES=2147483648
# The sweeper's pass that deletes images without a database row: on refuses when there are many of
# them (a database restored from an older snapshot looks like that), off skips it during a restore,
# force deletes them once you have checked.
MEDIA_RECONCILE=on

API_LOG_LEVEL=info
# Comma-separated browser origins allowed to call the API cross-origin. Empty in prod (same origin via Caddy).
API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:8081

# Auth. `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` fills the keys with random values and shares them with apps/api/.env.
# Origin the web app is served from (Caddy). Production: https://<your domain>.
API_APP_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8080
# Which header names the client: cloudflare when the tunnel is the only way in (the API then trusts
# cf-connecting-ip), caddy when Caddy's port is reachable directly. Never none behind a proxy.
API_TRUST_PROXY=caddy
API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY=change-me-key-auth-hmac
API_IP_HASH_KEY=change-me-key-ip-hash
API_TOTP_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-totp
# Earlier TOTP keys, comma-separated, kept only while secrets they encrypted are still stored; a secret
# read with one is re-encrypted with API_TOTP_ENC_KEY.
API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Encrypts what a signed-out notifier leaves to be told about their notice: a name, an address and the token of the
# mails' link. Keep it secret and backed up as API_TOTP_ENC_KEY is: without it korbat can neither mail a notifier nor
# say who sent a notice.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY=v1:change-me-key-notifier
# Earlier notifier keys, comma-separated. A contact is never encrypted again, so a key stays here while a contact it
# encrypted is still stored.
API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS=
# Cloudflare's documented always-pass test secret. Production uses the secret of your Turnstile widget.
API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY=1x0000000000000000000000000000000AA
# Mailpit from compose.dev.yml. Production: the EU relay, e.g. smtps://user:pass@smtp-relay.example:465
API_SMTP_URL=smtp://mailpit:1025
API_MAIL_FROM="korbat <no-reply@korbat.local>"
API_TERMS_VERSION=draft-2026-09
# Who checks the phone number behind the verified badge: off turns the badge off, dev accepts the code
# 000000 (development only; production refuses it), vonage texts a real code through Vonage Verify with the
# key and secret from the Vonage dashboard (the runbook in the 1b design says how).
API_VERIFY_PROVIDER=off
# Whether the web app's account settings show the verified badge section: on or off. Set it together with
# API_VERIFY_PROVIDER: off while that is off, on once it is dev or vonage (a section shown without a provider
# answers every Send code with "Verification is not available"). The web image reads it as EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE,
# which Expo inlines at export time.
WEB_BADGE=off
API_VONAGE_API_KEY=
API_VONAGE_API_SECRET=
# The sender name of the verification text: 1 to 18 characters, none of / { } : $.
API_VERIFY_BRAND=korbat
# Passkeys. The RP ID every passkey is bound to: empty means the host of API_APP_ORIGIN. It may instead be a parent
# domain of that host (korbat.example for app.korbat.example). The staff console does not use it: staff keys have their
# own RP ID. Production refuses an IP address or localhost. Choose it before the first passkey is added: changing it
# later strands every passkey.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=
# The site name password managers show next to a korbat passkey: 1 to 64 printable characters; empty means korbat.
API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=

# The staff console: the origin staff open it at, served by Caddy's second site (port 8090 in its container). Empty
# switches the console off: every /api/staff path then answers 404. It must differ from API_APP_ORIGIN and never appear
# in API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS. In development it is localhost on the port compose.dev.yml publishes the console on
# (DEV_CONSOLE_PORT below); open it there, never at 127.0.0.1. Production: https://<the console's own hostname>, a
# hostname apart from the app's.
API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN=http://localhost:8090
# The RP ID staff keys are bound to: empty means the hostname of API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN, which production requires. Choose
# the console's hostname before the first staff key is enrolled: moving the console later means enrolling every key
# again.
API_CONSOLE_RP_ID=

# Moderation. The hour of the UTC day, 0 to 23, at which the day's decisions on reports and notices are released to those
# who sent them, in one batch, so that nobody can tell from a mail's minute when a decision was made; empty means 7.
API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR=7
# The queue's emergency switch, published in the terms: on sorts cases whose open reports all come from unproven sources
# after the others of their lane, never below a less severe lane. off, the default, orders by lane and age alone.
API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN=off
# The retention job, which erases what is due and deletes kept image rows that nothing retains any more: on unless set
# to off. While it is off nothing is erased or deleted, the API logs a warning at every start, and the console counts
# what is late. off only for a restore window: README, Restoring, step 5
API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on

# Authorities' orders and the alert channel (3f). Whether the API judges the alert channel's health: on mails "Phone
# alerts are down" when the watcher's beat or a push is late; off (the default outside production) only skips that
# check, and the console's home says that phone alerts are switched off on this server. Leave it off until the
# contact-point mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
API_NOTIFY=off
# The operator's Member State, as an ISO code of a state whose facts the contracts hold (Germany's, DE, is the worked
# example), from which the console tells an order from another Member State; and the published contact point for
# authorities, an address. Leave the contact point empty until the owner's list is done (README, Before going public):
# the home state is required once it is set. The migrate service reads the home state too, for staff.js order-open.
API_HOME_STATE=DE
API_CONTACT_POINT=
# The report hold (3f): while a report of an account's sealed images to the authorities is owed, a deletion of the
# account keeps its email address, and nothing else of it, for at most seven days, and its deletion mail says so. on is
# the default; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once, and then a report needs the address taken
# before the account is deleted (README, Notifications and hand-overs).
API_REPORT_HOLD=on
# The edge's purge (3d): when an image stops being public, the API asks the network provider to drop its copies at the
# edge, by prefix, several images a request. off (the default) asks nothing, and the image's header is then
# the only bound on a copy. test is for the suites and is refused while APP_SITE is open. cloudflare needs the zone's
# id, an API token with the one permission Zone, Cache Purge (a secret: keep it as the keys above are, and it is in no
# log line), and the public hostname images are served under, without a scheme or a path (README, The edge).
API_EDGE_PURGE=off
API_EDGE_ZONE_ID=
API_EDGE_API_TOKEN=
API_EDGE_HOST=
# The recipients' count (3d): the transparency page and staff.js recipients count the accounts used each month and,
# while this is on, the readers without an account each day, by a keyed digest of the network and the browser's name
# under a random key that lives 26 hours and is written nowhere else. on is the default; off leaves readers without an
# account out, and the pages then say "at least" (README, The yearly edition).
API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT=on
# The watcher and the push server run under the Compose profile notify, switched on here once the mailbox and the phones
# exist: COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify. Nothing below is needed for the stack to start while it is off. The mailbox: IMAP over
# TLS on port 993, an application password that can only read, and the name of the junk folder as the mail host names it.
# The publisher's ntfy token is also in infra/ntfy/server.yml; production refuses the example's.
# COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify
# NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_USER=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD=
# NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK=Junk
# NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN=
# The push network's fixed subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse; Caddy is on that network with
# the profile off too. The default lies outside the pools Docker gives its own networks (172.17.0.0/16 to 172.31.0.0/16,
# and 192.168.0.0/16): set another only if this host's own network uses it.
# PUSH_SUBNET=172.16.91.0/24
# The watcher's fixed address on that network, which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
# (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): with another subnet, set an address inside it here and in that file's line.
# NOTIFY_PUSH_IP=172.16.91.254

# The app's site (3f): open, or closed while a restored database is checked, when it answers 503 to every path, the
# API's included; the console's site stays open. Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
# The API reads it too (3d), when it starts: it refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
APP_SITE=open

# Public Turnstile site key baked into the web image. Cloudflare's always-pass test key for development;
# production uses the site key of the same widget as API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY.
WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA
# The address people write to when the report form does not work for them, to ask for their data, or about a decision.
# It is baked into the web image as EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: the report form names it when the human check fails or
# the limits are reached, and the terms page shows it. The image refuses to build without an address, and a
# production build refuses a placeholder (a domain ending in .local, .localhost, .test, .invalid or .example, or
# example.com, example.org or example.net). A person reads this mailbox every working day.
WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL=contact@korbat.local
# 3f: the contact point for authorities and the Member State korbat is established in, baked into the web image as
# EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT and EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE for the terms' sections on them: the page cannot read the API's
# API_CONTACT_POINT and API_HOME_STATE, which hold the same two values. The terms print the contact point only while it
# is set, and the image refuses a point without its state. Set both, with the API's, as the last step of the README's
# Before going public, then rebuild the caddy service.
WEB_CONTACT_POINT=
WEB_HOME_STATE=DE

# development or production. It is the API's NODE_ENV (production refuses Turnstile test keys, plain-http
# origins and a relay without TLS) and a build argument of the web image (production refuses the
# Turnstile test site key). Set it to production before building the images for the public.
KORBAT_ENV=development
# on when cloudflared is the only way in: Caddy then keeps CF-Connecting-IP for the API (and
# API_TRUST_PROXY is cloudflare). off drops the header, so nobody on the network can claim an address.
TUNNEL=off
# Cloudflare Tunnel token (Zero Trust > Networks > Tunnels). Only needed with --profile tunnel. The
# tunnel has three public hostnames: the app's, pointing at http://caddy:8080, the staff console's (the hostname of
# API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN), pointing at http://caddy:8090, and the phones' push hostname (3f), pointing at
# http://caddy:8091. Leave the HTTP Host Header setting of each empty, so the API sees the hostname the browser used.
TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# The development stack's host ports, read only by infra/compose.dev.yml. Set one when another container
# on this machine holds the default, and give apps/api/.env the same port. Defaults: 55432, 56379, 3000,
# 8080, 8090, 51025, 58025, 8091, 2586.
# DEV_PG_PORT=55432
# DEV_REDIS_PORT=56379
# DEV_API_PORT=3000
# DEV_CADDY_PORT=8080
# The staff console's port: API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN must name the same port on localhost (http://localhost:<port>).
# DEV_CONSOLE_PORT=8090
# DEV_SMTP_PORT=51025
# DEV_MAILPIT_PORT=58025
# 3f, with the profile notify: the push site, which a test client subscribes through, and ntfy's own port, which only
# `pnpm --filter @korbat/api notify:dev` publishes to (NOTIFY_PUSH_URL in apps/api/.env).
# DEV_PUSH_PORT=8091
# DEV_NTFY_PORT=2586
```

### Replace `infra/compose.yml` (whole file)

```yaml
name: korbat

x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options: { max-size: "20m", max-file: "5" }

x-node-common: &node-common
  restart: unless-stopped
  read_only: true
  tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging: *logging

services:
  postgres:
    # PostgreSQL 18. From 18 on the image keeps the cluster under /var/lib/postgresql/<major>/docker, so
    # the volume is mounted one level up and a later major can pg_upgrade inside it. A cluster from the
    # earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) is moved over by scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs.
    image: postgres:18.6-alpine@sha256:77f585114c32fbca283dc835b0596f4e52b51b4c6662d7810b2f4084f60a1873
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 1g
    memswap_limit: 1g
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
      KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}
      KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}
      # The contact point's watcher's role (3f), which 01-roles.sh makes on a new data directory. Not required: a stack
      # without the watcher runs without it.
      KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD: ${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}
    volumes:
      - pgdata18:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro
    # watch: the watcher's own network to the database, which holds nothing else.
    networks: [data, watch]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  redis:
    # Valkey, the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, under the service name the URLs already use. A password
    # is required: nothing on the data network may read the session cache without it.
    image: valkey/valkey:9.1.2-alpine@sha256:48332870af354a799964c0012ae1194a0bf2bf894eb508f945810596dc2d8d11
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 384m
    memswap_limit: 384m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      REDIS_PASSWORD: ${REDIS_PASSWORD:?set REDIS_PASSWORD in infra/.env}
    command: ["sh", "-c", "exec valkey-server --appendonly yes --maxmemory 256mb --maxmemory-policy noeviction --requirepass $$REDIS_PASSWORD"]
    volumes:
    # A fresh volume: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into `redisdata`, and that
    # volume held only transient state (limits, codes in flight, cached sessions, queued image jobs).
      - valkeydata:/data
    networks: [data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "VALKEYCLI_AUTH=$$REDIS_PASSWORD valkey-cli ping | grep -q PONG"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  migrate:
    <<: *node-common
    restart: "no"
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
    command: ["node", "dist/migrate.js"]
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE: postgres://korbat_migrate:${KORBAT_MIGRATE_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      MIGRATIONS_DIR: /app/migrations
      # `staff.js enroll` runs here, as the migrator, the one role the running API never holds, and records on each link
      # the console's origin and relying party ID it is issued for. Empty, the console is off and enroll refuses.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # 3f: staff.js order-open runs here too, and reads the home state (whether an order is cross-border) and the app's
      # origin (how a link is read, as the console's route reads it). Neither is required: enroll and the migrations run
      # without them, and order-open refuses with one sentence while either is empty.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:-}
    networks: [data]
    depends_on:
      postgres: { condition: service_healthy }

  api:
    <<: *node-common
    # The image's name, the one Compose gives it by default, written out: notify (3f) runs the same image, so it is
    # built once.
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/api/Dockerfile
      args:
        KORBAT_VERSION: ${KORBAT_VERSION:-0.0.0}
    mem_limit: 512m
    memswap_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 256
    environment:
      # development or production, from infra/.env; production turns on the guards against test keys, plain-http
      # origins and a relay without TLS. The worker below always runs as production.
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
      PORT: "3000"
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_API: postgres://korbat_api:${KORBAT_API_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      DATABASE_URL_AUTH: postgres://korbat_auth:${KORBAT_AUTH_DB_PASSWORD}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
      REDIS_URL: redis://:${REDIS_PASSWORD}@redis:6379
      TRUSTED_ORIGINS: ${API_TRUSTED_ORIGINS:-}
      # Which header names the client: the stack refuses to start without a choice.
      TRUST_PROXY: ${API_TRUST_PROXY:?set API_TRUST_PROXY in infra/.env}
      # Auth settings. The stack refuses to start while any of these is missing from infra/.env.
      APP_ORIGIN: ${API_APP_ORIGIN:?set API_APP_ORIGIN in infra/.env}
      AUTH_HMAC_KEY: ${API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY:?set API_AUTH_HMAC_KEY in infra/.env}
      IP_HASH_KEY: ${API_IP_HASH_KEY:?set API_IP_HASH_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEY: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEY:?set API_TOTP_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      # Encrypts a signed-out notifier's name and address; earlier keys stay accepted for decryption.
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY:?set API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY in infra/.env}
      NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS: ${API_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS:-}
      TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY:?set API_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY in infra/.env}
      SMTP_URL: ${API_SMTP_URL:?set API_SMTP_URL in infra/.env}
      MAIL_FROM: ${API_MAIL_FROM:?set API_MAIL_FROM in infra/.env}
      TERMS_VERSION: ${API_TERMS_VERSION:?set API_TERMS_VERSION in infra/.env}
      # The verified badge's phone check. off (the default) hides the badge; vonage needs the two credentials.
      VERIFY_PROVIDER: ${API_VERIFY_PROVIDER:-off}
      VONAGE_API_KEY: ${API_VONAGE_API_KEY:-}
      VONAGE_API_SECRET: ${API_VONAGE_API_SECRET:-}
      VERIFY_BRAND: ${API_VERIFY_BRAND:-korbat}
      # Passkeys. Empty values leave the API's defaults: the host of APP_ORIGIN as the RP ID and korbat as the name.
      WEBAUTHN_RP_ID: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID:-}
      WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME: ${API_WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME:-}
      # The staff console, served by Caddy's second site: the origin staff open it at, and the RP ID staff keys are bound
      # to (empty means the console's hostname). An empty origin switches the console off: every /api/staff path then
      # answers 404. The migrate service gets the same two values for `staff.js enroll`.
      CONSOLE_ORIGIN: ${API_CONSOLE_ORIGIN:-}
      CONSOLE_RP_ID: ${API_CONSOLE_RP_ID:-}
      # Moderation: the UTC hour of the daily release of decisions to those who reported, the queue's emergency switch, and
      # the retention job's switch, which is off only for a restore window (README, Restoring, step 5).
      MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR: ${API_MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR:-7}
      MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN: ${API_MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN:-off}
      MODERATION_RETENTION: ${API_MODERATION_RETENTION:-on}
      # Authorities' orders (3f): whether the alert tick judges the alert channel's health. Empty means on in production;
      # off until the contact point's mailbox exists (README, Upgrading).
      NOTIFY: ${API_NOTIFY:-}
      # The operator's Member State, a state whose facts the contracts hold (DE is filled in), and the published contact
      # point for authorities. Both empty until the owner's list is done; the home state is required once the contact
      # point is set.
      HOME_STATE: ${API_HOME_STATE:-}
      CONTACT_POINT: ${API_CONTACT_POINT:-}
      # 3f Task 5: whether a deletion keeps an account's address, at most seven days, while a report of its sealed images
      # to the authorities is owed. Empty means on; off restores the purge that overwrites the address at once.
      REPORT_HOLD: ${API_REPORT_HOLD:-}
      # 3d: the app's site switch, Caddy's (3f), handed to the API too, which refuses a test adapter while the site is open.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
      # 3d Task 3: the purge of an image's copies at the edge once it stops being public: off (empty, the default), test
      # (refused while APP_SITE is open) or cloudflare, which needs the zone's id, the API token with the one permission
      # Zone, Cache Purge, and the public hostname images are served under (README, The edge).
      EDGE_PURGE: ${API_EDGE_PURGE:-}
      EDGE_ZONE_ID: ${API_EDGE_ZONE_ID:-}
      EDGE_API_TOKEN: ${API_EDGE_API_TOKEN:-}
      EDGE_HOST: ${API_EDGE_HOST:-}
      # 3d Task 4: whether readers without an account are counted among the recipients, each day's by a keyed digest of
      # the network and the browser's name under a salt that lives 26 hours; on unless set to off (README, The yearly edition).
      RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: ${API_RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT:-}
      # Images. The API writes uploads and only reads what the worker stored.
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
      MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES: ${MEDIA_MIN_FREE_BYTES:-2147483648}
      MEDIA_RECONCILE: ${MEDIA_RECONCILE:-on}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
    networks: [app, data]
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  # The image worker runs the decoder, the most exploitable code in the stack. It has no network at
  # all, no credentials and no capabilities: it reads uploads and writes the store, and that is
  # everything it can reach. The memory limit was sized on worst-case images (2b design, Research).
  worker:
    <<: *node-common
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: apps/worker/Dockerfile
    network_mode: none
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 768m
    memswap_limit: 768m
    cpus: 1.0
    pids_limit: 64
    tmpfs: ["/tmp:size=64m"]
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      MEDIA_UPLOADS_DIR: /media/uploads
      MEDIA_STORE_DIR: /media/store
      MEDIA_FORMATS: ${MEDIA_FORMATS:-jpeg,png,webp,gif,avif}
    volumes:
      - media-uploads:/media/uploads:ro
      - media-store:/media/store
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/media/store/heartbeat', 'utf8')).at < 60000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4

  # The contact point's watcher (3f design, section 5): the API's image with dist/notify.js, under the profile notify. It
  # reads the contact-point mailbox over IMAP and publishes the alerts to ntfy. On the network watch it reaches PostgreSQL
  # as korbat_notify, whose grants are four tables, and nothing else; on push it reaches ntfy. It never joins data, where
  # the API listens and the limit store is. It exits rather than hang, and Docker starts it again. No setting of it is
  # required by Compose: the program names the one it is missing and exits.
  notify:
    <<: *node-common
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["node", "dist/notify.js"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    # Measured in this image (3f Task 1): about 82 MB resident idle, a peak of 93 MB during a first read of 10,000 old
    # messages, which took 21 seconds and fell back to 81 MB; under this limit the container's peak was 85 MB, with no
    # kill. 128 MB keeps more than a third above that peak.
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:-production}
      LOG_LEVEL: ${API_LOG_LEVEL:-info}
      DATABASE_URL_NOTIFY: postgres://korbat_notify:${KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD:-}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_HOST:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_USER: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_USER:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_PASSWORD:-}
      NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK: ${NOTIFY_IMAP_JUNK:-}
      NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN:-}
    # A fixed address on push (3f's review, operations3), which infra/ntfy/server.yml exempts from ntfy's request limit
    # (visitor-request-limit-exempt-hosts): ntfy lets any one address publish 60 times and then once every 5 seconds (lab
    # L1), which would hold an order's alert behind a flood of contact mail. It lies inside PUSH_SUBNET, at the top of
    # the range, which Docker hands out last; change it, and the file's line, with the subnet.
    networks:
      watch: {}
      push:
        ipv4_address: ${NOTIFY_PUSH_IP:-172.16.91.254}
    depends_on:
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      ntfy: { condition: service_started }
    # The watcher writes the time of every round it ends; two minutes without one is a hang.
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "node", "-e", "process.exit(Date.now() - Number(require('fs').readFileSync('/tmp/korbat-notify-beat', 'utf8')) < 120000 ? 0 : 1)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # The hand-over of one seal's files (3f design, sections 5 and 7.14), under the profile handover, started by the operator
  # alone: docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests. The API's
  # image with dist/handover.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no credential, no capability,
  # the image store and (3d) the quarantine read-only, the quarantine looked in first. It has no bind mount here: the
  # directory for the archive is an argument of the command (an empty source would stop every Compose command of the
  # stack), on an encrypted volume owned by uid 1000, the image's user node, the only place it can write. No setting of
  # it is required.
  handover:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["handover"]
    command: ["node", "dist/handover.js"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store:ro
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine:ro

  # The quarantine's mover (3d design, sections 5 and 7.1), under the profile quarantine, started by the operator alone:
  # docker compose -f infra/compose.yml --profile quarantine run --rm -T quarantine < list > receipt, with the list that
  # staff.js quarantine-list printed, and the receipt then recorded by staff.js quarantine-record (the README,
  # Quarantine). The API's image with dist/quarantine.js, which opens no database and no socket: no network at all, no
  # environment, no credential, no capability and a read-only root; the image store and the quarantine read-write, and
  # nothing else. Its two roots are arguments of its entry point, and it refuses to start without both; what follows the
  # service's name on the command line (--lost, --inventory) is appended to them. It is the one service that writes the
  # quarantine; handover reads it, and the api, migrate and worker services never mount it.
  quarantine:
    image: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}-api
    profiles: ["quarantine"]
    entrypoint: ["node", "dist/quarantine.js", "/media/store", "/media/quarantine"]
    restart: "no"
    network_mode: none
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    stdin_open: true
    volumes:
      - media-store:/media/store
      - media-quarantine:/media/quarantine

  # The push server (3f design, section 5), under the profile notify, never linked into korbat's programs: ntfy at its
  # pinned release, reading its users, rights and tokens from infra/ntfy/server.yml (git-ignored, made from
  # server.yml.example), mounted read-only, since Compose would blank the $2a$10$ of a password hash in a variable. Only
  # on push, which is internal: it has no route out, so nothing is forwarded upstream. Its cache and auth files are on its
  # volume, at /var/tmp, the one directory of the image its user may write to.
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.28.0@sha256:6ef4b819f722fccdc036af611c4774cfdc2de821ab74fdd48bbf4c9d6f8973da
    profiles: ["notify"]
    command: ["serve", "--config", "/etc/ntfy/server.yml"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy-data:/var/tmp
    networks: [push]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:2586/v1/health"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 4

  # Caddy serves the web app on port 8080, proxying /api, the staff console on port 8090, proxying only /api/staff, and
  # (3f) the phones' push site on port 8091, proxying only the two topics' subscriptions to ntfy. It runs as its own
  # user, sees only the API and ntfy, and is the only thing cloudflared can reach. A client from the push network (ntfy,
  # the watcher) is refused 403 on the app's and the console's sites.
  caddy:
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ["/tmp"]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    mem_limit: 128m
    memswap_limit: 128m
    pids_limit: 64
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: infra/caddy/Dockerfile
      args:
        EXPO_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY: ${WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY:?set WEB_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY in infra/.env}
        KORBAT_ENV: ${KORBAT_ENV:?set KORBAT_ENV to development or production in infra/.env}
        TUNNEL: ${TUNNEL:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE: ${WEB_BADGE:-off}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL: ${WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL:?set WEB_CONTACT_EMAIL in infra/.env}
        # 3f: the terms' contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State; neither is required (Before going public).
        EXPO_PUBLIC_CONTACT_POINT: ${WEB_CONTACT_POINT:-}
        EXPO_PUBLIC_HOME_STATE: ${WEB_HOME_STATE:-}
    depends_on:
      api: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      # The push network's subnet, which the app's and the console's sites refuse (3f).
      PUSH_SUBNET: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}
      # The app's site, open (the default) or closed: closed answers 503 to every path while a restore is checked (3f,
      # section 7.17). Caddy reads it when it starts and refuses to start on any other value.
      APP_SITE: ${APP_SITE:-open}
    volumes:
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    networks: [edge, app, push]

  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.9.1@sha256:b269e8abd07a5bf6f3f4be65d5050b2174eca89c56a0241a8ff32a16aec454e4
    restart: unless-stopped
    read_only: true
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    logging: *logging
    profiles: ["tunnel"]
    command: ["tunnel", "--no-autoupdate", "run"]
    environment:
      TUNNEL_TOKEN: ${TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks: [edge]
    depends_on:
      - caddy

# cloudflared reaches only Caddy, Caddy reaches only the API and ntfy, and the API alone reaches the data services, but
# for the watcher's own network to PostgreSQL (3f).
networks:
  edge:
  app:
  data:
  # The watcher and PostgreSQL, nothing else. Not internal: the mail host's port 993 is reached through its gateway.
  watch:
  # ntfy, the watcher and Caddy. Internal: no route out. Its fixed subnet is what the app's and the console's sites refuse.
  push:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: ${PUSH_SUBNET:-172.16.91.0/24}

volumes:
  # PostgreSQL 18. The earlier pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 16) stays until scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs has
  # moved it and you remove it by hand.
  pgdata18:
  valkeydata:
  # Uploads wait here for the worker and are deleted once processed. Nothing in it needs a backup.
  media-uploads:
  # The images korbat serves. Back it up together with the database.
  media-store:
  # 3d: the files of images sealed for good, moved out of the store by the quarantine service, on the host's encrypted
  # disk. It is in no backup, by decision: a restore never brings a destroyed file back. Owned by uid 1000, mode 0700, the
  # path the API's image makes (the README, Quarantine and Backups).
  media-quarantine:
  # Caddy's state, owned by its own user; the earlier root-owned caddydata and caddyconfig volumes can go.
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
  # ntfy's message cache and its auth database (3f). The cache is how a phone gets an alert published while its
  # connection was down; the auth database is rebuilt from infra/ntfy/server.yml at every start.
  ntfy-data:
```

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

/** Every non-2xx response from the API has this shape. */
export const ErrorEnvelope = z.object({
  error: z.object({
    code: z.string().min(1),
    message: z.string().min(1),
    requestId: z.string().optional(),
    details: z.unknown().optional(),
  }),
});
export type ErrorEnvelope = z.infer<typeof ErrorEnvelope>;

export const CheckState = z.enum(["ok", "fail"]);

export const HealthResponse = z.object({
  status: z.enum(["ok", "degraded"]),
  version: z.string(),
  checks: z.record(z.string(), CheckState),
});
export type HealthResponse = z.infer<typeof HealthResponse>;

/** Keyset pagination query params shared by every list endpoint. */
export const Pagination = z.object({
  cursor: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional(),
  limit: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),
});
export type Pagination = z.infer<typeof Pagination>;

export * from "./account";
export * from "./auth";
export * from "./explore";
export * from "./media";
// Evaluated before ./staff, and importing nothing from it: staff.ts can read this module's constants while it loads.
export * from "./moderation";
// 3f: imports nothing from the other modules, so moderation.ts can read its constants while it loads.
export * from "./orders";
export * from "./passkeys";
export * from "./social";
export * from "./staff";
export * from "./text";
// 3d Task 4: the public figures. It reads moderation.ts and orders.ts for closed lists, and nothing reads it.
export * from "./transparency";
```

```ts
import { ORDER_NOTICE } from "./statement";
/**
 * The public rulebook. korbat restricts content when it breaks one of these rules, or when it is illegal under EU law or
 * the law of an EU country and korbat is told about it in a notice. Opinions are never a reason. Every decision cites one
 * of these rules or the law.
 *
 * The rulebook is versioned: a decision records the version it was made under, and its statement is always rendered with
 * that version's text, so an old statement reads exactly as it was sent whatever the rules say now.
 */
export type Automation =
  | "none"                 // report-driven, human decides
  | "withhold_for_review"  // automation may hide from others pending a human
  | "auto_remove";         // automation may remove (R2 only)

export interface Rule {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  text: string;
  allowed: string[];
  notAllowed: string[];
  automation: Automation;
  /** Decided by an admin: every final decision under the rule, whether it acts or not. */
  seniorQueue: boolean;
}

/** Version 1: the six rules as they stood before moderation cases. Kept as it was, for the decisions made under it. */
const RULES_V1 = [
  {
    id: "R1",
    title: "No sexual or pornographic content",
    text: "Images or text whose primary purpose is sexual arousal are not allowed. This includes nudity presented sexually, explicit sexual acts, and sexualised depictions of anyone. Images that score high on the automated check are hidden from others until a person reviews them; the author can always see their own post.",
    allowed: ["Medical or educational discussion of sexuality without explicit imagery", "Art with non-sexual nudity in a clearly artistic or historical context", "Frank discussion of sexual politics or policy"],
    notAllowed: ["Pornographic images or video", "Sexually explicit text posted for arousal", "Links whose preview is pornographic"],
    automation: "withhold_for_review",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },

    allowed: ["Reporting or discussing child safety issues without imagery", "News about arrests or legislation"],
    notAllowed: ["Any sexualised image of a minor, real or generated", "Links to such material", "Solicitation"],
    automation: "auto_remove",

Criticising ideas, beliefs, policies, institutions, public figures, or the actions of groups is allowed, even harshly. The line is attacking people for what they are, not disagreeing with what they think or do.",
    allowed: ["Criticism of any religion's doctrine or any government's policy", "Arguing that a political movement is wrong or harmful", "Blunt, offensive, or unpopular opinions about ideas"],
    notAllowed: ["Slurs directed at a person or group", "Calling for a protected group to be harmed or excluded", "Sustained pile-ons against one person because of a protected trait"],
    automation: "none",

  },
  {

    title: "No doxxing",

When a report is credible the post is hidden from others while a person decides, because the harm is immediate.",
    allowed: ["Public business contact details", "Information a public figure has published about themselves", "Linking to public court records in a news context"],
    notAllowed: ["Posting someone's home address or phone number", "Sharing private messages or images without consent", "Coordinating to find where someone lives"],
    automation: "none",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },
  {

    title: "No direct threats of violence",
    text: "Stating an intent to physically harm a specific person or group, or calling for others to do so, is not allowed. Hyperbole, dark humour, and discussion of violence in news, history, or fiction are allowed. Cases go to the senior queue.",
    allowed: ["Discussing wars, crimes, or historical violence", "Obvious hyperbole ('I could kill for a coffee')", "Fiction and satire"],
    notAllowed: ["'I will hurt you' directed at a person", "Calling for a named person to be attacked", "Posting a target list"],
    automation: "none",

    allowed: ["Promoting your own work in your own posts", "Clearly labelled parody accounts", "Sharing a link once in a relevant thread"],
    notAllowed: ["Posting the same link across many threads", "Phishing or crypto giveaway scams", "An account presenting itself as a real person or brand it is not"],
    automation: "none",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },
] as const satisfies readonly Rule[];

/**
 * Version 2, with moderation cases: nothing is automated (a person decides every case; the automated checks of R1 and R2
 * return with a later version), R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them, R4 and R5 say who
 * hides content while a case is decided and who decides it, and R6 names coordinated manipulation. R3 is unchanged.
 */
const RULES_V2 = [
  {
    ...RULES_V1[0],
    text: "Images or text whose primary purpose is sexual arousal are not allowed. This includes nudity presented sexually, explicit sexual acts, and sexualised depictions of anyone.",
    automation: "none",
  },
  {
    ...RULES_V1[1],
    text: "Any sexualised depiction of a minor is not allowed. Nobody at korbat opens images that are reported or found as such material while the report is unanswered or the images are sealed. After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image. Whoever is on duty may seal them while an admin decides: sealed images are shown to nobody, their author included. An admin either seals them for good, in which case they are kept only for the authorities and reported to them, or answers without a seal. /** The version a decision made now records. */
export const RULES_VERSION = 3;

/** Every version of the rulebook, by its number. */
export const RULEBOOKS = { 1: RULES_V1, 2: RULES_V2, 3: RULES_V3 } as const satisfies Record<number, readonly Rule[]>;

/** The rules in force. */
export const RULES = RULEBOOKS[RULES_VERSION];

/** One version of the rulebook as the rules page's change log prints it: the day it came into force and what it changed. */
export interface RulesChange {
  version: number;
  /** The day the version came into force, as the pages print a day. */
  date: string;
  summary: string;
}

/**
 * The rulebook's change log (3d design, sections 2 row 7, 9.2 and 10.8; W.1), oldest first: one dated sentence a version.
 * The day is a literal written by the task that ships the version; versions 1 to 3 carry the day of the commit that added
 * each to this file. The rules page prints it newest first.
 */
export const RULES_CHANGES: readonly RulesChange[] = [
  { version: 1, date: "2026-09-14", summary: "The six rules as first published." },
  {
    version: 2,
    date: "2026-10-04",
    summary:
      "A person decides every case; the automated checks that R1 and R2 named are withdrawn until they exist. R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them. R4 and R5 say who may hide content while a case is decided and who decides it. R6 names coordinated manipulation.",
  },
  { version: 3, date: "2026-10-12", summary: "R6 names repeated, plainly unfounded reporting." },
];

export type RuleId = (typeof RULES)[number]["id"];

/** A rule as one version of the rulebook words it: the current version unless told. Undefined for an id or a version that does not exist. */
export function getRule(id: string, version: number = RULES_VERSION): Rule | undefined {
  const book: readonly Rule[] | undefined = (RULEBOOKS as Record<number, readonly Rule[]>)[version];
  return book?.find((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

export function isRuleId(id: string): id is RuleId {
  return RULES.some((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

/** What a statement of reasons tells its author they can do about the decision. Which text applies follows from the decision's own kind and outcome. */
export interface RedressTexts {
  /** A final decision that restricts: korbat's appeal. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal, which the statement fills in. */
  appeal: string;
  /** A decision taken while korbat decides. */
  interim: string;
  /** Any other decision, which its author cannot appeal. */
  notAppealable: string;
  // Version 2 (3e design, section 18, W.3). Their numbers are literals of the version, held to STANDING_RULES by a table
  // test: a changed number is a new version, so an old statement keeps its own.
  /** After a strike's sentence: the prior warning of what strikes lead to. */
  strikeNext?: string;
  /** An announced suspension or termination: the reply before the start. */
  reply?: string;
  /** A suspension or termination taken at once: the reply while it runs. */
  replyAtOnce?: string;
  /** A kept answer to a reply. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal of the decision it keeps. */
  replyAnswered?: string;
  /** After a warning about reporting: what may follow it. */
  warnNext?: string;
  /** An announced measure: the appeal does not wait for the start. */
  appealNow?: string;
  /** Version 3 (3f design, W.2 and W.3): the notice of an authority's order, ORDER_NOTICE. */
  order?: typeof ORDER_NOTICE;
}

/** The version of the redress texts a decision made now records. */
export const REDRESS_VERSION = 3;

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

const REDRESS_V1 = {
  appeal: `You can appeal this decision once, free of charge, within six months of being told, until {deadline}: choose "Appeal" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator who took no part in the case reviews it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  interim: `This applies while korbat decides, and ends with its decision. If korbat's decision restricts your post or profile, you can appeal it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  notAppealable: `korbat's appeal does not apply to this decision. Where an earlier decision about this content still stands in part, its own screen in korbat says whether you can still appeal it. You can go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
} as const;

/** Account sanctions (3e): six more texts beside version 1's three, which version 2 holds word for word. */
const REDRESS_V2 = {
  strikeNext:
    "A strike restricts nothing by itself. When an account has 3 active strikes, a moderator may decide to suspend it for a limited time or, after three suspensions in 365 days, an admin may decide to terminate it. You would be told first and could reply before anything is restricted.",
  reply: `Before it starts you can reply: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and say anything you want the moderator to weigh. A reply sent before the start holds the start until a moderator has read it and answered you; if the decision is kept, it then starts with the answer, and never before the time you were given. A reply sent later is read and answered too, and can end this measure, but does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAtOnce: `You can reply at any time while it runs: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator reads your reply and answers you, and can end this measure at once; the reply does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAnswered: `This answer is not appealed by itself. The appeal is against the decision it keeps: once, free of charge, until {deadline}, with "Appeal" on that decision's screen under Settings, Cases. The six months for it count from this answer when you replied before the start, and otherwise from the day you were told of that decision. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  warnNext: "If 3 of the reports you send after this warning are marked that way while it counts, a moderator may restrict your reports under korbat's rules for up to 30 days.",
  appealNow: "You can appeal from now; you do not have to wait for the start. An appeal does not hold the start: only a reply sent before the start does.",
} as const;

/** Every version of the redress texts, by its number, kept as the rulebooks are. */
export const REDRESS_TEXTS = {
  1: REDRESS_V1,
  2: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2 },
  /**
   * 3f (design, section 10.7; W.3): version 2's nine texts word for word, and the group `order`, the notice of an
   * authority's order (ORDER_NOTICE of the statement's module), so a notice reads under its own version.
   */
  3: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2, order: ORDER_NOTICE },
} as const satisfies Record<number, RedressTexts>;

/** The redress texts of one version. Undefined for a version that does not exist. */
export function getRedress(version: number): RedressTexts | undefined {
  return (REDRESS_TEXTS as Record<number, RedressTexts>)[version];
}

// The statement of reasons, rendered over the rulebooks and the redress texts above. The package exports only this file,
// so the app, the console and the API reach the statement through it.

  IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE,

  STATEMENT_WORDS,

  retireEnd,
```
